chapters.title: Aquatic Mammals: Whales, Walruses and Dugongs

paragraphs.text: In ancient times any aquatic creature was called matsya or fish. The word makara means crocodile, but according to some, a makara is háuṋgar or kámat́a. If it belongs to the sea, it is called háuṋgar [big shark]; if it belongs to saline river water, it is called kámat́a [small shark]. But the háuṋgar or kámat́a is of course a fish – a fish with rows of sharp teeth that, because of its characteristics, is sometimes described as a water vulture. However, there cannot be any justification for calling the crocodile a fish. It belongs to the land, eats on the land, and sleeps on the land. It lives in cavities near any pond. No pond with its nearby cavities and land can be found in the ocean. That is why there is no crocodile in the ocean. Where would it find shelter? Where would it eat? Where would it sleep? Even then, since ancient times common people have called the crocodile makaramatsya [crocodile fish], from which in current Hindustani has come the word magaramaccha. In a village in Khulna, I have heard people calling shrimps ciḿŕi mách and crabs kákŕá mách [mách means “fish”], although there is no head or tail relation between the fish and the crab.
summary: In ancient times any aquatic creature was called matsya or fish.
It lives in cavities near any pond.
In a village in Khulna, I have heard people calling shrimps ciḿŕi mách and crabs kákŕá mách [mách means “fish”], although there is no head or tail relation between the fish and the crab.

paragraphs.text: Similar is the case of dolphins (shishumár, porpoises), whales, seals and walruses; they do not belong to the fish category. They are not born from eggs; they are mammals. Yet many people wrongly term the whale and the seal as fish. This is certainly incorrect. In ancient times, dolphins were land mammals. Losing the battle of survival, they were compelled to take shelter in the water. Hence their lungs function like those of land animals. They develop respiratory problems if they remain too long under water. So at intervals, they swiftly float up to the water surface, breathe deeply, and then again dive to the depth.
summary: Similar is the case of dolphins (shishumár, porpoises), whales, seals and walruses; they do not belong to the fish category.
In ancient times, dolphins were land mammals.
So at intervals, they swiftly float up to the water surface, breathe deeply, and then again dive to the depth.

paragraphs.text: Although whales are large in size, they were also originally land creatures. Due to fear of other gigantic, carnivorous land animals, the whales were likewise compelled to retreat into the water. Even today their way of breathing is different from that of other sea creatures. Their ways of eating are also different. They combine their eating and breathing. With mouths wide open, they dive deep into the water and swallow not only small but also many large creatures. At that time, both air and water enter their gullet. After some time, through a slit in their head, they spray the water up and outwards like a fountain. One can locate whales from their water spraying. In this manner, whale hunters come to know the location of whales.
summary: Although whales are large in size, they were also originally land creatures.
With mouths wide open, they dive deep into the water and swallow not only small but also many large creatures.
In this manner, whale hunters come to know the location of whales.

paragraphs.text: In English, “whale” is not considered to indicate the fish category. It is needless to say that what in Sanskrit is called the timiuṋgal – the blue whale – is not a fish either. ( 1 )
summary: In English, “whale” is not considered to indicate the fish category.
It is needless to say that what in Sanskrit is called the timiuṋgal – the blue whale – is not a fish either.

paragraphs.text: Dugong: Stories circulate in certain parts of the world about sea creatures called mermaids. The lower part of their (dugongsʼ) body below the navel is like that of a fish; on its upper part there are wings and fins for moving ahead and steering through the water. Its facial appearance is similar to the walrus. It is a kind of mammal, hence this creature has teats above the navel. Generally it keeps the lower part of its body under water and will bring the upper part above the surface of the water for a short while. It then immediately dives back into the water. Since it has teats above the navel, people at a distance used to wrongly perceive it as a woman. In fact, these creatures are like whales and walruses – a type of mammal living in the water.
summary: Dugong: Stories circulate in certain parts of the world about sea creatures called mermaids.
Generally it keeps the lower part of its body under water and will bring the upper part above the surface of the water for a short while.
In fact, these creatures are like whales and walruses – a type of mammal living in the water.

paragraphs.text: It is said that these creatures have excessive emotions or sentiments. The word kaeshik is applied to them; it means inordinate articulation of anger, shyness, hatred, affection, love, attachment or disaffection. In their welling up of emotions, people cry out in joy, which they cannot restrain with the help of their nervous system. Though unwilling to express hatred, they often fail to suppress it. Thoughts stirred by feelings of love, affection, compassion and attachment are suddenly articulated when people become unable to confine those feelings to the subterranean currents of their hearts. Probably later they think that they should not have said such things. They realize that it was not proper for them to have expressed themselves. This expression of emotion varies from creature to creature, from human to human, and even varies in the mode and trend of expression. The general name for this form of expression is kaeshik. Under the influence of kaeshik, human beings often commit suicide. Being goaded by kaeshik [the urge for emotional expression], they climb high mountains, sail through space and kiss the soil of the poles.
summary: It is said that these creatures have excessive emotions or sentiments.
Probably later they think that they should not have said such things.
Being goaded by kaeshik [the urge for emotional expression], they climb high mountains, sail through space and kiss the soil of the poles.

paragraphs.text: A long time ago, in eastern Indonesia, a man killed an innocent dugong. The dugong does not have the strength or intelligence to fight against human beings. After some days it was found that about fifty to sixty dugongs had helplessly flung themselves onto the seashore. Since they are marine creatures, when they sprang out of the water and dashed themselves onto the land, they all died immediately. The local people then understood that for their murder of one innocent dugong, fifty to sixty dugongs, in an emotional, silent protest, had made a sacrifice of themselves. ( 2 )
summary: A long time ago, in eastern Indonesia, a man killed an innocent dugong.
After some days it was found that about fifty to sixty dugongs had helplessly flung themselves onto the seashore.
The local people then understood that for their murder of one innocent dugong, fifty to sixty dugongs, in an emotional, silent protest, had made a sacrifice of themselves.

paragraphs.text: Porpoise and intermediate-stage animals: Úś + kan = úśaka. In the etymological sense, it means “something related to saline water”. In common usage, it means a salt-water porpoise [the same suborder as the dolphins]. Although uśaka means salt-water porpoise, in colloquial Sanskrit the word is used to mean any kind of porpoise – fresh-or salt-water. Another name for the porpoise is shishumár.
summary: Porpoise and intermediate-stage animals: Úś + kan = úśaka.
In common usage, it means a salt-water porpoise [the same suborder as the dolphins].
Another name for the porpoise is shishumár.

paragraphs.text: Zoologists say that life first evolved in water. Different water animals, driven by the urge for self-preservation, became land animals and birds. All water animals of those days were oviparous. Hence, all animals which later became land animals or birds were all oviparous in the primary stage. Those that became land animals were in their initial stage reptiles, for example, the dinosaur, coctatius [such as alligators and crocodiles], etc. The ancient dinosaurs and coctatius were all oviparous. Those of their direct descendants that still exist on earth in the form of different species – the crocodile, lizard, chameleon and snake – are all oviparous. Those that evolved from water animals into flying animals (i.e., birds) are all oviparous.
summary: Zoologists say that life first evolved in water.
Those that became land animals were in their initial stage reptiles, for example, the dinosaur, coctatius [such as alligators and crocodiles], etc.
, birds) are all oviparous.

paragraphs.text: When reptiles, in a transformed state after becoming land animals, gave up crawling on their chests and learned how to move on their hind legs or on four legs, they abandoned their oviparous character and became mammals. During the intermediate stage of their evolution into mammals, for a certain period they retained some of the characteristics of both oviparous animals and mammals. For example, some of them were oviparous, yet at the same time were mammals. Some were not oviparous and also were not mammals. On certain isolated islands today, such intermediate-stage animals still exist. The duckbill [platypus], living in certain South Pacific islands, belongs to this category. They belong to the cat family, are oviparous and yet are mammals. However, due to natural law, these animal species are not expected to survive on the earth much longer. Certain land animals glide through the air and fly with the help of webbing on their hands and body. They are simultaneously land animals and oviparous mammals. Although they can fly, they are not really birds. Examples are bats, titmice and flying squirrels.
summary: When reptiles, in a transformed state after becoming land animals, gave up crawling on their chests and learned how to move on their hind legs or on four legs, they abandoned their oviparous character and became mammals.
They belong to the cat family, are oviparous and yet are mammals.
Examples are bats, titmice and flying squirrels.

paragraphs.text: Even after leaving behind their reptilian characteristics upon becoming land animals and mammals, some of them again returned to the water for self-preservation. Although they are now aquatic animals, they still show many characteristics of land animals. Of these, some familiar names are the whale and the porpoise. They are aquatic animals, but they do not belong to the fish group. They are not oviparous, and their young ones suck milk from their motherʼs breast. Many mistake whales for fish. Whales are whales; they are not fish. The walrus and seal are not fish either. Although the prawn, octopus, lobster and tortoise are partly aquatic and partly terrestrial, they are not fish. They are oviparous.
summary: Even after leaving behind their reptilian characteristics upon becoming land animals and mammals, some of them again returned to the water for self-preservation.
They are not oviparous, and their young ones suck milk from their motherʼs breast.
Although the prawn, octopus, lobster and tortoise are partly aquatic and partly terrestrial, they are not fish.

paragraphs.text: The coelakanth, the ancestor of the fish group, is in no way similar to the prawn, octopus, tortoise and lobster. Yet they share one similarity; they are all oviparous. Octopuses are akin to spiders in many respects. Hence although the octopus is an aquatic animal, some say that one species, after becoming land animals, might have been transformed earlier into spiders. However, the ciḿŕi [prawn] has little similarity with the ucciḿŕe [cricket]. (Uŕ + ciḿre = ucciḿŕe, that is, “flying ciḿŕe”.)
summary: The coelakanth, the ancestor of the fish group, is in no way similar to the prawn, octopus, tortoise and lobster.
Hence although the octopus is an aquatic animal, some say that one species, after becoming land animals, might have been transformed earlier into spiders.
(Uŕ + ciḿre = ucciḿŕe, that is, “flying ciḿŕe”.

paragraphs.text: Let us return to the story of the porpoise. In the distant past the porpoises were land animals. Now they have turned aquatic. However, in order to inhale they have to quickly float to the surface of the water. They are quiet by nature, but they will bite in self-defence; otherwise not. It is not their habit to kill young animals. Hence the word shishumár [“child killers”] does not represent their real nature.
summary: Let us return to the story of the porpoise.
However, in order to inhale they have to quickly float to the surface of the water.
Hence the word shishumár [“child killers”] does not represent their real nature.

paragraphs.text: There are certain fish who, despite being aquatic animals, have been struggling for millions of years to become land animals. Hence they have developed certain changes in their physiology. They can survive on land for a fairly long period. This type of fish we call jiiyal [“that which can be kept alive in a vessel of water”]. Some examples of this are nyát́á, kai (in Maethilii kavai), shiuṋgii (shruṋgiká), mágur (madgur), etc. If they could survive for a few million more years, they would be transformed into land animals. ( 3 )
summary: There are certain fish who, despite being aquatic animals, have been struggling for millions of years to become land animals.
This type of fish we call jiiyal [“that which can be kept alive in a vessel of water”].
If they could survive for a few million more years, they would be transformed into land animals.

paragraphs.text: Birds and Animals, Our Neighbours [a compilation]
summary: Birds and Animals, Our Neighbours [a compilation]

footnotes.text: The foregoing four paragraphs are from Shabda Cayaniká Part 20, Discourse 155.
The foregoing three paragraphs are from Shabda Cayaniká Part 7, Discourse 48.
The foregoing seven paragraphs are from Varńa Vicitrá Part 3, Discourse 22.

paragraphs.text: The creatures of the coctatius ( 1 ) group such as crocodiles, mecho kumir [fish-eating alligator], alligators, salamanders, large-sized iguanas, iguanas, golden iguanas, house lizards (in Bengali t́ikt́iki, in other Indian languages – t́ikt́ikiá, bichaoti, chipkali, etc), have the power to mesmerize other creatures by their gaze. You might have seen on the wall a t́ikt́iki staring with a fixed gaze at a cockroach. The cockroach can fly, but the house lizard cannot fly. When the cockroach sees the house lizard, it becomes unnerved with fear. It then flies and comes just close to the mouth of the lizard, which then swallows it. Other creatures belonging to this category get hold of their prey in the same way.
summary: The creatures of the coctatius ( 1 ) group such as crocodiles, mecho kumir [fish-eating alligator], alligators, salamanders, large-sized iguanas, iguanas, golden iguanas, house lizards (in Bengali t́ikt́iki, in other Indian languages – t́ikt́ikiá, bichaoti, chipkali, etc), have the power to mesmerize other creatures by their gaze.
When the cockroach sees the house lizard, it becomes unnerved with fear.
Other creatures belonging to this category get hold of their prey in the same way.

paragraphs.text: The crocodile cannot run fast, although somehow it manages to do so; however the deer moves very fast. If the deer, while quenching its thirst by the river bank, catches the eye of a crocodile or vice-versa, sometimes it happens that the deer trembles, frozen in fear to the spot, and the crocodile slowly advances and grabs it. In this manner, the fish-eating alligators [mecho kumiir] are able to catch fish and other water animals that move with relatively greater speed. The crocodile and the alligator, although they submerge into the water for their prey, live in cavities near the riverbed. Due to the mesmerizing power of their eyes, they not only get hold of agile water and land animals and eat them, they are also able to catch and eat air-borne creatures.
summary: The crocodile cannot run fast, although somehow it manages to do so; however the deer moves very fast.
In this manner, the fish-eating alligators [mecho kumiir] are able to catch fish and other water animals that move with relatively greater speed.
Due to the mesmerizing power of their eyes, they not only get hold of agile water and land animals and eat them, they are also able to catch and eat air-borne creatures.

paragraphs.text: Lizards such as the salamander climb up trees and eat birds as well as their eggs. On several occasions, although the bird is quite capable of flying away it somehow is unable to do so. Perhaps it does not escape due to attachment to its eggs, but more likely it is overwhelmed by the gaze of the salamander and cannot move. However, the birds can fly away if they happen to see the salamander but they have not yet locked eyes with each other.
summary: Lizards such as the salamander climb up trees and eat birds as well as their eggs.
Perhaps it does not escape due to attachment to its eggs, but more likely it is overwhelmed by the gaze of the salamander and cannot move.
However, the birds can fly away if they happen to see the salamander but they have not yet locked eyes with each other.

paragraphs.text: Those creatures belonging to the coctatius group stare at their prey with a fixed gaze for a long time until water trickles from their eyes. It is not that they weep, as some people might think. It is called kumbhiiráshru in Bengali, “the tear drops of the crocodile”. In Hindi it is described as ghaŕiyáli áṋshu, the tear-drops of the ghaŕiyál, that is, crocodile. So you should understand that the crocodile never sheds tears when eyeing its prey; what we call in English “crocodile tears” are not actually tears. Due to staring at its prey for a long time, this class of creatures has been called koke in Sanskrit. ( 2 )
summary: Those creatures belonging to the coctatius group stare at their prey with a fixed gaze for a long time until water trickles from their eyes.
In Hindi it is described as ghaŕiyáli áṋshu, the tear-drops of the ghaŕiyál, that is, crocodile.
Due to staring at its prey for a long time, this class of creatures has been called koke in Sanskrit.

paragraphs.text: Iguana, Salamander: By t́it́ibha we mean the type of house lizards that live in tree holes. In Bengali and Sanskrit they are also called takśak. In most parts of East Bengal they are called gui sáp. However, we have to remember that the word gui sáp and go sáp [iguanas] are not the same. The Sanskrit name of go sáp is godhá or godhiká. In India the iguana or go sáp is divided mainly into two classes: the dark iguana (krśńa godhiká) and golden iguana (svarńa godhiká). The iguana is much larger in size than the chameleon (in Bengali girgit́i, in Sanskrit krkalása). Some iguanas of the salamander order are much larger in size than crocodiles.
summary: Iguana, Salamander: By t́it́ibha we mean the type of house lizards that live in tree holes.
The Sanskrit name of go sáp is godhá or godhiká.
Some iguanas of the salamander order are much larger in size than crocodiles.

paragraphs.text: Iguanas are fond of eating the eggs of birds by climbing up the tree. So for birds, iguanas are a source of fear. Yet iguanas are very much afraid of human beings. If they have any opening for escape, they will at once run away at the sight of a person. Large-sized iguanas can be found in Japan, Indonesia, Malaysia and in the Sundarbans in India. ( 3 )
summary: Iguanas are fond of eating the eggs of birds by climbing up the tree.
Yet iguanas are very much afraid of human beings.
Large-sized iguanas can be found in Japan, Indonesia, Malaysia and in the Sundarbans in India.

paragraphs.text: In ancient times, people believed that this lizard-like creature or go sáp ran after cows to suck the milk from their udders, and when they failed to get milk, they bite the cowsʼ udders, which caused ulcers to form. The cows became blind and even died due to the impact of the venom. Since these reptiles ran after the cows, they were called godhá>gohá >goh. At certain places they were called goh, gohágil or go sáp. Go sáp means “the snake that is associated with cows”. As indicated earlier, this reptile is much larger in size than the chameleon, and even more heavyset. In ancient times, people used to eat these iguanas after roasting them in the fire. Even today some groups of people do this. In the middle era of Bengali literature, the poet Kavikauṋkan narrates that pregnant women in Bengal used to eat roasted iguanas.
summary: In ancient times, people believed that this lizard-like creature or go sáp ran after cows to suck the milk from their udders, and when they failed to get milk, they bite the cowsʼ udders, which caused ulcers to form.
Go sáp means “the snake that is associated with cows”.
In the middle era of Bengali literature, the poet Kavikauṋkan narrates that pregnant women in Bengal used to eat roasted iguanas.

paragraphs.text: In physical appearance, dark skinned iguanas are larger in shape. In some areas of the Sundarbans, iguanas are so large in appearance that from a distance they may be mistaken for crocodiles. Of course, like the crocodiles, they belong to the reptilian order. Ranging from huge crocodiles to alligators, man-eating crocodiles, fish-eating crocodiles or ghaŕiyáls, chameleons, house lizards or tiny lizards that lie hidden in the corners of rooms, all belong to the same order of reptiles. They are born from eggs and all are carnivorous. The manner in which they grab their prey is quite similar. They all possess the capacity to create a vacuum in their palms. They can all lash with their tails during flight. Their ancestors, the coctatius, had thorny backs, the remnants of which we can still see on crocodilesʼ back. By nature they are very cruel. Those species living on land, such as iguanas, chameleons, house lizards and small lizards living in rooms, are afraid of human beings, but their amphibian relatives such as crocodiles, fish-eating crocodiles and ghaŕiyáls are not afraid of people. Sometimes, though, they run away at the sight of people in self-preservation.
summary: In physical appearance, dark skinned iguanas are larger in shape.
They all possess the capacity to create a vacuum in their palms.
Sometimes, though, they run away at the sight of people in self-preservation.

paragraphs.text: For the amphibian species, raw turmeric is as good as poison. Even for those that live on land, raw turmeric acts like poison. Since they move on their breasts, they are all reptiles. Long, green-coloured iguanas are found in Southeast Asia and Japan in great numbers, but in the Sundarbans there are only a small number; they are also called salamanders. The hide of this variety of iguana is very soft, smooth and comfortable. For this reason, during the British rule [of India] iguanas were killed and nearly obliterated. Later during the same regime, certain restrictions were imposed on the killing of these creatures. But by then, substantial harm and loss had already been caused to the iguanas. Like the water snakes (d́hoṋŕá, d́hyámná and jald́hoṋŕá), its population has also declined. Though iguanas primarily eat the eggs of birds, they also eat their own eggs. In this regard, their habits are somewhat similar to those of snakes.
summary: For the amphibian species, raw turmeric is as good as poison.
For this reason, during the British rule [of India] iguanas were killed and nearly obliterated.
In this regard, their habits are somewhat similar to those of snakes.

paragraphs.text: In the forest, in the absence of the mother and father birds, they climb up the tree and devour the eggs ceaselessly. After excessive eating, when they feel exhausted and trip over the branch of the tree and fall down; they lie flat on the ground as if dead. After digesting the eggs, they start moving once again. There is a misconception that people die if bitten by an iguana. However, it is a wrong notion. Of course, since it is a carnivorous animal, its bite does have a poisonous effect. The notion that the iguana bites and does not let a person go until the clouds burst is also not correct. Although a small creature, its cries are very loud and shrill; it sounds like a bird calling from a distant tree. In this regard it is similar to the hedge cricket and cricket.
summary: In the forest, in the absence of the mother and father birds, they climb up the tree and devour the eggs ceaselessly.
However, it is a wrong notion.
In this regard it is similar to the hedge cricket and cricket.

paragraphs.text: Non-venomous chameleon (Takśak): The takśak or guisáp is a species similar to the iguana and house lizard; they rarely live in rooms; rather, they live in the holes of large tree trunks, especially banyan trees. By nature and temperament they are more akin to go sáp [i.e., iguanas] than house lizards. They drink the sap from the pots hung on date palm trees and then run away. ( 4 )
summary: Non-venomous chameleon (Takśak): The takśak or guisáp is a species similar to the iguana and house lizard; they rarely live in rooms; rather, they live in the holes of large tree trunks, especially banyan trees.
, iguanas] than house lizards.
They drink the sap from the pots hung on date palm trees and then run away.

paragraphs.text: House lizard (t́ikt́iki): The house lizard or t́ikt́iki of Bengal is generally lean in appearance and makes a t́ikt́ik sound. Since they make a t́ikt́ik sound, they are called t́ikt́ikis. In the Auṋgiká language they are called t́ikt́ikiá. In northern Bihar and the eastern part of Uttar Pradesh, house lizards are large in size, white in appearance and are dumb. The people of this region call the house lizard bichaoti, and in Hindi they call it chipkali. In their habits, the house lizard is no exception to other lizards. As they create a vacuum in the curves of their feet, they can move quickly along the walls. While moving in this way, if they lose this vacuum grip, they fall down. The connection between the house lizard and its tail is very slender. That is why, when somebody presses down on their tail, they run away leaving it behind. They develop another tail after a few days. ( 5 )
summary: House lizard (t́ikt́iki): The house lizard or t́ikt́iki of Bengal is generally lean in appearance and makes a t́ikt́ik sound.
In their habits, the house lizard is no exception to other lizards.
They develop another tail after a few days.

paragraphs.text: You might have noticed house lizards sitting on a wall. How do they remain like that? Below the feet of most of lizards is a pad. By placing that pad on the wall, they create a vacuum, and thus remain fixed on the wall. However, when they move quickly on the wall, they cannot retain that vacuum. So they wait and move slowly, because if they move too fast, sometimes they slip to the ground.
summary: You might have noticed house lizards sitting on a wall.
By placing that pad on the wall, they create a vacuum, and thus remain fixed on the wall.
So they wait and move slowly, because if they move too fast, sometimes they slip to the ground.

paragraphs.text: You may have also noticed cockroaches. They are called telápoká in Bengali. Since they drink oil, they are called taela [oil] páyiká [that which drinks oil] in Sanskrit. From this word taela páyiká has come the Bengali word telápoká. Cockroaches are a favourite food item of house lizards. In Asia there are approximately fourteen types of cockroaches that are able to fly, but the house lizard cannot do so. The lizard order cannot fly. Nevertheless, they are all very ferocious. You may have noticed a house lizard sitting on the wall fixing its gaze on a cockroach, and the latter is quite mesmerized and has lost the power to fly. Since its nerve cells have stopped functioning, it is unable to fly with the help of its nerve fibres. Then the house lizard slowly moves forward. It moves slowly because it will fall down from the wall if it tries to move fast. The benumbed cockroach remains at that very spot, and the house lizard then slowly swallows it. After it has been partially swallowed, the cockroach becomes restless, but by then it is too late for it to escape from the mouth of the lizard.
summary: You may have also noticed cockroaches.
Nevertheless, they are all very ferocious.
After it has been partially swallowed, the cockroach becomes restless, but by then it is too late for it to escape from the mouth of the lizard.

paragraphs.text: One night I saw a house lizard swallow seventeen cockroaches. Even then it was not satisfied. After overeating, it fell down from the wall. The next morning, I saw it had died of overeating. I saw countless ants around its dead body. Notice how even overeating could not satisfy its greed. I am afraid that its greed was not quenched even at the time of death.
summary: One night I saw a house lizard swallow seventeen cockroaches.
The next morning, I saw it had died of overeating.
I am afraid that its greed was not quenched even at the time of death.

paragraphs.text: I once imported from another shore of the Bay of Bengal an Indonesian variety of a brilliant, red-tongued and red-eyed, green salamander. The place where it was kept became the source of congregation for ants. The lizard continued to swallow the ants ceaselessly as if this was its main preoccupation in life. After about two hours the salamander was dead, and I saw that the ants were biting it.
summary: I once imported from another shore of the Bay of Bengal an Indonesian variety of a brilliant, red-tongued and red-eyed, green salamander.
The lizard continued to swallow the ants ceaselessly as if this was its main preoccupation in life.
After about two hours the salamander was dead, and I saw that the ants were biting it.

paragraphs.text: In astrology books many stories have been told about the sounds or cries of these (dark) house lizards. It has also been predicted what might happen if these house lizards fall on various parts of the human body. For these species, the vacuum created in their palms is stronger than that of other species. The common name for all house lizards is pallii. In the almanac, the fall (patan) of the house lizard has been called pallii-patan.
summary: In astrology books many stories have been told about the sounds or cries of these (dark) house lizards.
For these species, the vacuum created in their palms is stronger than that of other species.
In the almanac, the fall (patan) of the house lizard has been called pallii-patan.

paragraphs.text: Any small area of the village is called pallii in Bengali, and any small village is called palliigrám. The word pallii is not a Sanskrit word. Many people think that palliigrám means a small village. The word pallii means a small area, or mahallá (Persian origin) and gańd́agrám means a big village. Gańd́agrám correctly stands for a big village, but the word gańd́a has another meaning; it means the entrance to the village. But the word palliigrám is not a Sanskrit word.
summary: Any small area of the village is called pallii in Bengali, and any small village is called palliigrám.
The word pallii means a small area, or mahallá (Persian origin) and gańd́agrám means a big village.
But the word palliigrám is not a Sanskrit word.

paragraphs.text: The word pallii stands for the house lizard. The word is of Dravidian origin, just as Trichinapalli means Srichinapalli or the village dedicated to the name of Lakśmináráyańa. Id́ápalli stands for the village of the Iid́ává community. So, although the proper name of Bhát́páŕa is Bhat́t́apallii, it is not a Sanskrit word. If we want to consider Bhat́t́apallii as a Sanskrit word, the meaning of Bhat́t́apallii would be Bhat́t́a or pandit, with pallii meaning house lizard (t́ikt́iki); that is, it will mean “pandit house lizard”. I will not say this, and if I have ever said this, I withdraw my words! ( 6 )
summary: The word pallii stands for the house lizard.
So, although the proper name of Bhát́páŕa is Bhat́t́apallii, it is not a Sanskrit word.
I will not say this, and if I have ever said this, I withdraw my words!

paragraphs.text: Golden coloured chameleon (Áiṋjuni or grhagodhiká): Many think that one will be infected ophthalmia if one touches the Aiṋjuni [small house lizard]. Hence in Bengali, ophthalmia is called áiṋjuni. It is called grhagodhiká or grhasvarńa godhiká.

paragraphs.text: Crocodiles (krkalás group): I have said before that in Sanskrit, the krkalás group of reptiles refers to the coctatius sub-order. In the ancient world, this group of animals appeared on earth several thousand years before the appearance of humans. Their ancestors were much larger in size than present-day crocodiles (kumiir). This group appeared after the appearance of dinosaurs. The primitive dinosaurs were graminivorous. However, later they split up into branches: one remained graminivorous and was bigger in size, and the other a little smaller in size. They came to have mixed food habits, meaning they were graminivorous as well as carnivorous – both vegetarian and non-vegetarian. These carnivorous dinosaurs evolved into the ancestors of the prehistoric lizards.
summary: Crocodiles (krkalás group): I have said before that in Sanskrit, the krkalás group of reptiles refers to the coctatius sub-order.
The primitive dinosaurs were graminivorous.
These carnivorous dinosaurs evolved into the ancestors of the prehistoric lizards.

paragraphs.text: There are various justifications for this hypothesis. Dinosaurs could not climb trees or move across steep hills. They had to move along the plains like human beings and cows (Zebu indica). Yet those animals belonging to the prehistoric lizards could climb trees and even up steep rocks because under their feet they had soft pads by which they could create vacuums and adhere to walls. This krkalás group of animals later split into two groups: one group comparatively large, hard-bodied and thorny, and the other comparatively soft and free from thorns on their body. Those without thorns, such as the go sáp or iguana, the girgit́i or chameleon, gui sáp or takśak, lived on land. Those with thorns habitually remained on land. To get hold of their prey, they went down into the water and, in that case, became “animals of the water”. Amongst them are crocodiles, alligators, etc.
summary: There are various justifications for this hypothesis.
This krkalás group of animals later split into two groups: one group comparatively large, hard-bodied and thorny, and the other comparatively soft and free from thorns on their body.
Amongst them are crocodiles, alligators, etc.

paragraphs.text: By nature, the thorny variety of these reptiles is very ferocious. Their mode of catching prey (i.e., catching both land and aquatic animals) is quite similar. They attack their prey even when well-fed. If they are not capable of eating their prey, they leave it to rot in a secluded spot and return to consume it some days later. This reptile, fixing its gaze for a long time on its prey, scrutinizes which part of the preyʼs body it will eat first. Due to gazing at the prey for a long time, sometimes tears trickle from its eyes. Observing this, people wrongly think that it is weeping in grief over its prey. No, this is not the case.
summary: By nature, the thorny variety of these reptiles is very ferocious.
If they are not capable of eating their prey, they leave it to rot in a secluded spot and return to consume it some days later.
No, this is not the case.

paragraphs.text: Creatures belonging to the krkalás group are all born from eggs. Almost all mesmerize their prey and then attack. By nature and habit, because they are somewhat dirty, excessively carnivorous and drink little water (those that live in water, such as crocodiles and alligators, hardly drink any water), their teeth are weak and worm-ridden, and due to being excessively carnivorous, a foul smell emanates from their bodies. In earlier days, in the Burdwan district in the River Gáuṋgur (Devidaha) and on the borders of Birbhum-Burdwan-Murshidabad in the River Kuey (at the confluence of Bakreshvar and Kopái rivers), there were plenty of crocodiles. Crocodiles also remain in the lower rung of the Rupnarayan River, in some areas of Tamluk sub-division, and in the Shyampur region of Howrah. At one time in Midnapur district, the Rasulpur and Digha rivers were full of crocodiles of the saline water. In those days the rural people of Midnapur and 24 Parganas never crossed the rivers without spears in their hands. All those narrow rivers were called kháŕi (estuary) in ancient Bengali. The water of these estuaries was invariably saline.
summary: Creatures belonging to the krkalás group are all born from eggs.
Crocodiles also remain in the lower rung of the Rupnarayan River, in some areas of Tamluk sub-division, and in the Shyampur region of Howrah.
The water of these estuaries was invariably saline.

paragraphs.text: Not only in south Bengal but in the whole of Bengal people had to live with crocodiles. In the forest-infested Bengal of those days, there were crocodiles in the water, tigers on the land and snakes like mayál (python) in the trees. It was mentioned earlier that for those creatures living in water, raw turmeric is a dangerous poison. That is why, by filling the corpses of goats with raw turmeric paste and hooking them to fishing rods, people of those times used to prey upon the crocodiles. In this context, the poet Ramprasad has written:
summary: Not only in south Bengal but in the whole of Bengal people had to live with crocodiles.
It was mentioned earlier that for those creatures living in water, raw turmeric is a dangerous poison.
That is why, by filling the corpses of goats with raw turmeric paste and hooking them to fishing rods, people of those times used to prey upon the crocodiles.

paragraphs.text: This krkalás group of reptiles – and not just the house lizard – all of them are hungry for food. So the word koke applies equally to them all. It should be remembered in this context that the coctatius have become extinct on this earth. However their fossilized remains ( 7 ) are still found in different parts of the world. I have seen in various parts of western Ráŕh the fossilized remains of these prehistoric lizards. I have brought some of these fossils to my own museum.

paragraphs.text: In assessing the present situation, crocodiles still remain in India. However, they are almost on the verge of extinction. There were also crocodiles in that part of Hazaribag district through which the Damodar River flows; they are now present only in limited numbers. Just as tigers eat people today, in those days crocodiles would swoop upon and catch human beings in their grip. It was a regular, everyday phenomenon. I heard a story regarding the crocodiles of the southern part of Midnapur. Once a certain co-wife was having a meal with banana, curd and ciŕá [pressed rice]. The news reached her that her counterpart (second co-wife) had been caught by a crocodile. If the second co-wife died, then she (the first co-wife) would become impure as per the social code and would not be allowed to finish her meal. So she continued to wolf down her meal. By the time the crocodile had finished dragging the second co-wife into its cavity, the first co-wife had also finished her breakfast. So there is a rhyme:
summary: In assessing the present situation, crocodiles still remain in India.
I heard a story regarding the crocodiles of the southern part of Midnapur.
By the time the crocodile had finished dragging the second co-wife into its cavity, the first co-wife had also finished her breakfast.

When it died and its stomach was torn open, the skeleton of her body and all her ornaments were recovered. ( 8 )

chapters.title: Nature, Characteristics and Habitats of Snakes

paragraphs.text: Hibernation of cold-blooded creatures: There are some cold-blooded creatures that cannot move during the winter. They feel exhausted during that time and succumb to cold. Some examples of these life forms are snakes, frogs, marmots, etc. Some species of the scorpion order are also reduced to this state. These creatures that go into hibernation cannot move during the winter; they are affected by a particular kind of drowsiness. They expend the fat collected in their body during this period in order to preserve the body. The heat generated by their fat keeps them alive. At the end of winter, with the touch of the refreshing warm spring breeze, they regain their power of movement. At that time they are still quite weak. Their outer skin becomes very loose because, with the consumption of fat, the external cover of the body shrinks to a certain extent.
summary: Hibernation of cold-blooded creatures: There are some cold-blooded creatures that cannot move during the winter.
They expend the fat collected in their body during this period in order to preserve the body.
Their outer skin becomes very loose because, with the consumption of fat, the external cover of the body shrinks to a certain extent.

paragraphs.text: At the end of winter when the warm season begins, like all other creatures in hibernation the snake also awakens. At that time, in comparison to its body, the outer skin is very loose. The snake then sheds its own skin. So, that discarded skin serves temporarily as its cover (kholas). In proper Bengali it is called nirmok (nir + muc + ghaiṋ suffix), or slough. When it sheds this slough, the light skin underneath is exposed. Neither sunlight nor daylight can be endured by this newly exposed skin. That is why, during this period, the snake comes out after dusk and its nature becomes sensitive and ferocious. ( 1 )
summary: At the end of winter when the warm season begins, like all other creatures in hibernation the snake also awakens.
In proper Bengali it is called nirmok (nir + muc + ghaiṋ suffix), or slough.
That is why, during this period, the snake comes out after dusk and its nature becomes sensitive and ferocious.

paragraphs.text: Snakes are cowardly by nature: Although we consider snakes as very venomous creatures, they are in reality very cowardly by nature. They are always engrossed in protecting themselves. They are always restless in apprehension of the mongoose, that is, neuls (nakula > naula > neul; barjiká > bajjiá > beji. In Bengali both beji and neul are accepted names). Furthermore, snakes are always on the alert for peacocks coming from any direction. Out of the urge for survival and self-preservation, they are continuously aggressive and hissing. Except in a few instances, they will run away given the opportunity, instead of giving chase. When the snakeʼs tail is trampled upon, it bites out of fear of death. When it sheds its skin, for some time it remains very sensitive and excitable because of its new, thin skin, and as a result it bites at the slightest provocation. Except for black cobras, most snakes will usually take the first opportunity to run away. Since black cobras have excessive venom, they are by nature hot-tempered. That is why they are fond of comparatively cold environments, despite being tropical creatures. When snakes live in cold countries, they are non-venomous.
summary: Snakes are cowardly by nature: Although we consider snakes as very venomous creatures, they are in reality very cowardly by nature.
Except in a few instances, they will run away given the opportunity, instead of giving chase.
When snakes live in cold countries, they are non-venomous.

paragraphs.text: Black cobras are a variety of gokśurá [cobra] snakes. Gokśurá snakes usually live in houses; they are particularly fond of old houses. Many people call the old snakes that have shed their tails a vástu sáp [house snake]. Since they dwell in our houses, they are called vástu sáp. We have to remember that even black cobras belong to the larger group of gokśurá class. In English they all belong to the cobra suborder. Even the largest, most venomous snake, candracuŕa is called “king cobra” in English. This gokśuro or gokśura is generally known in the western part of Ráŕh as kharish. Due to the general habits of snakes – their way of searching out their foes for self preservation – the one meaning of the word d́ha, derived from d́huńd́ha + d́a, is snake.
summary: Black cobras are a variety of gokśurá [cobra] snakes.
We have to remember that even black cobras belong to the larger group of gokśurá class.
Due to the general habits of snakes – their way of searching out their foes for self preservation – the one meaning of the word d́ha, derived from d́huńd́ha + d́a, is snake.

paragraphs.text: Snakes are the natural enemies of human beings and most other creatures. Snakes are as much afraid of people as people are afraid of snakes. Usually non-venomous snakes do not have any circle on their skin; however, venomous snakes are never without circles on their bodies. Of course, there are some exceptions. Non-venomous snakes are called d́hoṋŕá in Bengali. I shall be talking about d́hoṋŕá shortly.
summary: Snakes are the natural enemies of human beings and most other creatures.
Of course, there are some exceptions.
I shall be talking about d́hoṋŕá shortly.

paragraphs.text: Cit́i, Hele and other species of non-venomous snakes belong mainly to the d́hoṋŕá category. Human beings are afraid of venomous snakes. There is a story:
summary: Cit́i, Hele and other species of non-venomous snakes belong mainly to the d́hoṋŕá category.
Human beings are afraid of venomous snakes.

paragraphs.text: To make fun of a blind man, a clever man said, “Oh blind man, there is a snake.” The blind man, unable to see it, reacted in fright, “Oh god, that cursed snakeʼs hood!” Now the clever man, feigning ignorance, said, “Where is it? Where is it?” Then the blind man retorted, ”Why, stupid, you only said it!” ( 2 )
summary: To make fun of a blind man, a clever man said, “Oh blind man, there is a snake.
” Now the clever man, feigning ignorance, said, “Where is it?
” Then the blind man retorted, ”Why, stupid, you only said it!

paragraphs.text: Habitats of snakes: In Iceland there are no snakes. In Ireland also hardly any can be found. If any snakes exist at all in Ireland, they are non-venomous. Remember, if there are venomous snakes, it can only be in a tropical habitat. Compared to Bengal, Rajasthan and Punjab are warmer, but in the latter the heat is dry; they are not humid regions. So compared to Bengal, the snake population is very small. In Bengal, Southeast Asia and parts of South America where, along with a hot, humid climate there is excessive rain, an abundance of snakes is sure to be found. As mentioned earlier, among snakes the largest venomous snakes are the king cobras (shauṋkhacuŕa). They are the original inhabitants of Bengal and Southeast Asia. Then there are venomous snakes; gokhro (gokśura: in Ráŕhii Bengali kharish cobra, in North India gahuman), keut́e or black cobra, rattlesnake or jhumjhumi sáp – they are all inhabitants of such a climate.
summary: Habitats of snakes: In Iceland there are no snakes.
So compared to Bengal, the snake population is very small.

Then there are venomous snakes; gokhro (gokśura: in Ráŕhii Bengali kharish cobra, in North India gahuman), keut́e or black cobra, rattlesnake or jhumjhumi sáp – they are all inhabitants of such a climate.

paragraphs.text: During British rule, a census revealed that Burdwan district had the highest number of deaths from snakebites. One can easily surmise that the highest number of snakes was prevalent in that district. Generally the snakebites occurred near ponds. The reason can be easily understood. Since Burdwan is a western district [of Bengal], summers were long and the rainy season was likewise prolonged. Being the land of sticky, clayish soil, there are plenty of ponds. In the sandy, soft earth the snake pits are readily filled with rain water. Yet it does not happen in sticky soil. The pits remain undisturbed for a longer period. For this reason, snakes thrived there. Since certain circumstances have changed, the number of snakes in that district has diminished substantially. Nevertheless, the eastern part of Burdwan district continues to have a significantly larger snake population.
summary: During British rule, a census revealed that Burdwan district had the highest number of deaths from snakebites.
In the sandy, soft earth the snake pits are readily filled with rain water.
Nevertheless, the eastern part of Burdwan district continues to have a significantly larger snake population.

paragraphs.text: In any case, you can understand that just as Bengal, being the land of rivers and canals, is the land of crocodiles, similarly it is also the land of snakes. This is because it is a region having excessive rain, heat and humidity. In this regard, Bengal is also the land of tigers that likewise prefer dense forest and exceedingly long summers followed by abundant rain. In ancient times in Bengal, except for the periphery of Ráŕh, there were few lions, but tigers thrived because it was the land of dense forests. Only along the periphery of western Ráŕh did lions and tigers live. Today tigers are on the verge of extinction, and there are no remnants of lion species in Bengal. The lions of Ráŕh have been extinct for the past two hundred years. There may be one or two lone survivors. However, if at all they exist, they are barely visible.
summary: In any case, you can understand that just as Bengal, being the land of rivers and canals, is the land of crocodiles, similarly it is also the land of snakes.
Only along the periphery of western Ráŕh did lions and tigers live.
However, if at all they exist, they are barely visible.

paragraphs.text: Worship of the Snake-Goddess out of fear: Being in the land of snakes, the inhabitants of Bengal worshipped their imaginatively conceived goddess of snakes, to whom they were devoted. In the pre-Buddhist era the goddess of snakes was known as Viśahari. In the Maháyánii Buddhist era, this laokika or folk-goddess was raised to the status of ritual worship. She was called Manasá. In the Puranic age, Manasá was looked upon as the daughter of Lord Shiva, and was also known as the daughter of the sage Káshyapa. According to the Puranas:
summary: Worship of the Snake-Goddess out of fear: Being in the land of snakes, the inhabitants of Bengal worshipped their imaginatively conceived goddess of snakes, to whom they were devoted.
In the Maháyánii Buddhist era, this laokika or folk-goddess was raised to the status of ritual worship.
In the Puranic age, Manasá was looked upon as the daughter of Lord Shiva, and was also known as the daughter of the sage Káshyapa.

paragraphs.text: The overindulgence of Manasá worship or devotion to the goddess Manasá is found only in the snake-infested regions of India. You will notice that, because people who relied on gods and fate, tried to safeguard themselves, Manasádevii emerged. However, in all countries there are always some practically minded people. People noticed that nakul (neul or beji, in English “mongoose”), keráńi pákhi [a bird of the woodpecker subfamily] and peacocks are very adept at killing snakes. The nakul kills snakes but has little interest in eating them. Unless compelled to do so, it does not eat snakes. Human beings who eat snakes generally sever the head and eat the rest of the body. Keráńi pákhi both kills and eats the snake, yet it hardly relishes eating it. However, the peacock both kills snakes as well as relishes eating them. More than male peacocks, the female peacocks are adept at killing as well as eating snakes. In ancient times people worshipped the goddess Manasá, but in pursuit of pragmatism they kept mongooses and peacocks as pets. They were more interested in keeping peacocks than mongooses as pets, because mongooses kill snakes only when they encounter them. In contrast, peacocks consider snakes as their food, and hence actively seek them out in their resting places and kill them. Those pet peacocks that were adept at killing snakes and trained for this work were called garavrata in ancient times. ( 3 )
summary: The overindulgence of Manasá worship or devotion to the goddess Manasá is found only in the snake-infested regions of India.
Keráńi pákhi both kills and eats the snake, yet it hardly relishes eating it.
Those pet peacocks that were adept at killing snakes and trained for this work were called garavrata in ancient times.

paragraphs.text: Python: You all know that because of the differences between non-venomous and venomous snakes, snakes are of two kinds. The large-sized snakes are mostly non-venomous. Also, venomous snakes are not equally venomous. Compared to other venomous snakes, the black cobra is by far the most venomous. They are divided into álkeut́e, kálkeut́e, gharkeut́e, gáckeut́e and other species: gokhro snakes (gokśurá, cobra; in Ráŕh Bengali called kharish) are divided into káligokhro, padma-gokhro, cakra-gokhro and other species. These gokhros are less venomous than the keut́e (black cobra). Apart from this, in [India] the other venomous snakes are laud́agá, sháṋkhámut́i, dumukho, biściti, etc. In America there is the rattlesnake (jhumjhumi sáp). In Southeastern Asia, among the venomous snakes the largest in size is the shauṋkhacuŕa (king cobra). They prefer humid forest areas. In the Sundarbans, sometimes a king cobra of fifteen to sixteen feet length can be found. In Burma, Malaysia, Indonesia and Thailand, king cobras of twenty-four to twenty-five feet length are found. These snakes are very venomous. Snake venom is used in preparing different kinds of medicines.
summary: Python: You all know that because of the differences between non-venomous and venomous snakes, snakes are of two kinds.
In America there is the rattlesnake (jhumjhumi sáp).
Snake venom is used in preparing different kinds of medicines.

paragraphs.text: Now let us come to our discussion on pythons. Pythons are large-sized, non-venomous snakes. In English we call it python, in Bengali, mayál. A python can easily swallow a goat. That is why it is called ajagar. All creatures belonging to the snake species maintain certain fixed habits. One of them is hibernation. Many cold-blooded creatures go into hibernation during the winter for a prolonged sleep. For several months they lie almost unconscious. Even if their limbs are chopped off, their sleep remains unbroken.
summary: Now let us come to our discussion on pythons.
All creatures belonging to the snake species maintain certain fixed habits.
Even if their limbs are chopped off, their sleep remains unbroken.

paragraphs.text: In [India] primarily snakes, frogs and ucciḿŕe hibernate in winter. Marmots (a rodent) that reside in cold countries, and a few in the Indian Himalayas, have the longest period of hibernation. As mentioned earlier, during this hibernation they consume their reserved energy. As a result of the reduced fat reserve in the body, when their sleep is broken with the arrival of spring, they appear very lean and thin. For this reason, their outer skin becomes very loose. They then have no alternative but to shed that old skin. When the warm breeze touches their body, snakes shed this outer crust. The inner skin of the snakeʼs body then becomes very sensitive. So the mood and temperament of the snake is very much on edge. Pythons are no exception to this rule. Of course, they do not hibernate for a long period. You all know that snakes have so many different names – bhujaga, bhujauṋga, bhujauṋgama, áshiibiś, ahi, phańii, etc. Their body functions like hands, and they are able to move with its support. Hence one of their names is bhujaga. Both bhujauṋgama and bhujauṋga have the same meaning. Generally pythons do not have venom. Therefore, the word áshiibiś [poisonous] is not applicable, as the word does not refer to non-venomous snakes. Usually non-venomous snakes do not have any hood [phań or phańá]. So also is the case with pythons. So they cannot be called phańii. ( 1 )
summary: In [India] primarily snakes, frogs and ucciḿŕe hibernate in winter.
Of course, they do not hibernate for a long period.
So they cannot be called phańii.

paragraphs.text: The python can eat a tremendous amount. Once they have filled their stomach, they remain in a still, motionless state for many days. Thereafter, once the food has been digested, they again start to move around. Thus, another meaning of the word karvva is ajagar [python]. In this case aja means “goat”. That which can swallow a goat is ajagar. ( 2 )

They are not as dangerous as their names would suggest; in fact, they are not at all dangerous. They have been given such names possibly because they are rather large in size. ( 3 )

paragraphs.text: Cobra and black cobra: You already know that cobras (gokhros) and black cobras (keut́es) are different species of the same subfamily of snakes. Black cobras are slender, blackish and refuse to stay in houses; they live in forests and jungles and on the outskirts of inhabited land. Although they are cold-blooded, their temperament is very hot. Their body does not emit a sweet aroma but rather a pungent smell, which may be due to their temperament and nerves. This particular pungent smell often emanates from the body of an ordinary man. A different kind of pungent smell emanates from the body of a courageous man. Then again, if the courageous man is of pious nature, the smell emanating from his body is somewhat like the piquant smell of marigold blossoms. If the man is only of pious nature, the smell emanating from his body is like the drenched earth after the first shower of rain. Belonging to the same family as the black cobras but of a different species are the cobras. The difference in temperament between the cobra and the black cobra is that cobras prefer to stay in peopleʼs houses, especially in derelict houses. Although they live in forests and jungles and next to ponds, they are very fond of abandoned houses. The venom of the black cobra is more potent than that of other cobras, but less than that of the largest – the king cobra shauṋkhacuŕa.
summary: Cobra and black cobra: You already know that cobras (gokhros) and black cobras (keut́es) are different species of the same subfamily of snakes.

paragraphs.text: Cobras on their own do not bite anyone. But if someone tramples upon them without realizing it, they bite in self-defence. Due to advanced old age, when they are bereft of their tails, they find it difficult to move. At that stage they no longer react to any creature or bite it. They live on ripe bananas, insects, milk and fatty items. In rural areas they are called vástu sáp [house-snakes]. Some people do not kill them. Whatever may be the case, no intelligent person should knowingly allow venomous creatures to live in their house – Sarpena saha grihe na vása – whatever you may or may not do to your enemies, you must not under any circumstances live with them in the same house. Some people keep the house-snake somewhere in the corner of their house, and feed it milk and ever ripe bananas. We proverbially say, “Nourishing the snakes with milk and bananas.”

In rural areas they are called vástu sáp [house-snakes].

paragraphs.text: In its old age, the smell of unparboiled rice emanates from the body of the cobra snake, due to secretion of a particular hormone. If you smell the fragrance of unparboiled rice in any part of your house, you must check whether there is a snake hiding in any hole in that area. Snakes cannot dig their own holes. They occupy the holes of rats after killing them. When the smell of the sun-dried unparboiled rice emanates from the body of a gokhro snake, it is called gandha-sarpa (káli-gokhro, padma-gokhro, cakra-gokhro, etc). ( 1 )

paragraphs.text: You must have also heard about kálasarpa. The black cobra is a sub species of gokśura [Cobra de capello]. A gokśura is called gokhro in the Kolkata region. In the Ráŕh region, both the names – gokhro and kharish – are prevalent. [As told little earlier] Gokśura has many species and subspecies – kaligokhro, padmagokhro, shauṋkha gokhro, etc., are examples. The keut́e or black cobra has several species and subspecies, such as kálakeut́e, álkeut́e, etc. A black cobra generally lives outdoors in fields away from human habitation. Kálakeut́e generally lives away from human habitation in forests, bushes and shrubs. Since the body of álkeut́e is very warm [in comparison to other snakes], it usurps rat holes on the sides of embankments in the rice fields [ál in colloquial Bengali] and lives there. When it feels very hot, it keeps its body submerged in water, keeping only its head above the water. Although álkeut́e is short, thin and as venomous as any snake of the cobra family, its temper is always very hot. If any person walking on the ridge inadvertently disturbs its peace, it at once rushes out and bites that person. But other snakes do not rush out to bite; they bite only in self-defence. Álkeut́e, kálakeut́e and common keut́e – all three – cannot stand heat. Many times they lie entwined along the rail lines at night when the rails are somewhat cold. On hearing the sound of a coming train, other snakes flee the rail lines, but the ill-tempered keut́e does not. Possibly it thinks, “Whom do I fear enough to run away from?” Accordingly it remains on the line. So most of the snakes that are run over by trains in the summertime, are keut́es. The Sanskrit name of this keut́e is krśńagokśura or kálasarpa.

paragraphs.text: The word sarpa is derived from the verbal root srp, which means, “to crawl on the chest”. In English also, the word “reptile” means “to crawl with the support of the chest”. This krśńagokśura or kálasarpa can be called simply kála.

paragraphs.text: The snake is one of the oldest creatures on earth. The snake appeared on the earth long before the appearance of quadrupeds; in fact, even long before the appearance of birds. The snake belongs to the reptile species. The nature of a snakeʼs blood makes it difficult for it to survive in a cold country. Even in hot countries, snakes go into hibernation for several months during winter. Generally it can be said that the few snakes we find in cold countries are non-venomous. Snakes live primarily in tropical countries, particularly where there are adequate wet lands. In Bengal, India and Southeast Asia, particularly in the land of Shyámdesh [Thailand], the number of snakes and reptiles is exorbitantly high. I had direct, eye-witness experience of this when I was in Thailand. The climate of Bengal is fairly similar to that of Thailand. That is why Bengal is nearly as snake-infested as Thailand. A poet of Bengal has said:

The stories of Manasámauṋgal, Padmávatii (Padumávát) as well the stories of Behulá and Lakhindar are particularly prevalent in eastern India. Most villages organize ritualistic ceremonies related to Manasá in the month of Bhádra. These ceremonies are held more often in the villages that have greater fear of snakes:

paragraphs.text: A snake runs away on seeing smoke. So Manasá, the snake-goddess, also does not like smoke. So runs the proverb, like eke má manasá tár opare dhunor gandha [“First it is Mother Manasá, and then on top of it the smell of burning incense.”] A snake fears the human being more than a human being fears the snake. However defeated in the war of intelligence, the snake family is about to disappear completely from the surface of the earth. Furthermore, after human beings came to know about the medicinal values of snake venoms, they began killing snakes to collect the venom. Snake venom is used in various medicines prepared in allopathy, unani, ayurveda and homeopathy, (Naja-cobra). In the Indian ayurvedic system, the effectiveness of spider venom, bee venom and snake venom in the treatment of poison has been clearly stated.

paragraphs.text: In astrology, a particular malefic constellation of stars is called kálasarpayoga. Some people believe that the congregation of too many planets in one particular house of the zodiac can bring about a cataclysmic upheaval in the world, and according to others, it can cause the total dissolution of the world. But, it has been seen that no such catastrophe takes place in reality. It is just possible, in the worst case scenario, that when a number of planets crowd together in the same orbit or the same angle of a particular house (of the zodiac), there is some radiational imbalance [from the planets]. This imbalance will not necessarily bring about a catastrophe – who knows, it may do good instead. Whatever the case may be, you are now acquainted with the word kálasarpayoga. ( 2 )
summary: In astrology, a particular malefic constellation of stars is called kálasarpayoga.

paragraphs.text: Snakes are normally timid creatures. They are always busy in protecting themselves against enemies. But black cobras are a marked exception. They come chasing and also bite. Perhaps they want to eliminate the possibility of being attacked, hence their aggressive attitude. They chase even an innocent person walking along the paddy field and bite them. Among venomous snakes shauṋkhacuŕas are the largest in appearance. The rattlesnakes of North America are very close to the cobra species but are not exactly cobra. In Ráŕh Bengal, ninety percent of the deaths from snakebite are caused by the cobras.

Perhaps they want to eliminate the possibility of being attacked, hence their aggressive attitude.

paragraphs.text: King cobra (shauṋkhacuŕas): Nága means a big snake. The word krśńa-nága stands for shauṋkhacuŕa [king cobra]. In India, especially in the Sundarbans in Bengal, king cobra snakes are fifteen to sixteen feet in length. In regions of Southeast Asia they are sometimes twenty-four to twenty-five feet in length. Of the venomous snakes, king cobras are the largest in size. The circles on their heads are placed in succession, like the shauṋkha or conch shell. Hence they are named accordingly. They are not black in colour. As they are extremely venomous, they are called krśńanága [black snake]. In the legend of Krśńa of Dváparyuga, the story of Káliyánága or Kálnága probably refers to this shauṋkhacuŕa or krśńanága.

paragraphs.text: As a result of unbounded slaughter by human beings, king cobras have reached their final stage of existence. Unless arrangements are made immediately for their preservation, perhaps in the near future they will also be annihilated from the face of the earth. They will meet the same fate as the dodo birds and Indian leopards. ( 3 )

paragraphs.text: Green camouflage snake (láud́agá): You might have occasionally seen a sort of green snake among green creeping plants. Their eyes glisten because they are green. That makes people afraid; they think that these snakes must be highly venomous. These snakes are called láud́agá [Opheodrys aestivus] snakes in certain parts of Bengal. They stare at a person from behind the leaves when they see that person approaching them. They are not easily visible at first because of their green camouflage. People run away the moment they see them. This láud́agá snake is also called kulaka.
summary: Green camouflage snake (láud́agá): You might have occasionally seen a sort of green snake among green creeping plants.
They stare at a person from behind the leaves when they see that person approaching them.

paragraphs.text: There is a controversy over whether or not this láud́agá snake actually bites people, whether or not they are venomous at all, and whether or not they belong to the snake suborder or the coctatius group. But many people believe that they are venomous. They are one among a number of creatures who live or keep themselves alive by camouflage. But they are not chameleons. Nor are they related in any way to the coctatius group creature that we call the chameleon. They are natural camouflage artists, and like other such creatures, they camouflage themselves to hunt their prey or to protect themselves from hunters. Lions, giraffes, and several species of deer are also creatures that create natural camouflage. There is a variety of tame deer that survives through natural camouflage. Generally lions, giraffes, and certain types of deer and golden iguana live in larger numbers in the desert areas or in areas where the surrounding natural colours are grey or sandy. Their enemies, their hunters and their prey cannot recognize them because their colour merges with the colour of their surroundings. This is called prákrtik varńavibhránti [“natural camouflage”].
summary: There is a controversy over whether or not this láud́agá snake actually bites people, whether or not they are venomous at all, and whether or not they belong to the snake suborder or the coctatius group.

paragraphs.text: Creating confusion in the mind of the enemy through camouflage has been practiced since ancient times in different armies of different countries by wearing khaki dress and other such colours. The purpose was to camouflage their presence by dint of the colour of the army dress merging into that of their surroundings. In any case, this láud́agá snake takes full advantage of the opportunity afforded by camouflage. ( 4 )

paragraphs.text: Snake venom therapy: You may perhaps know that on the basis of the principle Sama samaḿ shamayati [“poison controls poison”], the noble Hahnemann devised his theory called homeopathy, which is an invaluable treasure in human intellectual research. If this knowledge is properly utilized, new kinds of research could take place not only in the world of therapeutics, but in other realms of knowledge as well, and humanity would move boldly forward in different spheres of universal wisdom. The use of snake venom in human medicine has existed since the pre-Aryan age – it was very much prevalent at the time of the Mahábhárata. As in homeopathic medicine, the snake venom is used [such as cobra or Naja], so also other kinds of venom, such as bee-venom (Apis indica) were used. Still other kinds of poison are used today in medical treatment. We can assume that there would be further use of poisons in the future. In ancient India, the use of poison as medicine was widely prevalent. People benumbed with poison were saved or revived by the use of snake venom. When the Kaoravas poisoned them, the benumbed Pandavas, particularly the middle one, Bhimsen, recovered after being treated with snake venom. In those days, the venom of snakes, scorpions, spiders, and honey bees were all used as medicine. This method of treatment using poison acquired great importance and recognition in Kerala. In the royal family of Cochin, several kings and princes won fame in the use of this kind of therapy. ( 5 )
summary: Snake venom therapy: You may perhaps know that on the basis of the principle Sama samaḿ shamayati [“poison controls poison”], the noble Hahnemann devised his theory called homeopathy, which is an invaluable treasure in human intellectual research.
In ancient India, the use of poison as medicine was widely prevalent.
In the royal family of Cochin, several kings and princes won fame in the use of this kind of therapy.

paragraphs.text: For your information, however, let me tell you that only the male peacock dances and not the female peacock, which itself has no unfurled tail. Similarly, the female frog does not croak, only the male frog croaks. The croaking of the frogs that you hear is all done by the male frog. Of course, it is said that there is an exception in the case of kat́kat́e vyáuṋga [frogs making harsh sounds]. It is said that even the female of this species croaks. The large frogs in Bengal that croak as they sit beside the pond sands are known as kolá-vyáuṋgas (hefty Bengal frog). Their colour is slightly blackish, and they are physically hefty-looking. The tadpoles that emerge from their eggs during the rainy season have lengthy tails. Gál phulo kolá vyáuṋg dákiche ghyáuṋgar ghyáuṋg – meaning, the kolá-vyáung with swollen necks croaking – is a commonplace sight that you all come across in the rainy season.
summary: For your information, however, let me tell you that only the male peacock dances and not the female peacock, which itself has no unfurled tail.
It is said that even the female of this species croaks.
Gál phulo kolá vyáuṋg dákiche ghyáuṋgar ghyáuṋg – meaning, the kolá-vyáung with swollen necks croaking – is a commonplace sight that you all come across in the rainy season.

paragraphs.text: In appearance, almost equal in size to the kolá-byáuṋ, perhaps slightly smaller, is the golden-coloured frog, which we would call sońá-vyáuṋg. It is very handsome and its cry is also very forceful. In Sanskrit it is called svarńamańd́uka or svarńavyáuṋg. The kat́kat́e-vyáuṋg is much smaller in size than the sońá-vyáuṋg; its colour is light black, and it makes a harsh, croaking sound; it is also very adept at swallowing mosquitoes. This kind of frog lives more often on land than in water. The kuńo-vyáuṋg [frog likes to live in corners] typically keeps itself concealed in the nooks and crevices of the house or farmyard. It does not overly like exposure to light. If you disturb it, [this frog] will again find shelter in a shady corner. As it prefers to live in corners, it is called kuńo-vyáuṋg.
summary: In appearance, almost equal in size to the kolá-byáuṋ, perhaps slightly smaller, is the golden-coloured frog, which we would call sońá-vyáuṋg.
This kind of frog lives more often on land than in water.
As it prefers to live in corners, it is called kuńo-vyáuṋg.

paragraphs.text: The man who does not like to go out of the house for weeks and keeps himself concealed in the house is known as kuńo or ghar-kuńo [house concealed]. You may have dislike for such people. Is it not so?
summary: The man who does not like to go out of the house for weeks and keeps himself concealed in the house is known as kuńo or ghar-kuńo [house concealed].
You may have dislike for such people.

paragraphs.text: There is another type of frog that spends most of the year in hibernation and lives very close to water during the rainy season. It can also fly for a few feet. That is why it is called the flying frog (uŕukku-vyáuṋg). In warmer regions to the south of the Mediterranean Ocean, and especially in the coastal regions of Africa, they even live on the sea. Like the flying fish, they fly in the air for some time and then dive into the water.
summary: There is another type of frog that spends most of the year in hibernation and lives very close to water during the rainy season.
That is why it is called the flying frog (uŕukku-vyáuṋg).
Like the flying fish, they fly in the air for some time and then dive into the water.

paragraphs.text: In East Bengal, among wild growths of the edible root called kocu (arum), one can find a species of large kolá-vyáuṋgs. They are few in number and their cries are very forceful. They croak in unison and it sounds very musical. In the folksongs of Mymensing [East Bengal, now Bangladesh] there is a familiar tune:

They are few in number and their cries are very forceful.
They croak in unison and it sounds very musical.

paragraphs.text: All of you must have seen the tadpoles of frogs. In Sanskrit vyáuṋg means “fun and humour.” Vyáuṋg also means “frogs.” Look at the physical appearance of any frog and you will notice that the limbs of this creature are very loose or slack, for which reason it is called vyáuṋg in Sanskrit. The newly born tadpole has a tail. As long as it has that tail, it is described as a tadpole. When the tail drops off, it is called a frog. You will notice that the frog is always moving its mouth. When it eats, it moves its mouth automatically; when it makes noises or croaks, it vibrates its throat. The female frog does not make any noise; still it vibrates its throat.
summary: All of you must have seen the tadpoles of frogs.
As long as it has that tail, it is described as a tadpole.
The female frog does not make any noise; still it vibrates its throat.

paragraphs.text: Young ducks and hens may eat too much and die of dysentery epidemic; the same thing happens with young frogs, and with even greater regularity. Tadpoles die of overeating in huge numbers, rather in the millions. ( 2 )
summary: Young ducks and hens may eat too much and die of dysentery epidemic; the same thing happens with young frogs, and with even greater regularity.
