chapters.title: Nature, Characteristics and Habits of Elephants

paragraphs.text: Primitive Mammoth: In English, the word for aerávat is mammoth. You certainly describe a large meeting as a “mammoth meeting”. This mammoth was a prehistoric animal. Their descendants are the elephants. In the world today, among the various elephant species the largest one is the African elephant. It is somewhat lacking in intelligence, but is quite huge in height. It is surmised that the primitive mammoth was twice the size of these African elephants. Their tusk was quite long. This huge animal, lacking in intelligence, became extinct nearly half a million years ago. Fossils of this creature have been found in certain areas of Bankura and Purulia. Others have even been found in the eastern part of Ranchi district in the Suvarnarekha Valley. In any case, from what we have come to know thus far, after the primitive dinosaur, these mammoths were the largest creatures to appear on earth. In other words, they were the “second-order” animals in the animal kingdom. Still, it must be remembered that mammoths and dinosaurs did not belong to the same period. Dinosaurs were more primitive than mammoths. In addition, among dinosaurs, the huge-sized dinosaurs (mainly vegetarian) were more primitive than the smaller (mainly non-vegetarian) dinosaurs. ( 1 ) It is surmised that since they were food for the smaller dinosaurs, these huge mammoths became extinct long ago. The smaller-sized dinosaurs became extinct during an Ice Age, most probably under the cover of snow.
summary: Primitive Mammoth: In English, the word for aerávat is mammoth.
Fossils of this creature have been found in certain areas of Bankura and Purulia.
The smaller-sized dinosaurs became extinct during an Ice Age, most probably under the cover of snow.

paragraphs.text: Yes, I was speaking of the aerávats (mammoths). “Risen from the sea” – if that is the etymological meaning of “mammoths” – then in that sense, whatever comes from the sea can be called aerávats, however small or large they might be in appearance.
summary: Yes, I was speaking of the aerávats (mammoths).
“Risen from the sea” – if that is the etymological meaning of “mammoths” – then in that sense, whatever comes from the sea can be called aerávats, however small or large they might be in appearance.

paragraphs.text: The imaginary páriját flowers, the imaginary amrta (nectar), aerávat and Puranic Mahálakśmii, are also, in that sense aerávat. Again, the silakantha, or primitive fish, and todayʼs conch shells, octopus and iodine, in that sense also belong to the category of aerávat; but in common usage only mammoths are aerávats and no one else. ( 2 )
summary: The imaginary páriját flowers, the imaginary amrta (nectar), aerávat and Puranic Mahálakśmii, are also, in that sense aerávat.

Again, the silakantha, or primitive fish, and todayʼs conch shells, octopus and iodine, in that sense also belong to the category of aerávat; but in common usage only mammoths are aerávats and no one else.

paragraphs.text: Elephants are endangered animals: In ancient times, in various countries of the world, there were several types of elephants (hátii) of different colours and species. Now, because of deforestation, the habitats of elephants have been reduced, more or less, to Africa and India. In addition, in the northern and western parts of India, elephants are nearly extinct. They exist only in the southern and eastern parts of India. To the south, in Andhra Pradesh (adjacent to Orissa), in Karnataka, and in some parts of Kerala they are still found. In the highly crowded state of Kerala there are few forests. Earlier, when there were ample forests, tall and handsome elephants lived there. Some of these elephants could be found in the well-known forest reserves of Tekkari in Kerala. In the state of Karnataka, there was once a predominance of elephants.
summary: Elephants are endangered animals: In ancient times, in various countries of the world, there were several types of elephants (hátii) of different colours and species.
To the south, in Andhra Pradesh (adjacent to Orissa), in Karnataka, and in some parts of Kerala they are still found.
In the state of Karnataka, there was once a predominance of elephants.

paragraphs.text: Until recently, elephants were caught with the help of improvised traps (khedás). However, in Orissa there was no such practice of catching elephants. In the mountainous parts of Orissa, better known as Koshal, there were once a good number of elephants; their population had diminished; but now, with Government protection, their numbers are rising.
summary: Until recently, elephants were caught with the help of improvised traps (khedás).
However, in Orissa there was no such practice of catching elephants.
In the mountainous parts of Orissa, better known as Koshal, there were once a good number of elephants; their population had diminished; but now, with Government protection, their numbers are rising.

paragraphs.text: In Bihar, in the Ráŕh region of Bengal, there were large numbers of elephants. Due to fear of elephants during autumn and winter, people used to light fires outside their homes to scare them away. Today there are still elephants in Bhanjabhum in Ráŕh, in Dhalbhum, in Jhargram, in the southwestern part of Bankura, in some areas of the north Midnapur Sadar (main), in Purulia, and in the hilly areas of Seraikella and Dalma. There were once plenty of elephants, even mammoths, in the Jaicandi hills of Purulia, in the hills of Tilabani, in the Panchakot hills, and in the hills of Sushunia and Beharinath (according to some, Beharilal). I once saw fossils of mammoths in these areas. The age of mammoths came to an end several million years ago. Although the elephant era still continues, there are no elephants in those regions today. In the hills of Purulia, Ayodhya, Taherbera, and especially Jabar, there remain some elephants, which enter the villages during winter in search of ripe paddy and maize.
summary: In Bihar, in the Ráŕh region of Bengal, there were large numbers of elephants.
I once saw fossils of mammoths in these areas.
In the hills of Purulia, Ayodhya, Taherbera, and especially Jabar, there remain some elephants, which enter the villages during winter in search of ripe paddy and maize.

paragraphs.text: In the northern parts of West Bengal, in Coochbehar, Jalpaiguri, Siliguri, and in the forest areas of Goalpara, the number of large elephants and their dominion was quite impressive. Today their number has dwindled almost into non-existence. Nevertheless, a few of them remain. In Meghalaya, in the northern part of Maymansingh, in the northern part of Sylhet district, everywhere in Cachhar district, in the Nowgong and Karbiang, there were once plenty of elephants. They belong to the species of small elephants that are very clever.
summary: In the northern parts of West Bengal, in Coochbehar, Jalpaiguri, Siliguri, and in the forest areas of Goalpara, the number of large elephants and their dominion was quite impressive.
Nevertheless, a few of them remain.
They belong to the species of small elephants that are very clever.

paragraphs.text: One feels uneasy upon realizing that once upon a time, in the forest of Naritabari, Sarisabari, Susanga and Bhawal [in Bangladesh], hordes of elephants used to roam. Even until the end of the Moghul period, elephants of smaller size were in abundance in Tripura. After the battle between the King of Tripura and the Moghul emperor, the ruler of Tripura offered elephants as a gift to the emperor.
summary: One feels uneasy upon realizing that once upon a time, in the forest of Naritabari, Sarisabari, Susanga and Bhawal [in Bangladesh], hordes of elephants used to roam.
Even until the end of the Moghul period, elephants of smaller size were in abundance in Tripura.
After the battle between the King of Tripura and the Moghul emperor, the ruler of Tripura offered elephants as a gift to the emperor.

paragraphs.text: Since the forests of Tripura have been reduced, the number of elephants there has also diminished. Some elephants are still found in Mizoram, Manipur, along the borders of Nagaland, Arunachal, and the Brahmaputra valley of Assam. They are quite large in size. They now heave a sigh of relief after the creation of the Kaziranga forest reserves. They have also been saved to some extent from the khedá operations, that is, improvised traps set by poachers inside the jungles to capture elephants.
summary: Since the forests of Tripura have been reduced, the number of elephants there has also diminished.
They are quite large in size.
They have also been saved to some extent from the khedá operations, that is, improvised traps set by poachers inside the jungles to capture elephants.

paragraphs.text: Since ancient times, Assam or Prágjyotiśpur or Kamrup was quite famous for its elephants. That is why in ancient Sanskrit literature, Kamrup was not only known as Kámákhyádhám but also as Gajadhám [land of the elephant]. In Assam even today, khedá operations are carried out. In one of my earlier discourses I mentioned that at one time, elephants were bought and sold throughout the year, but particularly during Kárttik Purńimá at the Hariharkśetra fair (in Hazipur district of Bihar). Nowadays there are more people wanting to sell their elephants, but only a few people interested to purchase them. In Gajadhám (Kamrup) at one time the number of elephants decreased substantially. I am now told that it has risen slightly. Still, compared to other parts of India, the number of elephants in Kamrup is appreciably more than that of other places.
summary: Since ancient times, Assam or Prágjyotiśpur or Kamrup was quite famous for its elephants.
Nowadays there are more people wanting to sell their elephants, but only a few people interested to purchase them.
Still, compared to other parts of India, the number of elephants in Kamrup is appreciably more than that of other places.

paragraphs.text: At one time hordes of elephants used to move about in the forests of western Ráŕh, especially in the forests of the adjoining hills and hillocks (duḿri). Although the number of elephants has been reduced, they are still quite prevalent. Of course, their number is greater in the forests of Jhargram, Bhanjabhum and Dhalbhum, in Jabar Hills, Dalma Hills, and in the areas adjoining the Ayodhya Hills. When elephants make an inroad into the villages in quest of ripe paddy and maize, the villagers kneel down with folded hands and say their prayers:
summary: At one time hordes of elephants used to move about in the forests of western Ráŕh, especially in the forests of the adjoining hills and hillocks (duḿri).
Although the number of elephants has been reduced, they are still quite prevalent.
Of course, their number is greater in the forests of Jhargram, Bhanjabhum and Dhalbhum, in Jabar Hills, Dalma Hills, and in the areas adjoining the Ayodhya Hills.

But O, please spare me.

paragraphs.text: Nature of elephants: Fools can be divided into several groups: “absolute fool”, “ignorant fool”, “blatant fool”, “solid fool”, “elephant-fool” (hastimúrkha), and some people even say “cow-fool” (go-múrkha). The word gańd́a-múrkha means someone whose foolishness has reached down to their cheeks and might come out of their mouth any moment. The solid-fool (niret́-múrkha) is one who is stock full of stupidity with no room to spare. Some people think that the elephant is a large creature but its intelligence is not comparable to its large body. That is why they call some fools hastimúrkha [fools like elephants] when their intelligence is not commensurate with their size. However this expression is not wholly correct. Certain species of elephant have lower intelligence, but not all of them are unintelligent. In fact, some have sharp intelligence. Although the elephants are descendants of ancient mammoths or aerávat, still they cannot be classified into one species at present. The African elephants are quite tall but their heads are comparatively smaller; they have less intelligence and are not amenable to human control.
summary: Nature of elephants: Fools can be divided into several groups: “absolute fool”, “ignorant fool”, “blatant fool”, “solid fool”, “elephant-fool” (hastimúrkha), and some people even say “cow-fool” (go-múrkha).
However this expression is not wholly correct.
The African elephants are quite tall but their heads are comparatively smaller; they have less intelligence and are not amenable to human control.

paragraphs.text: The branch of elephants of the indica group is smaller than African elephants, but their heads are larger. They may lack somewhat in sharpness, but they do have more or less an average intelligence. This species of elephant is found in most parts of India. Starting from West Bengal, Assam, Bhutan, and Nepal to southern Kerala are the habitats of this elephant species. They also reside in Bankura and Purulia districts of West Bengal and in Orissa. They are found in Betla sanctuary of Palamau [Jharkhand], and also reside in the Tekkari sanctuary of Kerala. At one time this elephant species was found in abundance in Karnataka; even today they are prevalent.
summary: The branch of elephants of the indica group is smaller than African elephants, but their heads are larger.
Starting from West Bengal, Assam, Bhutan, and Nepal to southern Kerala are the habitats of this elephant species.
At one time this elephant species was found in abundance in Karnataka; even today they are prevalent.

paragraphs.text: Another Indian elephant species of smaller size and of semi-gray colour is found in northern Assam, Cachar, Manipur and Tripura. They are of very sharp intelligence and are not easily amenable to human control. At one time they used to roam about in hordes in the forests of Tripura. They are not the elephants that we describe as domesticated elephants.
summary: Another Indian elephant species of smaller size and of semi-gray colour is found in northern Assam, Cachar, Manipur and Tripura.
At one time they used to roam about in hordes in the forests of Tripura.
They are not the elephants that we describe as domesticated elephants.

paragraphs.text: The third species of Indian elephant comprises the white elephants. In reality there is no such thing as a white elephant. Among the gray (ash) coloured elephants, there is a particular group of elephants whose colour is a shade whitish. They are also very limited in number. They are valued and respected as very sacred animals.
summary: The third species of Indian elephant comprises the white elephants.
Among the gray (ash) coloured elephants, there is a particular group of elephants whose colour is a shade whitish.
They are valued and respected as very sacred animals.

paragraphs.text: Bearing this in mind, would it be wise to describe someone as hastimúrkha? All animals have less intelligence than human beings. So people with lower intelligence are often described as animals. That is why some people with less intelligence are also called go-múrkha [as stupid as a cow]. ( 4 )
summary: Bearing this in mind, would it be wise to describe someone as hastimúrkha?
So people with lower intelligence are often described as animals.
That is why some people with less intelligence are also called go-múrkha [as stupid as a cow].

paragraphs.text: Some people think that the sour wood apple (kaed-bel) is a non-Indian fruit, imported from overseas. No, this is not correct. It is a local fruit belonging to a number of Southeast Asian countries. Its Latin name is Feronia elephantium or Feronia elephantinum. Some people might think, “Why is the name of an elephant associated with the fruit called kaed-bel or sour wood apple?” The general consensus of the people of Southeast Asia is that this is a favorite fruit of elephants. Elephants eat this fruit intact, and when the entire fruit comes out in its excreta, one can observe that the elephant has digested the entire core of the fruit, while from the outside it appears that the fruit is intact. That is why the object that appears outwardly intact but is inwardly hollow is called in Sanskrit Gajabhukta kapitthaka [like the hollow wood apple eaten by the elephant]. Elephants eat these fruit intact. They think that the whole fruit tastes very delicious. Elephants do not have the intelligence to realize that taste lies in the taste buds of the tongue; once the food goes past the tongue, there is no difference between sweetmeats and cow dung. In comparison to their size, elephants have low intelligence.
summary: Some people think that the sour wood apple (kaed-bel) is a non-Indian fruit, imported from overseas.

Elephants eat this fruit intact, and when the entire fruit comes out in its excreta, one can observe that the elephant has digested the entire core of the fruit, while from the outside it appears that the fruit is intact.
In comparison to their size, elephants have low intelligence.

paragraphs.text: You may be aware of the fact that among different species of elephants, the largest are the African elephants. They have a comparatively smaller head, with shorter cranium, less intelligence, and are not amenable to human control. The large Indian elephants, although physically smaller than African elephants, have a larger cranium and greater intelligence. Once, in South Asia and Tripura, the thousands of elephants that roamed about were smaller in appearance but had greater intelligence. These ash-coloured elephants sometimes vied with human beings as regards their intelligence. Out of fear of these elephants, it was impossible for trains to run at night in these regions [of Assam].
summary: You may be aware of the fact that among different species of elephants, the largest are the African elephants.
Once, in South Asia and Tripura, the thousands of elephants that roamed about were smaller in appearance but had greater intelligence.
Out of fear of these elephants, it was impossible for trains to run at night in these regions [of Assam].

paragraphs.text: Apart from this, in Burma and Shyámdesh (now called Thailand; the prince of Ráŕh, Sahasraváhu called this land Shyámdesh, since the country was a lush, deep green) there were white elephants (in reality, of whitish ash-colour) with average intelligence. Nevertheless, while elephants are physically large in appearance, in intelligence and sharpness they are not so great, although they cannot be described as stupid animals. ( 5 )
summary: Apart from this, in Burma and Shyámdesh (now called Thailand; the prince of Ráŕh, Sahasraváhu called this land Shyámdesh, since the country was a lush, deep green) there were white elephants (in reality, of whitish ash-colour) with average intelligence.
Nevertheless, while elephants are physically large in appearance, in intelligence and sharpness they are not so great, although they cannot be described as stupid animals.

paragraphs.text: Herd instinct of the elephant: Like the human being, the lion, the crow and other kinds of birds and beasts, the elephant also has a strong herd instinct. If the herd does not have an unquestioned leader, it breaks up in internal feuds and its security is affected. Hence you can see that when a crow is killed by someone or meets an unnatural death, thousands of crows gather together and raise their voices vociferously in their own language to protest against such an atrocity. At that time, even the most valiant retreat to safety. Those who are against hero worship in human society or are against showing respect to leadership, those who oppose individual superiority, should understand that if such individual recognition is accorded to an honest personality, it helps to guarantee the longevity of human society. If that recognition is misplaced, it becomes harmful. Human beings have advanced in knowledge, science and learning. Since by nature human beings are collective-living creatures, they must find out, irrespective of time and place, a true universal leader who should be given full recognition in the greater interest of collective welfare. Otherwise for the ever-feuding human society, there is no scope for optimism.
summary: Herd instinct of the elephant: Like the human being, the lion, the crow and other kinds of birds and beasts, the elephant also has a strong herd instinct.

Those who are against hero worship in human society or are against showing respect to leadership, those who oppose individual superiority, should understand that if such individual recognition is accorded to an honest personality, it helps to guarantee the longevity of human society.
Otherwise for the ever-feuding human society, there is no scope for optimism.

paragraphs.text: Yes, I was saying that elephants are herd animals. In every herd of elephants there is a leader. All other male and female elephants and their babies accept the leader without question. When this elephant leader becomes too old, physically incapable or sick, another young or capable one is chosen in its place and is given responsibility, and the old leader goes away to a lonely place.
summary: Yes, I was saying that elephants are herd animals.
All other male and female elephants and their babies accept the leader without question.

When this elephant leader becomes too old, physically incapable or sick, another young or capable one is chosen in its place and is given responsibility, and the old leader goes away to a lonely place.

paragraphs.text: From the Cretaceous to the Oligocene, Miocene and Pliocene periods, mammoths were among the great animals that appeared on earth, and were the predecessors of elephants. Leaving aside those belonging to the reptilian class, all these large animals were herd creatures. They had similarity or uniformity in one respect: their old and physically incapacitated leader used to leave the herd and go to a secluded place, very much like people of ancient times when they became superannuated. In their extreme old age, those ancient people used to leave the society and go into váńaprastha [seclusion]. Living in the forest, they would devote themselves to worship, meditation, and to writing books. They no longer had direct social commitments.
summary: From the Cretaceous to the Oligocene, Miocene and Pliocene periods, mammoths were among the great animals that appeared on earth, and were the predecessors of elephants.
In their extreme old age, those ancient people used to leave the society and go into váńaprastha [seclusion].
They no longer had direct social commitments.

paragraphs.text: At the very end of old age, when they became physically incapacitated, they turned into Bhikśus [renunciates]. They had no further social obligations or mundane responsibilities. They had nothing to do except to worship the Lord in seclusion. Those who lived in isolation in forests (váńaprastha) looked after these Bhikśus. The society directly cooperated with and helped these váńaprasthiis living in the forests, and indirectly helped those who had become Bhikśus.
summary: At the very end of old age, when they became physically incapacitated, they turned into Bhikśus [renunciates].
They had nothing to do except to worship the Lord in seclusion.
The society directly cooperated with and helped these váńaprasthiis living in the forests, and indirectly helped those who had become Bhikśus.

paragraphs.text: The malady of elephant insanity: You may have heard that sometimes elephants, particularly males, begin to lose their minds. When their heads become too heated – and especially if their tusks become too long and reach [and rub] the ground – the elephants become mad. In normal conditions, elephants never cause any harm to human beings. Wild elephants sometimes enter human settlements in search of ripe paddy or maize. Usually they come along with their families. At that time they generally remain calm. However, when they face any direct physical resistance during the collection of their food, they react and resist. Villagers often light fires in their cornfields to drive away the elephants. Elephants will then run away; they will not attack the villagers. At least, this is the experience of the villagers of Ráŕh. They do not ill-treat the elephants that are in search of ripe crops, and they do not receive any ill treatment from the elephants. I have seen simple villagers in western Ráŕh making obeisance to elephants with folded hands and praying to them.
summary: The malady of elephant insanity: You may have heard that sometimes elephants, particularly males, begin to lose their minds.
However, when they face any direct physical resistance during the collection of their food, they react and resist.
I have seen simple villagers in western Ráŕh making obeisance to elephants with folded hands and praying to them.

paragraphs.text: However, when the male elephant becomes mad, it is no longer calm and controlled. Whosoever crosses its path will be grabbed by its trunk, thrown to the ground and trampled. Occasionally in this excited state, the veins on its face burst, and lymph exudes. When this lymph is seen, one can understand that the elephant has gone mad. When it reaches such a state, it never returns to normalcy. Veterinary physicians should investigate this condition and see how they can save the elephants from this disease. ( 6 )
summary: However, when the male elephant becomes mad, it is no longer calm and controlled.
When this lymph is seen, one can understand that the elephant has gone mad.
Veterinary physicians should investigate this condition and see how they can save the elephants from this disease.

paragraphs.text: People once believed that if water fell from the star Sváti [the fifteenth of the twenty-seven zodiacal stars], pearls would be produced. Similarly, there was a belief that during the dark fortnight of the moon, if water fell from the Sváti star onto the head of an elephant, jewels (gajamáńikya or gajamoti or maoktika) would form on its head. When this jewel is produced, the elephants turn mad and finally die. In reality, this elephant jewel or gajamoti is something else. Compared to other animals, elephants develop more tumors (arbud) on their head. If any one of these tumors grows too large, the elephant becomes mad and eventually dies. These tumors sometimes become so hard that they cannot be broken or sliced. The common people call it gajamoti or elephant jewel. In English a shrub-like tamarisk is called Thuja, which in Sanskrit is called arbudágni. This shrub-like Thuja neutralizes the tumor. From the Sanskrit word arbud has come the Bengali word áb.
summary: People once believed that if water fell from the star Sváti [the fifteenth of the twenty-seven zodiacal stars], pearls would be produced.
If any one of these tumors grows too large, the elephant becomes mad and eventually dies.
From the Sanskrit word arbud has come the Bengali word áb.

paragraphs.text: Thuja is an effective medicine in the treatment of tumors. If elephants are fed the leaves of shrubs like tamarisk on any night during the dark lunar fortnight in the month of Fálgun, Caetra or Vaeshákh [the last two months and first month of the Bengali calendar], they can be cured of this mental malady. Hence you should understand what this term gajamoti means. Whether it be from the growth of a tumor that impairs the brain of the elephant, or whether it be from the rupturing of its [facial] veins due to the scorching heat of the sun, this state of madness is known as gajamoti. And the oozing from the ruptured veins is called gajadána. ( 7 )
summary: Thuja is an effective medicine in the treatment of tumors.
Hence you should understand what this term gajamoti means.
And the oozing from the ruptured veins is called gajadána.

paragraphs.text: Ivory work: In ancient times, people thought that the diamond was the hardest substance on earth and that the elephant tusk was the next hardest. People of those days had the impression that diamonds and elephant tusks could not be broken; they were to be cut with a small hand saw. As ivory and diamond craftsmanship developed, it became necessary to cut both the diamond and elephant tusk. The need for cutting diamonds arose because diamond pieces of different sizes had to be fitted into various settings while making bejeweled ornaments, especially finger rings. The diamond had to be cut according to the size required by the setting. Thus diamond-studded jewelry and diamond-studded rings came into being.
summary: Ivory work: In ancient times, people thought that the diamond was the hardest substance on earth and that the elephant tusk was the next hardest.
The need for cutting diamonds arose because diamond pieces of different sizes had to be fitted into various settings while making bejeweled ornaments, especially finger rings.
Thus diamond-studded jewelry and diamond-studded rings came into being.

paragraphs.text: The brilliance of the diamond depends upon the skill in the cutting. Due to this technique, if even a small amount of light shines on a piece of diamond, it is reflected in myriad directions and illuminates the surroundings. Diamond glitters in shimmering light or even in near darkness solely due to the quality of its cutting. In this respect, the jewellers of the Netherlands (formerly Holland, with its capital in The Hague, and presently known as the Netherlands with its capital in Amsterdam) has earned the highest renown in terms of diamond cutting proficiency. There was a time when jewelry traders used to have costly pieces of diamond cut in Holland. Nowadays diamond cutting industries of reasonable quality have arisen in almost all countries of the world. In India the diamond craft was first developed in Mumbai. The people living in the region between Howrah and Amta, especially those living in areas adjacent to Makardaha, attained excellence as diamond craftsmen. They are now the famous diamond artisans in the market of Mumbai.
summary: The brilliance of the diamond depends upon the skill in the cutting.
There was a time when jewelry traders used to have costly pieces of diamond cut in Holland.
They are now the famous diamond artisans in the market of Mumbai.

paragraphs.text: Cutting the elephant tusk is also a job requiring expertise and experience. At one time, the artisans of Bankura district developed expertise in this craft. Generally those who preoccupied themselves with terracotta art had relatives or friends who were engaged in this art. In different regions of Ráŕh, in Birbhum, Dumka, Manbhum and Singbhum districts, where there is terracotta artwork on the temples, most of the artisans who created these hailed from Bankura district. In the beginning, when the ivory craftsmen from Bankura district, Murshidabad and Dacca district won celebrity and recognition, those artists were mostly from Bankura. The ivory work of Dacca is no more. I have not inquired about the artists of Bankura. But if we made inquiries about the limited number of artists still living in Murshidabad, we could ascertain whether their predecessors belonged to Bankura. Although the art of ivory craftsmanship became popular during the middle of the Moghul period, it is a very ancient art. During the Buddhist era this craft was in vogue. The dancers of that age wore ivory rings set with diamonds.
summary: Cutting the elephant tusk is also a job requiring expertise and experience.
The ivory work of Dacca is no more.
The dancers of that age wore ivory rings set with diamonds.

paragraphs.text: Elephants never use their two tusks for chewing. Nowadays the tusks could be described as show pieces on the male elephants. But in ancient times, when mammoths, the ancestors of elephants, roamed on earth, their tusks were often used as weapons rather than ornaments. They used their tusks to pierce through the stomach of enemies and to level the ground in order to make a comfortable resting place. With the help of their tusks they would dig up the earth and gather it so as to create comfortable cushions for themselves.
summary: Elephants never use their two tusks for chewing.
But in ancient times, when mammoths, the ancestors of elephants, roamed on earth, their tusks were often used as weapons rather than ornaments.
With the help of their tusks they would dig up the earth and gather it so as to create comfortable cushions for themselves.

paragraphs.text: Human beings had probably not appeared on the earth at that time. Even if humans had existed, they would have been less intelligent. Initially, they did not make use of ivory for their own benefit. When they did discover its utility, they saw that it was not only decorative but also very hard and durable. Thus they utilized it to manufacture various kinds of ornaments and merchandise. When it became a manufactured product, it became known as “ivory” instead of “tusk”. In Bengali, of course, the use of the word gajadanta continued. During the Moghul period, ivory craftsmanship enjoyed the patronage of Nawabs, their peers and lords, and the leading zamindars. ( 8 )
summary: Human beings had probably not appeared on the earth at that time.
Thus they utilized it to manufacture various kinds of ornaments and merchandise.
During the Moghul period, ivory craftsmanship enjoyed the patronage of Nawabs, their peers and lords, and the leading zamindars.

paragraphs.text: The circle of elephant guards (Gajamańd́aliká): I have several times mentioned earlier that, like humans, elephants are social animals (they have herd instinct). The greatest enemy of the elephant is the lion. The elephant prefers dense forest. It does not bother so much about whether the place is dry or wet; but it must make sure that the water of that area is not salty and that it is deep enough. The elephant is not concerned about whether it is plains or hills; but it does require a watershed nearby because the elephant habitually bathes in water and plays in it for a good while.
summary: The circle of elephant guards (Gajamańd́aliká): I have several times mentioned earlier that, like humans, elephants are social animals (they have herd instinct).
The elephant prefers dense forest.
The elephant is not concerned about whether it is plains or hills; but it does require a watershed nearby because the elephant habitually bathes in water and plays in it for a good while.

paragraphs.text: Elephants are only fond of those fruits that are intoxicating or contribute to intoxication. After eating these fruits, the elephants, in an intoxicated state, plunge into the water and remain there for quite some time. There are some red berries in Africa which are very sweet and from which sugar can be produced. Elephants are very fond of these berries. If these berries are taken in large quantity (say about five or six kilos), they produce intoxication. They may not lead to intoxication in humans, but they will produce inebriation in elephants. Be that as it may, if the areas where elephants live are dry and full of bushes, and if some tall trees are also present, then lions will also be prevalent.
summary: Elephants are only fond of those fruits that are intoxicating or contribute to intoxication.
Elephants are very fond of these berries.
Be that as it may, if the areas where elephants live are dry and full of bushes, and if some tall trees are also present, then lions will also be prevalent.

paragraphs.text: The elephant is a very powerful creature. In physical strength the tiger cannot vie with the elephant. Yet the tiger has greater courage than the elephant. If there is a fight between the tiger and the elephant, there is a likelihood that the tiger will meet its death, of which it is quite aware. The reasons that the adult tiger does not want to disturb the adult wild boar are similar to the case of the tiger and the elephant. The lion does not have all these considerations. It simply attacks the elephant; sometimes the lion dies, and sometimes the elephant. Elephants have to move about cautiously, especially at night, wherever lions are more plentiful.
summary: The elephant is a very powerful creature.
The reasons that the adult tiger does not want to disturb the adult wild boar are similar to the case of the tiger and the elephant.
Elephants have to move about cautiously, especially at night, wherever lions are more plentiful.

paragraphs.text: In intelligence the elephant is inferior to the lion. In our Ananda Nagar area, there were once three different kinds of creatures – elephants, lions and tigers. Tigers became extinct there nearly fifty years ago, the Ráŕhii lions about ninety years ago, and the elephants have moved miles away into the distant forest. In the late autumn, they often come across again, sensing the smell of the ripe harvest.
summary: In intelligence the elephant is inferior to the lion.
Tigers became extinct there nearly fifty years ago, the Ráŕhii lions about ninety years ago, and the elephants have moved miles away into the distant forest.
In the late autumn, they often come across again, sensing the smell of the ripe harvest.

paragraphs.text: In the lion-infested areas, elephants keep their females and young ones in an encircled area at night. The female elephants sleep peacefully with their cubs while the male elephants stand guard around them in a circle. Finding so many elephants together keeping guard on their herd, lions will not venture in that direction. This circle of elephant guards is known as gajamańd́aliká. Since the elephant has a herd instinct, it creates this circle of protection. Now you understand what gajamańd́aliká means. ( 9 )
summary: In the lion-infested areas, elephants keep their females and young ones in an encircled area at night.
This circle of elephant guards is known as gajamańd́aliká.
Now you understand what gajamańd́aliká means.

paragraphs.text: Auspicious elephants: At midnight, a sweet fragrance comes forth from the body of noble, well-developed elephants. If there is a mild breeze, this scent lingers for a long time; otherwise it remains for about an hour. Usually these elephants are mild-natured and dutiful, and their intelligence is sharp. Once they identify their enemies, they take severe steps against them. Otherwise, they are merry, large-hearted and sportive. These easily domesticated, large elephants are called gandhagaja. In ancient times, the kings used these elephants for their pleasure trips, but never on the battle field. ( 10 )
summary: Auspicious elephants: At midnight, a sweet fragrance comes forth from the body of noble, well-developed elephants.
Once they identify their enemies, they take severe steps against them.
In ancient times, the kings used these elephants for their pleasure trips, but never on the battle field.

paragraphs.text: Rhinoceros: The rhinoceros (gańd́ar) is an animal from ancient times that is dying out but somehow still survives. Amongst the living animals on the earth today, it has the thickest and roughest skin. It is called gańd́ar because of its rough skin. This ancient creature may not be a contemporary of the dinosaur or brontosaurus, but it appeared on earth some time before the Pliocene Age. The rhinoceros of ancient times was very large in shape and appearance, and had two horns. Due to its horns, it is also called shruṋgiká [horned creature]. You would know better that our familiar, two-horned scaleless fish (siuṋgi mách) has a better name, shruṋgiká. (The other name of mágur or catfish is mudgara fish.) Among those known as shruṋgiká, the rhinoceros is the largest.
summary: Rhinoceros: The rhinoceros (gańd́ar) is an animal from ancient times that is dying out but somehow still survives.
The rhinoceros of ancient times was very large in shape and appearance, and had two horns.
) Among those known as shruṋgiká, the rhinoceros is the largest.

paragraphs.text: At one time the northern and eastern regions of India, which are mostly rainswept, provided a habitat for the rhinoceros. In most parts of Bengal the rhinoceros used to move about, if not in hundreds of thousands, then at least in the thousands. In ancient times there might have been various rhinoceros species; but today it is confined to three species; the one-horned rhino, the two-horned rhino and the small-sized rhino. The one-horned rhino and two-horned rhino dwelt in Assam, North Bengal and the Terai areas of Nepal (in Madhya Desh or Madesh); even today some of them can be seen there. In the Dooars (Himalayan foothills) areas of Jalpaiguri, when humans had not yet settled down, a huge number of rhinos were found, especially in the Hashimara region.
summary: At one time the northern and eastern regions of India, which are mostly rainswept, provided a habitat for the rhinoceros.
In ancient times there might have been various rhinoceros species; but today it is confined to three species; the one-horned rhino, the two-horned rhino and the small-sized rhino.
In the Dooars (Himalayan foothills) areas of Jalpaiguri, when humans had not yet settled down, a huge number of rhinos were found, especially in the Hashimara region.

paragraphs.text: The maximum number of rhinoceros was found in Jalpaiguri. Aside from this, one could find them in northeast Rangpur and in Rangpur. Of course, in the Nilfamari region of Rangpur district [now in Bangladesh], about 125 years ago there were plenty of rhinos – both the single-horned and double-horned varieties. Not only in North Bengal, in the Sahebganj district of Rárh, in Birbhum district, and in the Rajmahal hills of Dumka district, in the dense jungle of sábui grass about 150 years ago, herds of rhinoceros used to roam. Along with the rhinos, numerous large pythons and countless myna birds abounded.
summary: The maximum number of rhinoceros was found in Jalpaiguri.
Of course, in the Nilfamari region of Rangpur district [now in Bangladesh], about 125 years ago there were plenty of rhinos – both the single-horned and double-horned varieties.
Along with the rhinos, numerous large pythons and countless myna birds abounded.

paragraphs.text: Where have those rhinos, big pythons and mynas gone? People must have killed the pythons and used their fat to adulterate clarified butter. Relentlessly trapping the mynas and putting them in cages, people have thwarted their breeding and growth. Slaughtering rhinos, people have eaten the tender meat concealed under the cover of their hard, thick hide. Although the rhino is a powerful animal, its eyesight is very poor. Hence, it is easy to kill this animal. Although it looks ferocious, it is a feeble-minded creature. It loves the young, especially human children. Yet due to its ferocious appearance, humans have needlessly feared it and have killed it. About a century ago there were small-sized rhinos in the Sundarbans. Humans have annihilated them so as to eat their meat. The kayasthas of aristocratic families considered it a privilege to offer the meat of rhinos to their guests.
summary: Where have those rhinos, big pythons and mynas gone?
Although it looks ferocious, it is a feeble-minded creature.
The kayasthas of aristocratic families considered it a privilege to offer the meat of rhinos to their guests.

paragraphs.text: Acarya P.C. Roy in his autobiography has mentioned that his [estate] subjects used to offer him rhino meat. The ancestral home of the Roys was in the Raruli-Katipara village in the Paikgachia police station area of Khulna district in the Sunderbans. People have the wrong notion that the horn of the rhino has the power to cure impotency. Even today, due to this misplaced idea, humans kill rhinos. The number of rhinos has declined drastically and reached very low numbers in northern Bengal, Assam and Nepal. One can surmise that their total number is only about three hundred. Half of them are in Assam, one-fourth are in the Terai areas of Nepal, and one-fourth remain in Bhutan and Jalpaiguri.
summary: Roy in his autobiography has mentioned that his [estate] subjects used to offer him rhino meat.
Even today, due to this misplaced idea, humans kill rhinos.
Half of them are in Assam, one-fourth are in the Terai areas of Nepal, and one-fourth remain in Bhutan and Jalpaiguri.

paragraphs.text: In the Madarihat police-station area adjoining Bhutan in Jalpaiguri, there were once so many rhinos that agriculture became almost impossible there. If one says there are about one hundred rhinos in Bengal today, it can be considered a good estimate, since outside Garumara and Jaldapara (North Bengal), how many of them would you come across?
summary: In the Madarihat police-station area adjoining Bhutan in Jalpaiguri, there were once so many rhinos that agriculture became almost impossible there.
If one says there are about one hundred rhinos in Bengal today, it can be considered a good estimate, since outside Garumara and Jaldapara (North Bengal), how many of them would you come across?

paragraphs.text: In ancient times there was a concentration of rhinos in Bengal, since they preferred rain-washed wetlands. They are also fond of bushes and thorny shrubs. As Bengal has such a climate, they were very fond of this region. Both one-horned and two-horned rhinos lived in Bengal. In the Sundarbans there were one-horned, small-sized rhinos that could move faster than other rhinos. Their favourite food was grass, Hintal trees (Hetál – a forest plant) and Gille plants [Bahunia acuminata]. The long collarless shirts of the babus of those days were pressed and creased using the seeds of the Gille trees.
summary: In ancient times there was a concentration of rhinos in Bengal, since they preferred rain-washed wetlands.
Both one-horned and two-horned rhinos lived in Bengal.
The long collarless shirts of the babus of those days were pressed and creased using the seeds of the Gille trees.

paragraphs.text: The skin of the rhinoceros is very hard and thick; but its meat is not stiff. Rather, it is very similar to that of pigs or boars. It was nearly a century ago that, because of human tyranny, the rhinos of the Sundarbans became extinct.
summary: The skin of the rhinoceros is very hard and thick; but its meat is not stiff.
Rather, it is very similar to that of pigs or boars.
It was nearly a century ago that, because of human tyranny, the rhinos of the Sundarbans became extinct.

paragraphs.text: As mentioned earlier, in those days the meat of the rhinos was a rare delicacy for upper-caste Hindus. Due to their omnivorous greed, the rhinos of South Bengal have become extinct.
summary: As mentioned earlier, in those days the meat of the rhinos was a rare delicacy for upper-caste Hindus.
Due to their omnivorous greed, the rhinos of South Bengal have become extinct.

paragraphs.text: In all the forests of Ráŕh, there lived large-sized, extremely powerful rhinos. While on the one hand, the extension of human settlements and deforestation resulted in scarcity of rainfall, on the other hand, due to displacement, elephants, pythons, rhinos and mynas were all banished from these jungles. However, more than their banishment, the rhinos were victims of upper class peopleʼs hunger for their meat. In the land of Ráŕh today, not even a single rhinoceros can be found. The presence of rhinos in Ráŕh, as I mentioned, does not date back many years. You need go back merely 200 years. Even 150 years ago in the Borio, Barhet, Rajmahal and Tinpahar regions of Sahebganj district, there was a good concentration of rhinos. Today their place is in the museum.
summary: In all the forests of Ráŕh, there lived large-sized, extremely powerful rhinos.
The presence of rhinos in Ráŕh, as I mentioned, does not date back many years.
Today their place is in the museum.

paragraphs.text: In ancient times, just as shields were made from the hide of rhinos, weapons and utensils for worship were made from their horns. People had the notion that when rhino horn is rubbed on stone, the paste produced therefrom is used as a medicine for impotency. Spurred by this notion, many poachers kill rhinos even today. Authorities of rhino sanctuaries face great hardship as a result. With the exception of the Kaziranga sanctuaries of Assam, and Jaldapara and Burimara in Bengal, there is hardly a single rhino to be found anywhere in India. Even the few rhinos that remain in the forests of Assam and West Bengal are counting the days until their extinction. There still remain a few rhinos in the Dooars area of Nepal adjoining West Bengal. Thus there are no rhinos today in Asia except a very limited number in India and Nepal. In Africa also, the footprints of the rhino are fast disappearing. ( 1 )
summary: In ancient times, just as shields were made from the hide of rhinos, weapons and utensils for worship were made from their horns.
With the exception of the Kaziranga sanctuaries of Assam, and Jaldapara and Burimara in Bengal, there is hardly a single rhino to be found anywhere in India.
In Africa also, the footprints of the rhino are fast disappearing.

paragraphs.text: Etymologically the word kit́i means one who provokes fear in others while walking on the path. The sight of a prowling wild boar evokes a feeling of fear in a person. It is just possible that the wild boar in that case did not have any intention to attack or even to frighten the person concerned. It was just roaming about as per its own sweet will.
summary: Etymologically the word kit́i means one who provokes fear in others while walking on the path.
It is just possible that the wild boar in that case did not have any intention to attack or even to frighten the person concerned.
It was just roaming about as per its own sweet will.

paragraphs.text: Suppose a rhinoceros is simply enjoying itself by wallowing in mud and slime – in eating mud and chewing grass. Even then a person can feel frightened, and in fact people do get frightened. In common usage, a wild boar is therefore called a kit́i.
summary: Suppose a rhinoceros is simply enjoying itself by wallowing in mud and slime – in eating mud and chewing grass.
Even then a person can feel frightened, and in fact people do get frightened.
In common usage, a wild boar is therefore called a kit́i.

paragraphs.text: Both kinds of rhinoceros – one with one horn and the other two horns – are called kit́i. You surely know that a rhino is one of those prehistoric animals, which, although on the verge of extinction, somehow still survives. It is believed that the prehistoric rhino was one and half sizes larger than the present ones. Although there is no definite proof, it can be said on the basis of certain strong inferences that the ancestors of the present rhinos had several horns on the upper part of the body. Those horns were also stronger than the horns of todayʼs rhinos. The present day rhinos have very weak vision. It is not easy to know the quality of vision of ancient rhinos. Prehistoric rhinos have evolved into the one-horned rhino, two-horned rhino, wild boar and common hog of our time.
summary: Both kinds of rhinoceros – one with one horn and the other two horns – are called kit́i.
Those horns were also stronger than the horns of todayʼs rhinos.
Prehistoric rhinos have evolved into the one-horned rhino, two-horned rhino, wild boar and common hog of our time.

paragraphs.text: There are two major differences between a rhino and a member of the hog family (shúkaravarga):
summary: There are two major differences between a rhino and a member of the hog family (shúkaravarga):

paragraphs.text: 1. The skin of a rhino is harder, thicker and more impenetrable than that of any other animal. The skin of the hog family, on the other hand, is very thin. It is quite unimaginable that a ferocious animal like the wild boar could have such soft skin. I have seen communities in the Ranchi region boiling a wild boar along with its skin. They told me, “Sir, after boiling, you can simply rub off the skin.” It is due to this meager hide that the hog does not serve any commercial purpose. In ancient times items like brushes were made from the hair of particular parts of the hogʼs body. With the invention of plastic in modern times, that need no longer exists. The invincible skin of a rhino was used as a shield in olden times. Now the use of the shield in fighting is on the wane. Rhinos have also become scarce.
summary: The skin of a rhino is harder, thicker and more impenetrable than that of any other animal.
” It is due to this meager hide that the hog does not serve any commercial purpose.
Rhinos have also become scarce.

paragraphs.text: 2. Another difference between a rhino and members of the hog family is that the later avoid water and are dirty by nature. But a rhino loves water and is much cleaner than a hog. Apart from this, there are certain minor differences as well. A rhino has weak vision, while the vision of a hog is by and large quite good. A domesticated hog is a pusillanimous animal, while a wild boar is very brave and obstinate. A rhino is brave but not obstinate; it is rather jolly in temperament. So much so that even in its wild state, it is not a natural enemy of anyone.
summary: Another difference between a rhino and members of the hog family is that the later avoid water and are dirty by nature.
A rhino has weak vision, while the vision of a hog is by and large quite good.
So much so that even in its wild state, it is not a natural enemy of anyone.

paragraphs.text: Domesticated hogs are generally vegetarian, but they have no objection to eating very hideous and dirty items. Wild boars are sometimes vegetarian, sometimes carnivorous, according to the situation. However, the wild boar is a very favorite food of tigers, and tigers frequent the Sundarbans where antelopes and wild boars abound. Even then, there remains some kind of long and distant familiarity between the tiger and the wild boar. An adult wild boar avoids the adult tiger. An adult wild boar kills the tiger cub and eats its flesh. And an adult tiger kills the wild boar that is yet to come of age and eats its flesh. The flesh of the wild boar is a very favourite food of the tiger.
summary: Domesticated hogs are generally vegetarian, but they have no objection to eating very hideous and dirty items.
An adult wild boar avoids the adult tiger.
The flesh of the wild boar is a very favourite food of the tiger.

paragraphs.text: Once upon a time there was a dense population of wild boars in every part of Bengal. Names like Barábanii (baráhabanii, that is, the forest inhabited by many boars), Barábhum (Baráhabhum: the capital was Baráhabázár – Bárábázár), bear evidence of this. The name of Baránagar near Kolkata, however, is of recent origin. It is said that the Portuguese used to export pork from that town. That is why the place was named Baráhanagar [Baráha means a “boar”].
summary: Once upon a time there was a dense population of wild boars in every part of Bengal.
The name of Baránagar near Kolkata, however, is of recent origin.
That is why the place was named Baráhanagar [Baráha means a “boar”].

paragraphs.text: A rhino is vegetarian by nature. It is not the enemy of any particular animal. Daunted by its hard, thick and adamantine skin, no one dares to attack it.
summary: A rhino is vegetarian by nature.
It is not the enemy of any particular animal.
Daunted by its hard, thick and adamantine skin, no one dares to attack it.

paragraphs.text: At one time there were rhino populations in various parts of India. What to speak of the prehistoric age, even just one hundred and fifty years ago, herds of rhinos used to roam in the Ráŕh region. Many rhinos lived at the foot of the Rajmahal hills, in the Birbhum district and along the South west bank of the Padma and Bhagirathii rivers. The smaller sized rhinos thrived in the Sundarbans even one hundred and fifty years ago. The flesh of the rhino was a very favourite food [a delicacy] for the Bengalis of that period. One feels quite astounded to learn or to think that human beings have killed the rhinos not only for their horns or skin but also for the flesh.
summary: At one time there were rhino populations in various parts of India.
The smaller sized rhinos thrived in the Sundarbans even one hundred and fifty years ago.
One feels quite astounded to learn or to think that human beings have killed the rhinos not only for their horns or skin but also for the flesh.

paragraphs.text: In India some rhinos still exist; they are found in the Dooars region of North Bengal and upper Assam, in the temperate plains of Bhutan and central Nepal. Everywhere they are counting the days [until their final extinction]. People of ancient times believed that medicines made from the rhinoʼs horn could rejuvenate them. Because of this wrong conception, the poaching rhinos continues to this day. The situation has come to such a pass that the few one-horned or two-horned rhinos that still remain may disappear any time from the face of the earth. Although there is a slight increase in their population in the Kaziranga Sanctuary of Assam, one rarely comes across them in ordinary forests. The medicinal property of a rhinoʼs horn neither is a verified truth nor has any scientific basis. Is it not utterly abominable to exterminate an innocent creature due to some mistaken belief about it?
summary: In India some rhinos still exist; they are found in the Dooars region of North Bengal and upper Assam, in the temperate plains of Bhutan and central Nepal.
The situation has come to such a pass that the few one-horned or two-horned rhinos that still remain may disappear any time from the face of the earth.
Is it not utterly abominable to exterminate an innocent creature due to some mistaken belief about it?

paragraphs.text: Let me mention in this connection that fossil records provide evidence that at one time rhinos thrived in coastal Orissa, Caromandel, at the foot of the Sivalik range [Himalaya], in Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, Punjab and Hariyana. Quite large-sized rhinos inhabited Bankura of Ráŕh region and Manbhum.
summary: Let me mention in this connection that fossil records provide evidence that at one time rhinos thrived in coastal Orissa, Caromandel, at the foot of the Sivalik range [Himalaya], in Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, Punjab and Hariyana.
Quite large-sized rhinos inhabited Bankura of Ráŕh region and Manbhum.

paragraphs.text: According to some, one branch of ancestors of the hog family, of the rhinos and boars, when attacked by more ferocious animals, escaped into the water, and these are now known as porpoises. Like the boars, the porpoises are also mammals. Since, strictly speaking, the porpoises were originally terrestrial animals, they cannot breathe properly under water. That is why even today they surface from time to time above the water and then again dive under.
summary: According to some, one branch of ancestors of the hog family, of the rhinos and boars, when attacked by more ferocious animals, escaped into the water, and these are now known as porpoises.
Since, strictly speaking, the porpoises were originally terrestrial animals, they cannot breathe properly under water.
That is why even today they surface from time to time above the water and then again dive under.

paragraphs.text: There are various reasons by which it can be proved and established that the porpoise is a descendant of certain prehistoric terrestrial animals. But it cannot be emphatically claimed that a porpoise is the descendant of a member of a hog family, because the members of the hog family are strongly allergic to water. The population growth rate of domesticated hogs is exceptionally high. In this regard, it exceeds any other terrestrial creature. In the insect family it is comparable only to a kit́ibha [locust].
summary: There are various reasons by which it can be proved and established that the porpoise is a descendant of certain prehistoric terrestrial animals.
The population growth rate of domesticated hogs is exceptionally high.
In the insect family it is comparable only to a kit́ibha [locust].

paragraphs.text: 3. The population growth rate of wild boars is much lower than that of domesticated hogs. The population growth of rhinos is miserably low. On the one hand a minimal increase in population and on the other the slaughtering ceremony of the human beings – the combination of the two has brought rhinos to the brink of extinction. Officially not a single rhino remains in the Ráŕh region or in the Sundarbans. In this connection, let me tell you that the horn of a rhino is nothing but a thick, solid mass of hair.
summary: The population growth rate of wild boars is much lower than that of domesticated hogs.
On the one hand a minimal increase in population and on the other the slaughtering ceremony of the human beings – the combination of the two has brought rhinos to the brink of extinction.
In this connection, let me tell you that the horn of a rhino is nothing but a thick, solid mass of hair.

paragraphs.text: 4. Rhinos like a humid tropical climate, and they live only in such regions. However, hogs are seen to survive in any climate and in any part of the world except unusually cold regions. While in Spain sitting on a hillock on the beach of the Mediterranean, I saw the wild boars of that country. Although they appeared to be like the wild boars of Bengal in every respect, I noticed a difference in complexion. The wild boars may not be declining in number as fast as the rhinos, but they are also fast heading towards extinction. From my personal experience, I know that at one time a substantial number of wild boars inhabited the River Behulá basin (Gáungur) in Burdwan district. I doubt if even a few still remain.
summary: Rhinos like a humid tropical climate, and they live only in such regions.
Although they appeared to be like the wild boars of Bengal in every respect, I noticed a difference in complexion.
I doubt if even a few still remain.

paragraphs.text: Both rhinos and wild boars are called kit́is. So in order to make a distinction between the two in ancient times, certain scholars used to describe the rhino as a big kit́i. ( 2 )
summary: Both rhinos and wild boars are called kit́is.
So in order to make a distinction between the two in ancient times, certain scholars used to describe the rhino as a big kit́i.

paragraphs.text: Antelope: The deer (hariń) and the antelope (kárśńa) are not the same creature. You have to remember that the creature known as krśńasár, mentioned in history or found in the forest, is none other than the antelope. Even sixty years ago a sizeable number of antelope used to roam in the forests of the Ráŕh region. Even fifty years ago in Jhalda, Silli and Singbhum, antelopes were found. Yet today they have certainly become extinct.
summary: Antelope: The deer (hariń) and the antelope (kárśńa) are not the same creature.
Even sixty years ago a sizeable number of antelope used to roam in the forests of the Ráŕh region.
Yet today they have certainly become extinct.

paragraphs.text: When the Aryans began wearing yajiṋopaviita [sacred thread – the symbol of their superior status during the performance of sacrificial rites] on the left shoulder during yajiṋas, they initially used the skin of the antelope. That skin identified them as performers of yajiṋa rites, who had just partaken of cooked rice-milk (charu). In that [ceremony], they did not drink wine (somarasa) or other liquor. When again they became busy in pitr yajiṋa ( 3 ) (during pitr yajiṋa they uttered the sváhá mantra, and while worshipping the gods, the svadhá mantra) they wore the antelope skin on their right shoulder. At that moment in time, this particular skin was called prácináviita. When they hung the antelope skin from the neck at other times, the skin was called nivit. Hence in the cultural history of India, the krśńasár deer had an important role to play. Out of greed for its meat and skin, humans ruthlessly slaughtered this krśńasár deer, which is why it is fast disappearing from the earth. ( 4 )
summary: When the Aryans began wearing yajiṋopaviita [sacred thread – the symbol of their superior status during the performance of sacrificial rites] on the left shoulder during yajiṋas, they initially used the skin of the antelope.
At that moment in time, this particular skin was called prácináviita.
Out of greed for its meat and skin, humans ruthlessly slaughtered this krśńasár deer, which is why it is fast disappearing from the earth.

paragraphs.text: More about antelopes: There are certain animals that do not belong to the cow or zebu species, nor do they fall into the deer family. They are creatures in between these two species; they are called antelope in English. The llama and alpaca, found outside India, and the Indian krśńasár deer, are not deer but antelope. The Sanskrit name for antelope is kárśńa. It comes from the word krśńa. Some features of the antelope or kárśńa are similar to those of the cow and some to those of the deer. Their tails, droppings, the shape of their horns, their milk and milk udders, as well as their heels are somewhat like the deer and somewhat like the cow.
summary: More about antelopes: There are certain animals that do not belong to the cow or zebu species, nor do they fall into the deer family.
The Sanskrit name for antelope is kárśńa.
Their tails, droppings, the shape of their horns, their milk and milk udders, as well as their heels are somewhat like the deer and somewhat like the cow.

paragraphs.text: One species of the antelope or kárśńa is called gabaya; in shape and appearance they are closer to the cow. They live in ample number on the banks of large rivers in northern India, in wild bamboo or in grass and reed bushes. These gabaya antelopes used to move around in herds on the sandy shores of the Ganges and the Sone. Some years back, a herd of about fifty such gabaya antelope entered the Patna airport and ransacked it. They are slightly larger in appearance than the ordinary deer. They are not lean like the deer; they are physically slightly heavier. The male species of these animals are called ghoŕpárash in Bihar; in Sanskrit they are called gabaya. The female species are called niilgái; in Sanskrit they are called gabayii. The meat of this animal of the antelope group is not at all tasty – it is rather bland. Yet greedy humans, hungry for meat, slaughter them to satisfy their hunger. Their skins fetch a good price.
summary: One species of the antelope or kárśńa is called gabaya; in shape and appearance they are closer to the cow.
They are not lean like the deer; they are physically slightly heavier.
Their skins fetch a good price.

paragraphs.text: Often large antelope herds come together to destroy crops. Since the word gái (i.e., cow) is associated with the name niilgái, some religious-minded Hindus do not like to slaughter them; they prefer to drive them away. Those greedy people who eat their meat do not call them niilgáis; to be safely outside the orbit of religious [dietary] laws; they call them niilbakris [blue-hued goats]. Whatever name you may give them, they are still the same creature. If you were ever in the rural areas of Bihar along the sandy banks of large rivers, you would surely have come across the niilgáis. ( 5 )
summary: Often large antelope herds come together to destroy crops.
Those greedy people who eat their meat do not call them niilgáis; to be safely outside the orbit of religious [dietary] laws; they call them niilbakris [blue-hued goats].
If you were ever in the rural areas of Bihar along the sandy banks of large rivers, you would surely have come across the niilgáis.

paragraphs.text: Deer and Antelope: Karńa + ań = kárńa. The etymological meaning of the word is related to the ears (auricular). Etymologically, an ear ornament is also called kárńa. In common usage kárńa means “ear ring”. Another meaning of the word kárńa is “species of antelope”. Although deer and antelope are similar, there are certain differences. For example:
summary: Deer and Antelope: Karńa + ań = kárńa.
In common usage kárńa means “ear ring”.
Although deer and antelope are similar, there are certain differences.

paragraphs.text: 1. The faeces of the deer are like pellets, like the shape of goat or sheep-droppings. The excrement of an antelope is clayish or viscid, like cow dung or the excrement of a buffalo, horse or elephant.
summary: The faeces of the deer are like pellets, like the shape of goat or sheep-droppings.
The excrement of an antelope is clayish or viscid, like cow dung or the excrement of a buffalo, horse or elephant.

paragraphs.text: 2. Generally the tail of a deer is short and tilted slightly upward. The tail of an antelope, however, hangs downward like the tail of a cow.
summary: Generally the tail of a deer is short and tilted slightly upward.
The tail of an antelope, however, hangs downward like the tail of a cow.

paragraphs.text: 3. Frequently but not always, a deer gives very little milk; in comparison the milk of an antelope is somewhat more.
summary: Frequently but not always, a deer gives very little milk; in comparison the milk of an antelope is somewhat more.

paragraphs.text: 4. In most cases, a deer has two teats, while an antelope [always] has four.
summary: In most cases, a deer has two teats, while an antelope [always] has four.

paragraphs.text: 5. A deer moves faster than an antelope. The famous krśńasár mrga [black deer] of India, which is called a deer by many, is actually an antelope. The animals residing in the Gauṋgá basin also belong to the antelope family.
summary: A deer moves faster than an antelope.
The famous krśńasár mrga [black deer] of India, which is called a deer by many, is actually an antelope.
The animals residing in the Gauṋgá basin also belong to the antelope family.

paragraphs.text: 6. The call of a deer is also different from the call of an antelope.
summary: The call of a deer is also different from the call of an antelope.

paragraphs.text: 7. The animals of the deer family are more timorous than the animals belonging to the antelope family.
summary: The animals of the deer family are more timorous than the animals belonging to the antelope family.

paragraphs.text: 8. The animals of the antelope family have more flesh.
summary: The animals of the antelope family have more flesh.

paragraphs.text: 9. When animals of the dog family or cat family get a chance to kill either a deer or an antelope, they first attack the antelope. Although the antelope fights for some time in self-defence, while a deer makes no such effort.
summary: When animals of the dog family or cat family get a chance to kill either a deer or an antelope, they first attack the antelope.
Although the antelope fights for some time in self-defence, while a deer makes no such effort.

paragraphs.text: 10. In some cases species of the antelope family surrender to domestication, while in other cases they do not; but animals of the deer family can rarely be domesticated. Quite often it has been seen that even a deer domesticated for a long time, once set free, never wants to return.
summary: In some cases species of the antelope family surrender to domestication, while in other cases they do not; but animals of the deer family can rarely be domesticated.
Quite often it has been seen that even a deer domesticated for a long time, once set free, never wants to return.

paragraphs.text: 11. Species of the deer family like to live in freedom, even if involving hardship, although not as strongly as a jackal or a zebra. But most species of the antelope accept domestication if given comfortable conditions. Of course, there are exceptions. ( 6 )
summary: Species of the deer family like to live in freedom, even if involving hardship, although not as strongly as a jackal or a zebra.
But most species of the antelope accept domestication if given comfortable conditions.
Of course, there are exceptions.

paragraphs.text: Musk deer (kasturii mrga): You all know that the kasturii mrga is a particular type of deer that lives in parts of Himachal Pradesh, some areas of Ladakh-Kashmir, parts of Tibet and some regions of the Pamir valleys, at high altitudes and in cold places. This deer species is very homely. From the navel of the male species there is a particular hormonal secretion which emits a very sweet fragrance. This becomes concentrated and hardened in their navel and spreads a sweet fragrance everywhere. In searching for the source of this fragrance, the deer dart about wildly, and after some days turn mad and meet their death. Human beings kill them in this state of madness or after their death extract that particular fragrant substance from their navels. This is known as kasturii [musk]. Due to that kasturii, this particular deer species is called kasturii mrga. The females of this species do not develop kasturiis. I came to know from a collector of kasturii that they had sometimes found kasturii even in the navels of female deer. However its quantity is very small. With regard to those people who, instead of inward quest and spiritual meditation, roam around holy places and waste their energy and money, Tantra says:
summary: Musk deer (kasturii mrga): You all know that the kasturii mrga is a particular type of deer that lives in parts of Himachal Pradesh, some areas of Ladakh-Kashmir, parts of Tibet and some regions of the Pamir valleys, at high altitudes and in cold places.
Human beings kill them in this state of madness or after their death extract that particular fragrant substance from their navels.
However its quantity is very small.

paragraphs.text: Idaḿ tiirthaḿ idaḿ tiirthaḿ bhramanti támasáh janáh,
summary: Idaḿ tiirthaḿ idaḿ tiirthaḿ bhramanti támasáh janáh,

summary: Átmatiirthaḿ na jánanti kathaḿ mokśa varánane.

paragraphs.text: [Here is one place of pilgrimage, there is another place. People of static nature wander from one place to another place. Yet without finding the real place of pilgrimage within themselves, how can they attain salvation?]
summary: [Here is one place of pilgrimage, there is another place.
People of static nature wander from one place to another place.
Yet without finding the real place of pilgrimage within themselves, how can they attain salvation?

paragraphs.text: Gandhe máti kasturii phire anveśań kari
summary: Gandhe máti kasturii phire anveśań kari

paragraphs.text: Jáne ná se nábhi táre suváse mátáy,
summary: Jáne ná se nábhi táre suváse mátáy,

paragraphs.text: Keno miche maris káshii gayáy
summary: Keno miche maris káshii gayáy
