summary: Se je muládháre base ache tomári káyáy.

paragraphs.text: [Rapt in fragrance, the kasturii deer moves about searching, Knowing not that its own navel maddens it with fragrance. Why do you aimlessly wander about in Káshii and Gayá, When all lies within you in the inner core of your own self.]
summary: [Rapt in fragrance, the kasturii deer moves about searching, Knowing not that its own navel maddens it with fragrance.
Why do you aimlessly wander about in Káshii and Gayá, When all lies within you in the inner core of your own self.

paragraphs.text: Yes, this kasturii mrga is not easily amenable to human control. Yet it is not true that all attempts to domesticate it fail. ( 7 )
summary: Yes, this kasturii mrga is not easily amenable to human control.
Yet it is not true that all attempts to domesticate it fail.

paragraphs.text: Sundarbans deer (kákara deer): The word kákara has come from the Sanskrit word kokad́. One meaning of kokad́ is the medium-sized deer of slightly red colour of the forests in wet and salty regions. The kákara deer of the Sundarbans belongs to this group. Due to its cry that sounds like kákar … kákar … in Bengali, it is called kákar hariń [kákara deer]. The máyá hariń of the Sundarbans is not a different species of deer. It is the female gender of this kákara-deer. It looks slightly different from its male counterpart. In using the expression meye hariń [female deer] in ancient Bengali, they often used the expression máiyá hariń. This very expression has turned into máyá hariń [legendary deer]. People of ancient Bengal never consciously slaughtered the female deer. Even in the case of ritual sacrifice, it was not the custom to slaughter the female deer. Probably for this very reason, the people of the Sundarbans in those days did not kill the máyá hariń [female deer].
summary: Sundarbans deer (kákara deer): The word kákara has come from the Sanskrit word kokad́.
It looks slightly different from its male counterpart.
Probably for this very reason, the people of the Sundarbans in those days did not kill the máyá hariń [female deer].

paragraphs.text: Goat-like deer (chágal pani): One of the meanings of kokad́ is “very small sized deer”, resembling a goat in appearance. They prefer to live in sparse forests. By nature and temperament they are very quiet and timid. They run away at the sight of humans even from a distance. There was a time when lakhs [hundreds of thousands] of these deer used to roam all over India, as did the krśńasár deer. A few years ago, because of human short-sightedness, the krśńasár deer was on the verge of extinction, but given some recent safeguards, their numbers are now rapidly increasing. Yet for the small-sized deer (kokad́), no such magic wand has been offered for their survival. For this reason they are about to become extinct. Only a limited number can be found in the forests of Assam, and a very few in the Dalma hills and adjoining areas in western Ráŕh. In the Assam region they are called chágalpani, in Rárhii Bengali they are described as mrgii. Due to their sentient nature, people generally look upon them as sacred creatures, which one should neither slaughter nor allow to be slaughtered. Yet, sinful humans are continuing to kill them surreptitiously, and this innocent creature is forced to face the critical question of survival. ( 8 )
summary: Goat-like deer (chágal pani): One of the meanings of kokad́ is “very small sized deer”, resembling a goat in appearance.
Yet for the small-sized deer (kokad́), no such magic wand has been offered for their survival.
Yet, sinful humans are continuing to kill them surreptitiously, and this innocent creature is forced to face the critical question of survival.

paragraphs.text: Bison or wild buffalo: In the ancient world wild buffaloes (mahiś) ranged wherever there were forests of tall, wild grass. In todayʼs world, bison are chiefly concentrated in the northern part of America where there are forests of tall grass. The number of bison is rapidly dwindling in other countries of the world. In those areas of Ráŕh where the rhinoceros once lived, and beside large lake areas called baŕa [big] Hizal and chot́a [small] Hizal in Murshidabad district (West Bengal), huge numbers of wild buffalo once roamed. They do not look like domesticated buffaloes. Their mouth is a little lower than that of domesticated buffalo. Their horns are bigger and very strong. Their back is somewhat elevated. Their forelegs are comparatively smaller than the hind legs. Domesticated buffaloes cannot run fast and hence they yield plenty of milk; wild buffaloes run very fast and hence give less milk. Domesticated buffaloes rarely get angry, but wild buffaloes are angry nearly all of the time. Once in Birbhum, some parts of Murshidabad, Sahebganj, Rajmahal and Gadda, there were vast stretches of wild jungle grass called sábui. People used to prepare ropes, sleeping cots, swings, slippers, and so forth out of this sábui grass. Today good quality paper can be made from this grass. At one time wild buffalo used to roam the bushes of this grass in Ráŕh. I have already said that the number of wild buffaloes is rapidly diminishing. There is no such buffalo in Ráŕh now. ( 9 )
summary: Bison or wild buffalo: In the ancient world wild buffaloes (mahiś) ranged wherever there were forests of tall, wild grass.
Their forelegs are comparatively smaller than the hind legs.
There is no such buffalo in Ráŕh now.

paragraphs.text: Kangaroo: There are differences with regard to self-confidence between humans and animals. Just as all humans are not equally self-confident, similarly amongst animals and birds the degree of self-confidence is not the same. Suppose a particular person says that they will surely perform a particular task. Another person then comes and discourages and threatens that person. The person loses their self-confidence and gives up. Yet there are other people who, after declaring their intentions and determination, will not bother about other peopleʼs discouragement and threats of obstruction. However, in the event of severe stress and torture, they break down internally. There are still other people, however, who believe in “do or die” and continue with this kind of firm determination. One must understand that their determination and self-confidence are as hard as kaśt́ipáthar [a hard stone]. They emerge victorious and give inspiration and momentum for others to work alongside them on the path of advancement. They not only lay down the foundation for humanity but also help in tirelessly building up the edifice of human wisdom with all their heart and soul. They are the symbols of the human soul, and the vanguard and pioneers of human existence.
summary: Kangaroo: There are differences with regard to self-confidence between humans and animals.
However, in the event of severe stress and torture, they break down internally.
They are the symbols of the human soul, and the vanguard and pioneers of human existence.

paragraphs.text: Yes, I was saying that the intensity of self-confidence is not equal in all creatures. There can be no comparison between the intensity of self-confidence of a lion and a jackal. The kangaroo is an ordinary creature. At one time, the kangaroo used to live throughout Southeast Asia. Today, the heartless human beings have slaughtered them mercilessly and reduced their habitation to only Australia. Yet by general assessment, they have greater self-confidence than many other animals. That is why the word khalureva stands for kangaroo.
summary: Yes, I was saying that the intensity of self-confidence is not equal in all creatures.
At one time, the kangaroo used to live throughout Southeast Asia.
That is why the word khalureva stands for kangaroo.

paragraphs.text: Although the kangaroo does not run fast, it has an appreciable power to run. However, the kangaroo calf has very little power to run. In addition, it has comparatively less ability to move quickly. In ancient times, cruel people took the opportunity to kill kangaroos because of their slow speed. In those times they had less power to move than they do today. In order to survive, their speed of movement had to increase to what it is today.
summary: Although the kangaroo does not run fast, it has an appreciable power to run.
In ancient times, cruel people took the opportunity to kill kangaroos because of their slow speed.
In order to survive, their speed of movement had to increase to what it is today.

paragraphs.text: The kangaroo gives little milk. However, it has one advantage: it has a sack in its belly in which it can carry its little ones when it is on the move. The children sleep in the sack. ( 10 )
summary: The kangaroo gives little milk.
However, it has one advantage: it has a sack in its belly in which it can carry its little ones when it is on the move.
The children sleep in the sack.

paragraphs.text: Horse: There are various animals and birds with which human beings have been familiar since ancient times. Amongst them are birds such as hornbills, partridges, cocks, crows, owls and vultures; animals such as donkeys (asses, gardabha,rásabha), horses (ashva, ghot́aka, haya) and leopards (vrka vyághra). Cows came in contact with human beings much later. On the other hand, sheep and goats came under human control much earlier.
summary: Horse: There are various animals and birds with which human beings have been familiar since ancient times.
Cows came in contact with human beings much later.
On the other hand, sheep and goats came under human control much earlier.

paragraphs.text: Compared to the present, people of those days were more simple and theistic. There were constant battles among them. In the beginning their armies comprised (1) infantry, (2) cavalry or charioteers, and (3) soldiers on litters. Later, with the addition of elephants, they became four-limbed. Some people only recognized the charioteers and the cavalry and not the litter borne soldiers.
summary: Compared to the present, people of those days were more simple and theistic.
In the beginning their armies comprised (1) infantry, (2) cavalry or charioteers, and (3) soldiers on litters.
Some people only recognized the charioteers and the cavalry and not the litter borne soldiers.

paragraphs.text: Some time later, as men adopted newer techniques in their struggle for life, they made use of greater intelligence in devising battle strategies. Near the beginning of civilization, people found it necessary to tame horses for use in the battlefield; for similar reasons, elephants were also tamed.
summary: Some time later, as men adopted newer techniques in their struggle for life, they made use of greater intelligence in devising battle strategies.
Near the beginning of civilization, people found it necessary to tame horses for use in the battlefield; for similar reasons, elephants were also tamed.

paragraphs.text: To obtain horse fodder, people had to cultivate gram. In present day Hindustani it is called cáná, in Urdu and Bengali cholá. No military or battle connotation can be derived from the word háti (elephant). Háti and kari are the two specific words for elephants, and are related to the shuńd́a or trunk. The word gaja, of course, has a military connotation.
summary: To obtain horse fodder, people had to cultivate gram.
No military or battle connotation can be derived from the word háti (elephant).
The word gaja, of course, has a military connotation.

paragraphs.text: In those days, in the Pamir valley of Central Asia, hordes of wild horses used to roam... maybe some of them still do. As they can endure both heat and cold, those horses were very much in demand then, and even now they are. They are also in demand for their swift motion. Although donkeys are amenable to control, like horses, they have two great drawbacks. One is their slow movement. The other is their loud braying, which can be heard from afar, and which alerts the enemies.
summary: In those days, in the Pamir valley of Central Asia, hordes of wild horses used to roam...
They are also in demand for their swift motion.
The other is their loud braying, which can be heard from afar, and which alerts the enemies.

paragraphs.text: Although most countries of the world have horses, and those countries have differences in their climate and environment, horses belonged in the beginning to the same species – mostly residing in central Asia. On the other side of the Atlantic, in Máyá Dviipa [America] there were no horses in ancient times, as was also the case in Australia. Today, however, horses have spread all over the world. Of course, certain environmental changes have affected them. The Burmese pony has remained outside these main groups [of horses]. We call it t́át́t́u in Bengali. Earlier the pony was not recognized as a horse . . . it was considered a different animal species. During the last three hundred years it was recognized as a horse. In Bengali, instead of ghoŕá [horse], it is presently called t́át́t́u ghoŕá [pony].
summary: Although most countries of the world have horses, and those countries have differences in their climate and environment, horses belonged in the beginning to the same species – mostly residing in central Asia.
We call it t́át́t́u in Bengali.
In Bengali, instead of ghoŕá [horse], it is presently called t́át́t́u ghoŕá [pony].

paragraphs.text: Let us now come back to the original discussion. People learned that horses, when properly trained, become very useful. As a means of recreation, they give pleasure to people by participating in racing. Trained horses know how to dance and how to perform acrobatic feats. In earlier times, by giving them battle training, horses came to be called baŕaba. In this profession, male horses used to display their acumen; female horses were timid to go to the battlefield. Yet a few female horses displayed their skill in battle and were very much in demand. Male horses were called baŕaba, and female horses were called baŕabá. You should not confuse baŕabá with báŕabánal. Báŕabánal means “marine fire, fire lit by marsh gas, will-oʼ-the-wisp, the fire from carbide gas”.
summary: Let us now come back to the original discussion.
In this profession, male horses used to display their acumen; female horses were timid to go to the battlefield.
Báŕabánal means “marine fire, fire lit by marsh gas, will-oʼ-the-wisp, the fire from carbide gas”.

paragraphs.text: One other name for battle-trained horses is khet́a. In normal circumstances horses generally live about sixty years. Khet́as or war-horses live for a shorter period. This might happen to them because of their involvement in battle, and the consequent, excessive strain.

paragraphs.text: In modern warfare, the necessity for horses has nearly disappeared. Today wars are fought on trucks, motorcycles, scooters and other vehicles, aeroplanes and submarines. So there is no longer any necessity for horses or elephants in battle. In our present day life, kings and monarchs have disappeared; in their place have appeared officers of varying official rank. They find horses and elephants irrelevant to their work. Hence in different walks of life, horses and elephants are becoming obsolete, and they are being replaced by automobiles.
summary: In modern warfare, the necessity for horses has nearly disappeared.
In our present day life, kings and monarchs have disappeared; in their place have appeared officers of varying official rank.
Hence in different walks of life, horses and elephants are becoming obsolete, and they are being replaced by automobiles.

paragraphs.text: Nowhere in the world is land cultivated with the help of elephants. However, in central-eastern Asia and in certain parts of northwest India, horses were used for the cultivation of land, and it is still done in some of those regions. In Europe the soil was cultivated with the help of horses, but they are no longer considered suitable for that task today. Tractors and power tillers are replacing them. Thus horses are found unsuitable for tilling land. It is true that compared to horses and cattle, tractors are more useful and powerful, but they do not offer any fertilizer in the form of excrement. That is why chemical fertilizers have been invented. Slow-moving, horse-drawn carriages and cattle carts have been replaced by taxis and omnibuses. So like the elephants, and along with cattle and camels, horses are nowadays considered redundant; their days in our lives are numbered. Maybe in a short time children will have to visit zoos to watch them from close quarters. If there are no more horses, there will also be no need for battle horses in our lives.
summary: Nowhere in the world is land cultivated with the help of elephants.
It is true that compared to horses and cattle, tractors are more useful and powerful, but they do not offer any fertilizer in the form of excrement.
If there are no more horses, there will also be no need for battle horses in our lives.

paragraphs.text: There is no need to be sad. Synthetic milk will be produced in laboratories, and then cows will become redundant in human life. One day they will also have to take permanent leave of this dusty earth. Cows, which are of various uses to us, which are so affectionately close to us, and so very necessary to us now, will also have to disappear behind the black curtain of history.
summary: There is no need to be sad.
One day they will also have to take permanent leave of this dusty earth.
Cows, which are of various uses to us, which are so affectionately close to us, and so very necessary to us now, will also have to disappear behind the black curtain of history.

paragraphs.text: Horse meat is seldom eaten by people in modern India. In ancient times the Aryans used to eat horse meat while staying in the Middle East and in India. After slaying the horse and making an offering of its meat in the Ashvamedha Yajiṋa [ritual sacrifice], they used to eat the meat afterwards. Even now in the Middle East, horse meat is taken by some people as food.

After slaying the horse and making an offering of its meat in the Ashvamedha Yajiṋa [ritual sacrifice], they used to eat the meat afterwards.
Even now in the Middle East, horse meat is taken by some people as food.

paragraphs.text: A long time ago, in Kolkata, the palanquin bearers went on strike to raise their fares. At that time most of the palanquin bearers were Oriya people. The fare was one paisa per mile; they demanded one and a half paisa per mile. The Britishers then living in India were opposed to such a hike in fare, and instead designed a type of carriage by tying horses to palanquins. Such a palanquin carriage drawn by horses came to be known as pálki-gáŕii, juri-gáŕii, or bagi-gáŕii. The word pálki comes from the English word ‘palanquin’. The word bagi comes from the English word ‘bogey’. Ravindranath Tagore and his family members, indeed all the aristocrats of Bengal, used to go by phit́an to the gaŕer mát́h [open air Kolkata meadows] in the morning and evening to enjoy the open air.
summary: A long time ago, in Kolkata, the palanquin bearers went on strike to raise their fares.
Such a palanquin carriage drawn by horses came to be known as pálki-gáŕii, juri-gáŕii, or bagi-gáŕii.

paragraphs.text: In ancient times, any covered, one-wheeled or two-wheeled carriage drawn by one or two horses and used in war was called ratha [chariot]. The sound ra is indicative of a start or movement, and the tha is indicative of a halt. The word ratha has emerged from these sounds. In northern India the modified version of this ratha is called táuṋgá. The word táuṋgá has come from the Sanskrit word tauṋgan. In ancient times, just as human beings moved about in rathas, so also their so-called mythological gods used to go to battle in chariots. During the Buddhist era there were rathayátrá [chariot festivals] centering on gods and goddesses. Even today in different parts of India these rathajátrá festivals are held. Such festivals are very old. The medieval king of Bengal, Matsyendranath – who in later years became the great yogi Matsyendranath – went to Nepal on a ratha to dispel the prevailing drought there. This journey of Matsyendranath by ratha later turned into the rathayátrá of Lord Jagannatha. In the Buddhist age in Bengal, ratha of Dharmarájiká or Dhámrái became very famous in Dacca and Comilla district.
summary: In ancient times, any covered, one-wheeled or two-wheeled carriage drawn by one or two horses and used in war was called ratha [chariot].
During the Buddhist era there were rathayátrá [chariot festivals] centering on gods and goddesses.
In the Buddhist age in Bengal, ratha of Dharmarájiká or Dhámrái became very famous in Dacca and Comilla district.

paragraphs.text: Wild horses like the Arabian horse of the Middle East, and the Russian and European horses of the Pamir valleys, belong to one category. However, these wild horses are very difficult to control. The ponies of upper Burma can of course be more easily tamed in the wild.
summary: Wild horses like the Arabian horse of the Middle East, and the Russian and European horses of the Pamir valleys, belong to one category.
However, these wild horses are very difficult to control.
The ponies of upper Burma can of course be more easily tamed in the wild.

paragraphs.text: The Indian horse is a mixture of the Arabian and Middle Eastern breed. This horse is not as fast moving or as large as the Arabian horse, nor even as intelligent and quick as the horses of the Middle East. Yet it is relatively less hostile. ( 1 )
summary: The Indian horse is a mixture of the Arabian and Middle Eastern breed.
This horse is not as fast moving or as large as the Arabian horse, nor even as intelligent and quick as the horses of the Middle East.
Yet it is relatively less hostile.

paragraphs.text: History of the horse-drawn chariot: The chariot is one of the most ancient carriages. Donkeys, horses and cows were amongst the domesticated animals kept by human beings in the past. The characteristic feature of these animals was that donkeys were very proficient in carrying luggage, but once they were tied to carriages, their capacity for work diminished. So although there might still be carriages drawn by donkeys in some parts of the world, they are seldom popular. Although ponies are quite capable of carrying goods, they are not as efficient as donkeys; but once they are tied to carriages and fitted with blinkers, they work quite efficiently. Donkeys and cows are not restless like horses. They are not predisposed to wayward movements. So when drawing carriages, they are never made to wear blinkers. In contrast, when cows are tied to the grinding tree of an oil-mill, they feel restless after some time and try to run from one place to another. Hence when fastening them to a grinding tree, blinkers must be put on the cows. They cannot carry goods on their back and often try to shake them off. When tied to carts, they work very efficiently; but if there is mud or slush on the road, the feet of the cows become stuck. Even their heels become stuck in the sand. Because of this, cows cannot pull a carriage properly on the sand. That is why in Rajasthan and other desert areas, though carriages are drawn by cows in the towns and villages, outside the towns and villages they are drawn mostly by camels. Carriages drawn by camels used to ply the route between Burdwan and Katwa, before the narrow-gauge railway came into existence.
summary: History of the horse-drawn chariot: The chariot is one of the most ancient carriages.
In contrast, when cows are tied to the grinding tree of an oil-mill, they feel restless after some time and try to run from one place to another.
Carriages drawn by camels used to ply the route between Burdwan and Katwa, before the narrow-gauge railway came into existence.

paragraphs.text: In the more frequented areas of Bengal, on the roads and lanes, cows draw carriages quite easily; but if there is mud or slush on the road, then people are compelled to use buffaloes instead of cows. It happens on agricultural land as well. On soil that is full of mud and slush, it is easier to plough with the help of buffaloes. Cows, buffaloes and camels are large animals. Cows have greater strength than human beings. Hence, to keep them under control, ropes are inserted through their noses by piercing them (in eastern India it is called natha [controlling rope], and in northern India nákel). The Zebu indica is physically smaller in appearance and by nature quiet and calm. So there is no need to apply natha to their nose.
summary: In the more frequented areas of Bengal, on the roads and lanes, cows draw carriages quite easily; but if there is mud or slush on the road, then people are compelled to use buffaloes instead of cows.
Cows have greater strength than human beings.
So there is no need to apply natha to their nose.

paragraphs.text: On the issue of carrying goods, horses and donkeys have contrasting natures. If goods weighing double their weight are loaded onto the back of donkeys, they do not complain; but even large horses refuse to carry great quantities of luggage. On the other hand, ponies are capable of carrying sufficient goods, and they do so. Still, they are unwilling to draw carriages [though they do so if fitted with blinkers].
summary: On the issue of carrying goods, horses and donkeys have contrasting natures.
On the other hand, ponies are capable of carrying sufficient goods, and they do so.
Still, they are unwilling to draw carriages [though they do so if fitted with blinkers].

paragraphs.text: Mules are faster than donkeys but slower than horses. The mule is a hybrid animal; its mother is a female donkey and the father is a male horse. Mules are normally eunuchs. They rarely bear children.
summary: Mules are faster than donkeys but slower than horses.
Mules are normally eunuchs.
They rarely bear children.

paragraphs.text: Among the luggage-bearing animals, human beings first became acquainted with horses, next with donkeys, and then with cows and camels simultaneously. Horses yield very little milk. The mule does not yield any milk. The donkey gives a modicum of milk but that milk does not yield any butter. The milk yielded by a female donkey is very much like that of a woman. So a motherless child can be fed on the milk from the female donkey, and this is also done. Camels offer less milk than cows of better breeds, but they do yield a good quantity of milk. Of course, there is very little butter in that milk. In certain parts of India, cowʼs milk is adulterated with camel milk.
summary: Among the luggage-bearing animals, human beings first became acquainted with horses, next with donkeys, and then with cows and camels simultaneously.
The milk yielded by a female donkey is very much like that of a woman.
In certain parts of India, cowʼs milk is adulterated with camel milk.

paragraphs.text: The buffalo yields the highest quantity of milk; almost one and a half times more than a cow yields. However, for certain reasons, [many] people do not want to keep buffaloes at home. The primary reason is that buffaloes cannot be fed only grass; they must be additionally fed with other foodstuffs such as thick corn bran.
summary: The buffalo yields the highest quantity of milk; almost one and a half times more than a cow yields.
However, for certain reasons, [many] people do not want to keep buffaloes at home.
The primary reason is that buffaloes cannot be fed only grass; they must be additionally fed with other foodstuffs such as thick corn bran.

paragraphs.text: Secondly, the buffalo requires a much larger quantity of food than the cow. When it does not yield any milk, it has to be fed at considerable expense to the owner. Thirdly, the buffalo must spend quite some time during the day submerging itself in water, as otherwise its body becomes emaciated, and it begins bleeding and abruptly dies. The women of the household can milk the cows, but in the case of buffaloes, let alone the women of the household, not even all the men can milk them. For this a milkman has to be called. Human beings learned to keep buffaloes at home much later. In fact, there is something inherently wild in the buffalo.
summary: Secondly, the buffalo requires a much larger quantity of food than the cow.
The women of the household can milk the cows, but in the case of buffaloes, let alone the women of the household, not even all the men can milk them.
In fact, there is something inherently wild in the buffalo.

paragraphs.text: People first invented horse-drawn carriages; carriages drawn by cows came much later than horse-drawn carriages. In ancient times there were constant feuds between different groups of people. There was hardly a day in peopleʼs lives when group clashes did not take place. To move from home or village to the battleground, people were compelled to use horse-drawn carriages. In its earliest stage the shape of this carriage was like that of a ratha. The horse was urged to move forward with the rrr…. sound and was made to stop with the sound tha … tha …That is why the carriage came to be known as ratha. In those days, when there were no battles, just as soldiers indulged in horse racing, so also they participated in chariot racing or ratha-racing. However, those chariots were built in a lighter style and used in a specific manner. They were called krd́á-ratha [sports chariots]. In the later period, for the purpose of competition, whatever ratha, carriage or animal came to be used, they were given the common name of ‘sports carriage’ – whether it was a ratha or boat, horse or camel. ( 2 )
summary: People first invented horse-drawn carriages; carriages drawn by cows came much later than horse-drawn carriages.
The horse was urged to move forward with the rrr….

In the later period, for the purpose of competition, whatever ratha, carriage or animal came to be used, they were given the common name of ‘sports carriage’ – whether it was a ratha or boat, horse or camel.

paragraphs.text: Black horse (Kurál horse): Usually the horse does not tire easily from work. The psychology of the horse is that whenever it is on the verge of engaging in strenuous labour, it lets out a shrill cry so as to reduce the strain. When it is unable to drag its four feet, its physical exhaustion becomes quite evident. In earlier times there was a popular notion that dark-coloured horses had the greatest capacity to undertake labour. Hence they were considered to be the smartest and most agile. In Hindustani they are called chaltápurjá. So in those days the black horse fetched the highest price in the market place. On the battlefield, if at the front [line of battle], the horse rider or charioteer was found to use black horses, the white horse or horses of the rival side ran away in panic. So the enemy party, after seeing the black horse of the opposing side, often retreated from battle. Black horses had such esteem in those days.
summary: Black horse (Kurál horse): Usually the horse does not tire easily from work.
In Hindustani they are called chaltápurjá.
Black horses had such esteem in those days.

paragraphs.text: The kings and soldiers of earlier times, to camouflage their appearance, used to wear white dresses and rode on a white horse during the day time, and after sundown rode black horses and wore dark or violet-coloured dresses as they moved about.
summary: The kings and soldiers of earlier times, to camouflage their appearance, used to wear white dresses and rode on a white horse during the day time, and after sundown rode black horses and wore dark or violet-coloured dresses as they moved about.

paragraphs.text: Kura + alac (kalac) = kurála. Etymologically kurála means “a special kind of fast animal”. Colloquially kurála refers to a rare kind of horse (aśva: ash + van) which used to inhabit central Asia and northwest India in olden times. These rare horses were very expensive. They were tall and golden-coloured with totally black legs. These kurála horses are not found in todayʼs world. Nowadays they are as extinct as the dodo.
summary: Kura + alac (kalac) = kurála.
These rare horses were very expensive.
Nowadays they are as extinct as the dodo.

paragraphs.text: The kurála horse was a high-bred species. The sheen of their coat was dazzling. So the aristocratic ladies of those days used to make petticoats of the same colour. Those petticoats were very long; they used to reach to the soles of their feet. The upper part was golden and the lower part, that is, the border, was jet black.After that, in the language of those days, kurála used to mean “petticoat”. ( 4 )
summary: The kurála horse was a high-bred species.
Those petticoats were very long; they used to reach to the soles of their feet.
After that, in the language of those days, kurála used to mean “petticoat”.

paragraphs.text: Donkey: Donkeys (gádhá) have been under human control since very ancient times. Both horses and donkeys came under human control nearly 15,000 years ago. Although much is made of horses in the Vedas, there are comparatively very few references to donkeys. The reason is that at the primitive stage of human civilization, horses were the prime mounts. Donkeys are not quick moving. So as transporters, their position was far behind that of horses. They could not draw carriages as effectively as horses. However, being more docile than horses and less expensive to maintain, the donkeys and mules (father: male horse and mother: she-ass) have long been used for transporting goods.
summary: Donkey: Donkeys (gádhá) have been under human control since very ancient times.
Donkeys are not quick moving.
However, being more docile than horses and less expensive to maintain, the donkeys and mules (father: male horse and mother: she-ass) have long been used for transporting goods.

paragraphs.text: Since ancient times, the Aryans and Mongols have used horses and horse-drawn carriages on the battlefield. Since they are slow-moving, donkeys were never used in battle. Of course, the donkey is more suitable than the cow and the horse for transporting goods. In comparison to donkeys, mules can carry still more goods. But the mule is relatively rare, since it is not a natural born creature. This means that it cannot be found in the forest. For drawing carriages, donkeys are not as adept as cows, but donkeys are more efficient in carrying luggage. For this reason, when there is no need of haste or speed, donkeys have been utilized for carrying goods. Even today people do so. Almost all over India there was the practice of keeping donkeys. In parts of Gujarat, Kutch and Rajasthan, hordes of multi-coloured donkeys could be seen that were not easily amenable to control. Nevertheless, they were quite swift. That is why human beings had little interest to keep or maintain such donkeys. For some natural reasons, since the last century those multi-coloured donkeys have been on their way towards extinction. The use of donkeys for carrying goods was common in India since ancient times, and it is still practiced there. But the use of donkeys for carrying luggage and drawing carriages was not so extensive. Today it is rarely seen. Previously, however, there were carriages in India drawn by donkeys.
summary: Since ancient times, the Aryans and Mongols have used horses and horse-drawn carriages on the battlefield.
Almost all over India there was the practice of keeping donkeys.
Previously, however, there were carriages in India drawn by donkeys.

paragraphs.text: Although riding on donkeys was not socially prohibited in India, it was considered shameful. Apart from this, since donkeys are slow-moving, people could hardly save any time by riding them. That is why it was never a popular practice. Once in Ráŕh, Bengal, well-to-do families maintained horses and sheep, just as they kept cows. However, except for the washerman, no one kept donkeys.
summary: Although riding on donkeys was not socially prohibited in India, it was considered shameful.
That is why it was never a popular practice.
However, except for the washerman, no one kept donkeys.

paragraphs.text: At one time, donkeys were largely used in Persia (now Iran). Just as there were plenty of carriages drawn by donkeys there, so also human beings moved here and there on the backs of donkeys. Today in the age of rocket science one would not expect people in Iran to use donkeys for pulling carriages, although it was once a common practice to do so. ( 5 )
summary: At one time, donkeys were largely used in Persia (now Iran).
Just as there were plenty of carriages drawn by donkeys there, so also human beings moved here and there on the backs of donkeys.
Today in the age of rocket science one would not expect people in Iran to use donkeys for pulling carriages, although it was once a common practice to do so.

paragraphs.text: The bray of the donkey is very strong and strange. The original habitat of the donkey was the dry desert region of western India, Afghanistan, Baluchistan, the northern part of Russia and Persia. When they live in forests they move about in herds. The colour of their body is quite varied – red, blue, violet, yellow, brown and gray. Unlike the wild horse or the zebra, which is not amenable to human control, the donkey is different. The gray-coloured or brown-coloured donkey is readily amenable to domestication and is quite mild-natured. It carries luggage in silence; but when luggage beyond its capacity of endurance is heaped on its shoulders, it quickly sits down. Then the owner, understanding the predicament, reduces the weight of the luggage.
summary: The bray of the donkey is very strong and strange.
Unlike the wild horse or the zebra, which is not amenable to human control, the donkey is different.
Then the owner, understanding the predicament, reduces the weight of the luggage.

paragraphs.text: The colourful donkeys often refuse to be domesticated. When they see humans they run away to keep a distance. Even those who could somehow manage to be domesticated try to run away. The nutritional value of donkey milk is far less than that of the cow or the horse. It also yields less butter. Yet in qualitative terms, the milk of the donkey is as good as the milk of a woman. So for an orphaned infant, the milk of the donkey is a good alternative to motherʼs milk. In English, the slow-moving, wide-eared, braying creature is called donkey. A comparatively swifter, long-eared and less vociferous animal is called “ass” in English, in Sanskrit rásava.
summary: The colourful donkeys often refuse to be domesticated.
It also yields less butter.
A comparatively swifter, long-eared and less vociferous animal is called “ass” in English, in Sanskrit rásava.

paragraphs.text: The donkey moves very slowly; that is why, since very ancient times, human beings used to put their luggage on the back of donkeys and preferred to themselves ride horses. The offspring of a male horse and a female donkey is known as a mule (khaccar). The mule or ashvetar is more industrious and capable of carrying more luggage than the ordinary donkey.

paragraphs.text: In Persia the donkey was once very much in demand. Even highly-placed people used to ride on donkeys. It was not considered dishonourable. From ras + avac with elongated i, we get the word rásava. The word rásava means “one who works according to oneʼs whims”. Its sound, behaviour and activities work according to the drift of its individual flow, regardless of whether that pleases someone or not. The donkey has similar behaviour. That is why the donkey is also called rásava.
summary: In Persia the donkey was once very much in demand.
The word rásava means “one who works according to oneʼs whims”.
That is why the donkey is also called rásava.

paragraphs.text: Khara signifies both gardhava and rásava. Gardhava means “the long donkey which carries luggage but is somewhat disobedient”. Its brays are forceful and very repetitious. Rásavii (the female rásava or wild ass) has lesser capability of yielding milk than the donkey (domesticated ass). ( 6 )
summary: Khara signifies both gardhava and rásava.
Its brays are forceful and very repetitious.
Rásavii (the female rásava or wild ass) has lesser capability of yielding milk than the donkey (domesticated ass).

paragraphs.text: Mule: Mules have greater capacity to carry goods than donkeys. Compared to donkeys, they are swifter animals. Even in drawing carriages they are more proficient than donkeys. In physical appearance they have greater affinity to horses, but in their habits they are akin to donkeys. Since they have to make movements up and down across the fields, it is not possible for them to develop udders. Hence for this reason, amongst mules there is no gender distinction; it can be said that they are all eunuchs. Since mules have a tendency to travel uphill, they are also called khesara. From this word khesara has come the word khaccara [mule].
summary: Mule: Mules have greater capacity to carry goods than donkeys.
Since they have to make movements up and down across the fields, it is not possible for them to develop udders.
From this word khesara has come the word khaccara [mule].

paragraphs.text: Prior to independence, I saw in the Kinnar district of Himachal Pradesh, along the Indo-Tibetan road, hordes of docile-natured mules carrying on their backs different kinds of food crops, goods and yarns manufactured in factories, along with various kinds of stationery. Similarly, hordes of such mules were coming from the opposite direction, carrying on their backs precious stones and wine produced from barley. Since Tibet is now a part of China, I cannot be sure of any such goods-related traffic by mules on the Indo-Tibetan road; but when it was there, it brought the two neighbouring peoples closer together. ( 7 )

paragraphs.text: Cow: You know that when the Aryans gave up their nomadic habits and turned into cultivators, they left their old habits of moving about and settled down at one place; that was when they needed the cow (goru) very badly. Possibly for this reason, due to their excessive love for the cow, they began addressing the cow as the cow-mother. It appears that humans did not learn to keep cows at the beginning of the Vedic age; they learnt to do it at the end of the Vedic age. In that age, although they were fond of the cow, they did not treat her like a mother. They even performed Go-medh yajiṋa [ritual sacrifice of the cow].

They even performed Go-medh yajiṋa [ritual sacrifice of the cow].

paragraphs.text: There has been many a storm in the tea cup among modern pandits over the exact nature of the Go-medh yajiṋa. One group of scholars opined that, as the horse was killed and sacrificed in fire during the Ashvamedha yajiṋa [the same was the case with cows in Go-medh yajina]. Since that time the name of the fire came to be hutáshana. The word huta means “that which was sacrificed in fire”, and ashan stood for eating. Hutáshana means “that which eats up anything offered to it as a sacrifice”. Hence, in a wider sense, hutáshana means “something that accepts as food anything offered to it”. Whatever is offered to fire is accepted and consumed by it. Since fire eats up anything offered to it, another name for fire is hutáshana or hutásh. Of course, since in any yajiṋa the use of fire was essential, the other names of fire became játaveda, hutáshana, pávaka and sarvabhuka. Fire has several other names according to its uses.
summary: There has been many a storm in the tea cup among modern pandits over the exact nature of the Go-medh yajiṋa.
Hence, in a wider sense, hutáshana means “something that accepts as food anything offered to it”.
Fire has several other names according to its uses.

paragraphs.text: I have said a little earlier that those who were excessively devoted to the cow refused to believe that the cow was ever killed and sacrificed. They treated the word go as meaning the sense organs or perceptibility of sense organs. They interpreted go-medha yajiṋa as meaning to control human senses or restrain human senses… restricting or controlling one of the essential human organs, the tongue. By consumption of cow flesh they meant, “controlling of our vák,” that is, the vocal cord or speech.

paragraphs.text: The word má stands for ‘tongue’ and the word aḿsa means the sequel. So máḿsa means the sequel of ‘tongue’, that is, speech. Go means sense organ. That is why the meaning of the go-máḿsa is anything derived from our speech or the sense organ tongue. So consumption of go-máḿsa [cow flesh] is not eating the flesh of the cow; it refers to control of the expression of our vocal cord or of speech.

paragraphs.text: Whatever storms arise over the teacups of pandits or over their coffee cups, there is no need to get a headache over this. Yet it is true that in agricultural society, cows occupied an important place. That importance is related to our needs. For that reason, there should be control over cow slaughter. But that restriction shall not be regulated by any religious dogma. Those who are opposed to animal slaughter or violence to animals should be vocal against not only cow slaughter but also against slaughter of other animals like buffaloes and goats.

For that reason, there should be control over cow slaughter.
Those who are opposed to animal slaughter or violence to animals should be vocal against not only cow slaughter but also against slaughter of other animals like buffaloes and goats.

paragraphs.text: Yes, for obvious reasons, among the agriculturally dependent Aryans in ancient times, the cow was given special importance. Human beings used to compare learned and qualified people with the high-grade oxen. A big pandit was called a Pańd́itpuṋgav [“pandit-ox”]; a great hero was called a Viirapuṋgav [“hero-ox”]. ( 1 )

Human beings used to compare learned and qualified people with the high-grade oxen.
A big pandit was called a Pańd́itpuṋgav [“pandit-ox”]; a great hero was called a Viirapuṋgav [“hero-ox”].

paragraphs.text: In ancient times, in the forests of India, the cow species belonging to the zebu group, or the wild cows, were also called khalureva.
summary: In ancient times, in the forests of India, the cow species belonging to the zebu group, or the wild cows, were also called khalureva.

paragraphs.text: When they were in the wild, they had ample ability to run, just as the goat, which could also run. To save themselves from attack by ferocious animals in the forest, they needed both mobility and speed. Due to their rapid movement, their milk udders were small, very much like those of deer today, or those of antelope. With large udders, it is not possible for animals to run rapidly. We might guess that in ancient times the cow and goat gave less milk, very much like the deer and antelope of today. Even now the cow species that gives a plenteous quantity of milk is very slow moving. For any movement it takes them a long time.
summary: When they were in the wild, they had ample ability to run, just as the goat, which could also run.
With large udders, it is not possible for animals to run rapidly.
For any movement it takes them a long time.

paragraphs.text: Of course, the enhancement of their capacity to yield more milk has come as a boon to human beings. People have come to be proud of this “White Revolution”. However, if one thinks of the welfare of this animal species, it has been harmful to them. Even if the calf is allowed to drink all the milk in the udder, it would not be able to do so. And by carrying this extra quantity of milk over a long period, the [mother] cow becomes physically weak. By yielding excessive milk the buffalo does not suffer physically as much as the cow, since it is physically bulky. Still, if their production of milk is excessively increased, their health is bound to suffer, just as to overnourish one particular organ of the human body enhances its power at the cost of oneʼs general health.
summary: Of course, the enhancement of their capacity to yield more milk has come as a boon to human beings.
Even if the calf is allowed to drink all the milk in the udder, it would not be able to do so.

Still, if their production of milk is excessively increased, their health is bound to suffer, just as to overnourish one particular organ of the human body enhances its power at the cost of oneʼs general health.

paragraphs.text: Of course, today there is no alternative but to enhance the supply of cowsʼ and goatsʼ milk because of the increasing demand of human beings. I also understand fully that one day in our science laboratories synthetic payasa [milk] will be produced. (I am avoiding the use of the word dugdha for ‘milk’, which is secured by milking the cow. Since we do not get synthetic milk by milking in the laboratory, I am using the word paya or payasa). At one time the horse was used as sophisticated mounts. The importance of the horse as a domestic animal has come to an end. Similarly, with the invention of the tractor, power tiller and synthetic milk, the necessity for cows will also come to an end. You might say that for the sake of eating meat, people will have to keep cows. However, I am not thinking along those lines. I believe that, with the advancement of human intellect, emotional sensitivity and rationality, human beings will be more inclined towards Neohumanism, they will develop indifference towards eating flesh and will give up their carnivorousness. ( 2 )
summary: Of course, today there is no alternative but to enhance the supply of cowsʼ and goatsʼ milk because of the increasing demand of human beings.
The importance of the horse as a domestic animal has come to an end.

I believe that, with the advancement of human intellect, emotional sensitivity and rationality, human beings will be more inclined towards Neohumanism, they will develop indifference towards eating flesh and will give up their carnivorousness.

paragraphs.text: Milk is derived from milking the cow, camel or buffalo. According to Puranic accounts, the kapilá cows did not require any milking; once they were worshipped, milk flowed endlessly from their udders. However, in the case of the earthly cow, milking is required. Giving milk to the baby is nothing strenuous for the mother, or for any other mammal. Still, milking is always a strenuous job for all, even for the milkman. It is very difficult to milk an animal whose udder is very stiff. In the village of Burdwan I saw that women milked the cows, but for milking the buffaloes they had to call the milkman. Very often even men with fragile health are unable to milk the buffaloes.
summary: Milk is derived from milking the cow, camel or buffalo.
Still, milking is always a strenuous job for all, even for the milkman.
Very often even men with fragile health are unable to milk the buffaloes.

paragraphs.text: In ancient times when cows were not yet brought under human control or when people were not yet able to bring the cow from the wild in the forest to a domesticated condition, they had first kept horses. The horse is a swift-moving animal, and a swift animal gives less milk. So for the sake of milk, no one keeps a swift animal. In those days people did not cultivate with the help of the plough and the bull. They kept the horse to ride and to use in battle field. Ancient human beings procured food for the horse and used it as a mount. It did not serve any other purpose. Although it offered very limited service, human beings had to take the responsibility of feeding the horse. Occasionally they felt irritated, yet they could not do without the horses. They called the horse ashva (ash + bun), which means “that which works on the strength of food”. When humans came in contact with the cow, they learnt to cultivate with the help of the cow. The cow is a slow animal, for which reason she gradually came to provide more milk. After domesticating the cow, humans also learnt to milk it. It was the men who did the heavy jobs while women did the milking.
summary: In ancient times when cows were not yet brought under human control or when people were not yet able to bring the cow from the wild in the forest to a domesticated condition, they had first kept horses.
Although it offered very limited service, human beings had to take the responsibility of feeding the horse.
It was the men who did the heavy jobs while women did the milking.

paragraphs.text: The word duhitá means “the milking women”. People had not yet learnt to bring the buffalo under control; may be they had not conceived of the idea. The buffalo always seeks a wet place or a pond. The Áryanyavraja or present Iran [where Aryans first arrived in their journey towards India] is a dry and hard country. Although cultivation is marginally satisfactory, it has very little wetland. It would be relevant to point out that, although milking the buffalo is quite difficult, tending the buffalo is not at all difficult. If you put the buffalo into a wetland, it will look after itself – the whole day. Scrub it well and bathe it in water; that will be good enough. After coming in contact with the cow, people learnt almost immediately about all the qualities of milk. If there is one food which has all the good qualities of many different foods, then it must be milk.
summary: The word duhitá means “the milking women”.
It would be relevant to point out that, although milking the buffalo is quite difficult, tending the buffalo is not at all difficult.
If there is one food which has all the good qualities of many different foods, then it must be milk.

paragraphs.text: After coming in contact with cowʼs milk, people then came in contact with buffalo milk. After coming in contact with the camel and the sheep and tasting their milk, they came to learn that whatever good qualities are present in cowʼs milk, they are also present in buffalo milk, and perhaps in even greater quantity. However, the fat content in buffalo milk is around 1¼ percent to 1½ percent more than in cowʼs milk. For this reason, it is suitable only for people in the age group of 16-40, and not for young people or even for older people. In Bihar, even where buffalo milk is available in larger quantity, babies and elderly people are fed on cowʼs milk. Sheepʼs milk, in which the fat content is less, is not fully nutritious. In the milk of the camel or the goat, there is hardly any fat content, due to which it also has less nutritional value.
summary: After coming in contact with cowʼs milk, people then came in contact with buffalo milk.
For this reason, it is suitable only for people in the age group of 16-40, and not for young people or even for older people.
In the milk of the camel or the goat, there is hardly any fat content, due to which it also has less nutritional value.

paragraphs.text: The milk of the donkey is considered to be as good as [human] motherʼs milk. So for a motherless baby cowʼs milk is good, but for a baby of more than two years, it is less nutritious. The clarified butter prepared from buffalo milk (bhaesá-ghee), if taken in large quantity, can cause stomach upset or dysentery. However, the clarified butter prepared from cowʼs milk normally does not do any harm. So to prevent any constipation arising out of regular intake of sunned rice, in ancient times people used to take it with clarified butter prepared from cowʼs milk. Since milk, especially cowʼs milk, has the power to offer vitality, and in addition has healing powers, it is called gadáhva. In the grass, especially in the variety called dudhiá, the vitamin content is sufficiently adequate. Graminivorous animals acquire their vitality through this grass and thus supply ample milk. The sap of the grass prevents blood poisoning, helps mitigate the oozing of blood and helps to heal the wound. Out in the field, in the event of accidental bleeding arising from any injury, if this grass is chewed and pasted on the wound, the bleeding stops in a short while. Grass, especially the green durbá grass [Cynodon sp.], has this healing power. ( 3 )
summary: The milk of the donkey is considered to be as good as [human] motherʼs milk.
In the grass, especially in the variety called dudhiá, the vitamin content is sufficiently adequate.
], has this healing power.

paragraphs.text: Uh means the upper side. Suppose there are many cows in an area. The most gifted among them, in all respects, is called gaboh. The native cows of India (Zebu indica) are smaller in shape and give less milk; but their milk is sweet and pleasant smelling. The cows of western India are larger in size and give more milk, but their milk has hardly any sweetness or nice fragrance. By this criterion, if the best cows are chosen from amongst all those in India, they would be the patniiá cows. When compared to common, indigenous cows, they are a little larger in appearance. Indian cows have a hump on their shoulder, which European cows do not normally have. The patniiá cows also have no hump. They give more milk and by nature are calm and quiet. They truly belong to the gaboh category.
summary: Uh means the upper side.
By this criterion, if the best cows are chosen from amongst all those in India, they would be the patniiá cows.
They truly belong to the gaboh category.

paragraphs.text: Next to these, the best variety of Indian cow is the Sirhindii cows of the western part of Haryana. In this region there is an upland plateau, which is a large water barrier; the rivers and canals on its eastern side flow down and into the Bay of Bengal, and those water bodies to the west flow down into the Arabian Sea across the Sindhu River basin. As it is an upland area, it is called Sirhind or “the head of India”. The cows of Sirhind are larger in size and give more milk. They are called Sirhindii cows.
summary: Next to these, the best variety of Indian cow is the Sirhindii cows of the western part of Haryana.
As it is an upland area, it is called Sirhind or “the head of India”.
They are called Sirhindii cows.

paragraphs.text: Aside from this, in the north of Sindhu there is a semi-desert region that belonged to the former Bahawalpur Kingdom; now it is a district of the Sindh province of Pakistan. The Bahawalpur cow is rather large in size and gives more milk. (The people of Bengal wrongly call this Bahawalpuri cow as the Bhagalpuri cow.) However, the amount of butter in the milk is less than that of Sirhindii cows. There is little taste in the curd made from the milk of the Bahawalpuri cow. Still, for other milk products the Bahawalpuri cow is very profitable. Then there is the Gujarati cow of western Punjab. The cows of Gujarat district adjoining Gujranwala and Sialkot districts of Punjab [Pakistan] are of higher quality; but when they are brought to eastern India, they do not reproduce well. They lose their health because of the humid climate. In certain areas of India like Rajasthan, Gujarat and Kutch, there are some worthy local cows or gabohs.
summary: Aside from this, in the north of Sindhu there is a semi-desert region that belonged to the former Bahawalpur Kingdom; now it is a district of the Sindh province of Pakistan.
Still, for other milk products the Bahawalpuri cow is very profitable.
In certain areas of India like Rajasthan, Gujarat and Kutch, there are some worthy local cows or gabohs.

paragraphs.text: In southern India in the Krishna River basin of Andhra Pradesh, some good quality cows or gabohs are found. From their milk a high quality of butter oil is produced. The butter of their milk cannot be preserved for a long period; but the butter oil can be preserved for quite some time, like that of other cows. Once in the districts of Nadia, Bagri, Murshidabad and Malda there were some “quality” local cows, but in the absence of proper care and attention, they are now practically extinct.
summary: In southern India in the Krishna River basin of Andhra Pradesh, some good quality cows or gabohs are found.
The butter of their milk cannot be preserved for a long period; but the butter oil can be preserved for quite some time, like that of other cows.
Once in the districts of Nadia, Bagri, Murshidabad and Malda there were some “quality” local cows, but in the absence of proper care and attention, they are now practically extinct.

paragraphs.text: In the Damodar basin of Hoogly and Burdwan districts there were once some excellent Bengali cows (Indian zebu of Banjalitis breed). If proper attempts are made even today, their breed can still be saved. These cows (of the Kriśńá variety) give fragrant and tasty milk. Even today in certain villages, after a proper search one can find one or two such dark-coloured or Krśńá type cows along with their calves. ( 4 )
summary: In the Damodar basin of Hoogly and Burdwan districts there were once some excellent Bengali cows (Indian zebu of Banjalitis breed).
These cows (of the Kriśńá variety) give fragrant and tasty milk.
Even today in certain villages, after a proper search one can find one or two such dark-coloured or Krśńá type cows along with their calves.

paragraphs.text: You must have seen cows that chase people or kick them if one tries to milk them. This kind of bad-natured cow is called a márkáńd́á cow in some places. This márkáńd́á cow is called karat́a. If this márkáńd́á cow is fed fodder mixed with mustard chaff before dawn, then its affliction will be alleviated, that is, its temper will be calmed. Often this kind of cow kicks its own calf and chases it away, that is, she does not allow it to drink her milk. In order that these calves do not die for want of nourishment during infancy, they can be fed pure roasted gram flour dissolved in water; then their life can be saved. ( 5 )
summary: You must have seen cows that chase people or kick them if one tries to milk them.
If this márkáńd́á cow is fed fodder mixed with mustard chaff before dawn, then its affliction will be alleviated, that is, its temper will be calmed.
In order that these calves do not die for want of nourishment during infancy, they can be fed pure roasted gram flour dissolved in water; then their life can be saved.

paragraphs.text: Buffalo: You all know that the buffalo (mahiś) is not that civilized, domesticated or gentle a creature as the cow is. It is not even as responsible as the cow is. While drawing the carriage, it sometimes runs straight to any bog or pond it comes across, dragging the carriage along with it. If it observes that its owner is not that alert and observant, it may not return home at all. The cow is different.
summary: Buffalo: You all know that the buffalo (mahiś) is not that civilized, domesticated or gentle a creature as the cow is.
While drawing the carriage, it sometimes runs straight to any bog or pond it comes across, dragging the carriage along with it.
The cow is different.

paragraphs.text: The original owner, Rambabu, sells the cow at the cattle market to Shyambabu, who lives six kilometers away. Shyambabu brings the cow home and entertains it; the women of the house smear its horns with vermillion and worship it, feed it with mustard oil cakes, sliced paddy hay and other delicacies. However, taking advantage of the open gate due to the ownerʼs carelessness, the cow slips away and returns to the house of its original owner miles away. Many villagers are acquainted with such events. I have told you long ago about a rhyme in western khat́t́á [mixture of Bhojpuri, Magahii and some other local sub-dialect] dialect:
