paragraphs.text: The herder leads the buffaloes into the pond and plays the flute, resting in the shade of the Indian olive tree. The buffalo, on the lookout for opportunity, shakes off the water from its body, enters into the nearby forest and may never return. The domesticated buffalo, once it is away from the herd and is entering the forest, if it remains there for some days, it turns into a wild animal. This wild buffalo is called gabala. But there is a difference between this kind of wild buffalo and the wild buffalo of the forest.
summary: The herder leads the buffaloes into the pond and plays the flute, resting in the shade of the Indian olive tree.
The domesticated buffalo, once it is away from the herd and is entering the forest, if it remains there for some days, it turns into a wild animal.
But there is a difference between this kind of wild buffalo and the wild buffalo of the forest.

paragraphs.text: The wild buffalo, which is called ‘bison’ in English, has a somewhat low front and raised back. They are normally calm and quiet by nature, but become furious when angry and refuse to be domesticated. The gabalas I have spoken about are not like bison; they look like domesticated buffaloes. Indeed they are. Compared to domesticated cows, they give less milk. Their udders are dry and smaller in size. ( 6 )
summary: The wild buffalo, which is called ‘bison’ in English, has a somewhat low front and raised back.
The gabalas I have spoken about are not like bison; they look like domesticated buffaloes.
Their udders are dry and smaller in size.

paragraphs.text: Let us compare the horse, the cow, the buffalo and the mule – these four animal species. There is a difference in their nature and appearance. The horse is swift. Its cry is shrill-sounding like ci – hi – hi, chi – hi – hi, chi – hi – hi. The horse cannot carry much luggage. It has a greater capacity to pull than to carry. So instead of putting more luggage on its back, its is made to pull chariots (rathas), carriages etc. It feels uneasy if more than one person rides it. If while moving along, the horse comes across one road that goes uphill, another that goes downhill and another that goes straight on flat land, it will choose the path that goes straight ahead on flat land. The foal must be fed from its infancy on tender green grass. It cannot receive full nourishment from its motherʼs milk. The cow, whether of the zebu, Bos indicus, or any other species, makes the usual sound of hámbá – a – a – hámbá. It has horns, but they are very weak. When there is a battle between the bulls, their horns break. The cow very much dislikes to carry any luggage on its back. It does not like anyone to sit on its back.
summary: Let us compare the horse, the cow, the buffalo and the mule – these four animal species.

If while moving along, the horse comes across one road that goes uphill, another that goes downhill and another that goes straight on flat land, it will choose the path that goes straight ahead on flat land.
It does not like anyone to sit on its back.

paragraphs.text: The horse submits to some extent when it is given a bath, but the cow sees a tiger when it is taken to water. It always wants to keep away from water. When someone found in a bad situation is cornered, people will say, “Give the cow a good wash”. Since the cow is slow moving, it has great capacity to provide milk. Not only is the calf nurtured on its motherʼs milk, but there is always an extra supply of milk, in fact more than double the quantity of milk the calf requires for its sustenance. Thus if the requisite milk for the calf is left aside and the excess milk is consumed by human beings, there is no question of depriving anyone.
summary: The horse submits to some extent when it is given a bath, but the cow sees a tiger when it is taken to water.
Since the cow is slow moving, it has great capacity to provide milk.
Thus if the requisite milk for the calf is left aside and the excess milk is consumed by human beings, there is no question of depriving anyone.

paragraphs.text: The buffalo came into human contact much later. The horse came into contact with humans the earliest; next came the cow, and then the buffalo. The horn of the buffalo is slightly circular. It has strength; hence it does not break easily. Sometimes with the help of its horns it is able to resist attack. The tiger is not at all afraid of the cow, but it treats the buffalo with a certain regard, although it is not afraid of it. If luggage is put on the back of the buffalo, it scarcely takes note and even endures the load. In northern and western India, people in rural areas move about on the back of buffaloes for miles and miles together.
summary: The buffalo came into human contact much later.
Sometimes with the help of its horns it is able to resist attack.
In northern and western India, people in rural areas move about on the back of buffaloes for miles and miles together.

paragraphs.text: One of my boyhood friends was a reputed zamindar from a place in Bihar. Let us assume that his name was Chandra Kanta Sinha. Once one of my distantly related nephews told me, “Uncle, please write a letter to Chandrakantajii in my favour, which will help me in accomplishing some work easily.” Accordingly, my nephew went to Chandrakantajii with my letter. Chandrakanta was not at home at that time. He was also a professor of Philosophy at a nearby college. My nephew thought that he must have gone to the college to teach his classes, so he went in the direction of the college. Almost taking him by surprise, Chandrakanta met him on the way. He was riding on the back of an indigenous buffalo towards the college four miles away. Of course, even then he had a voluminous Philosophy book in hand. My nephew asked him, “Uncle, is everything alright?” Chandrakantajii replied, “Yes, yes, you had better come along and sit beside me.” I did not ask my nephew what happened after that.
summary: One of my boyhood friends was a reputed zamindar from a place in Bihar.
My nephew thought that he must have gone to the college to teach his classes, so he went in the direction of the college.
” I did not ask my nephew what happened after that.

paragraphs.text: Apart from this, whatever the cow can do, such as tilling the soil or drawing the cart, the buffalo can do it all. In muddy soil the cowʼs feet get stuck and then it cannot till the field or draw the carriage properly. The buffalo can do this all very well. Compared to the cow, the buffalo is much more slow-moving. That is why in comparison with the cow it gives far more milk. However, the difficulty with the buffalo is that when it finds the road splitting into one going ahead on flat land, one rising uphill and one going downhill, it chooses the road going downhill. If it finds any slough or pond beside the road, it goes down to the water right along with the plough and the yoke or the covered carriage, dragging everything along behind. At that moment the buffalo hardly remembers that there is a hefty man sitting in the carriage. When tilling dry land belonging to someone, if it comes across water on the adjoining land, it does not hesitate to enter that land along with the plough and yoke. Due to its tendency to go downhill or towards any water body, it is called kasara, kásara or kesara. When the road goes in three different directions, the donkey, the horse and the cow all choose the road going on flat land, but the buffalo chooses the road going downhill; the camel prefers the dry road, and the mule chooses the road going uphill. For military purposes, and in the hilly regions for commercial and transportation purposes, people have used the mule more often since it likes to move uphill.
summary: Apart from this, whatever the cow can do, such as tilling the soil or drawing the cart, the buffalo can do it all.
If it finds any slough or pond beside the road, it goes down to the water right along with the plough and the yoke or the covered carriage, dragging everything along behind.
For military purposes, and in the hilly regions for commercial and transportation purposes, people have used the mule more often since it likes to move uphill.

paragraphs.text: When a person living in a particular country is nourished by the land and water, the beauty and flavour, the flow of life and vitality of that country, and if they come to address that country as their mother, it is not a grammatical error or desecration of history, or great sacrilege. Even the affectionate father holding the daughter in his lap caresses her as he would his mother, though everyone knows that the tiny girl is none other than his own daughter. If by drinking the milk of any creature a person receives nourishment, what is wrong if they address the animal as their mother? Does it really turn the animal into their mother? It is simply a kind of veneration that is offered here due to someone caring like a mother. Yes, it is true that human beings do not take only cowʼs milk but also the milk of the camel, goat and buffalo. So if we offer veneration, we have to also do the same to the camel, goat and buffalo. Yes, to make much ado of the cow as mother is not desirable, because it will appear ludicrous, and if someone thinks that they can worship the cow, smearing it with oil and vermilion they can worship it, while the buffalo can be slaughtered and with its blood one can even take a ritual bath, then it would be an intellectual betrayal. Their attitude cannot be appreciated. ( 7 )
summary: When a person living in a particular country is nourished by the land and water, the beauty and flavour, the flow of life and vitality of that country, and if they come to address that country as their mother, it is not a grammatical error or desecration of history, or great sacrilege.
It is simply a kind of veneration that is offered here due to someone caring like a mother.
Their attitude cannot be appreciated.

paragraphs.text: Domestic pig: That which multiplies in huge numbers or is counted in big numbers is called kot́ija. In that sense, various kinds of viruses or insects such as shyámápoká [Green leaf-hoppers] can be called kot́ija; but in the derivative sense it means “pigs” and “plantain trees”.
summary: Domestic pig: That which multiplies in huge numbers or is counted in big numbers is called kot́ija.
In that sense, various kinds of viruses or insects such as shyámápoká [Green leaf-hoppers] can be called kot́ija; but in the derivative sense it means “pigs” and “plantain trees”.

paragraphs.text: Among the domesticated animals, pigs (shúkara or shor or baráha) multiply very rapidly. Expenses incurred in maintaining pigs are also minimal. That is why since ancient times, poor people have invariably shown interest in keeping pigs. No other animal meat is as cheaply available. Pigs are very dirty creatures and are also fond of eating dirty items. In most countries of the world pigs are domesticated because they are easy to maintain. In India, people primarily belonging to the scavenger caste keep pigs. Others also keep pigs and many of them eat their meat as well. Except for those who are forbidden by religion, many people have been trading in pig meat since ancient times. When Englishmen came to Bengal, they used to dry pig meat (at that time the scientific method of de-hydration had not come into practice) and export it. It is said that pigs were even exported alive. The place from which the Portuguese came to collect pigs, just adjacent to Kolkata, is still known today as Baranagar or Barahanagar. Barabani of Burdwan district and Barabazar of Manbhum district, however, do not derive their names from the export of pigs. In the forest areas of those places, many wild pigs or baráha used to roam. That is why those localities came to have such names. In ancient India only the shúdras (lower caste people) were permitted to eat pig meat (pork). The kśatriyas had permission to eat pork during the time of battle. The practice of eating the meat of wild boar was prevalent among all people except Brahmans.
summary: Among the domesticated animals, pigs (shúkara or shor or baráha) multiply very rapidly.
When Englishmen came to Bengal, they used to dry pig meat (at that time the scientific method of de-hydration had not come into practice) and export it.
The practice of eating the meat of wild boar was prevalent among all people except Brahmans.

paragraphs.text: The population growth rate of wild boars is not similar to that of domesticated pigs. Besides this, living in the wild they are constantly struck down and ravaged by an uncongenial environment. Carnivorous people say that the meat of the wild boar is far more delicious than that of domesticated pigs. Wild boar meat is also very dear to the tiger. Of course, the huge tiger does not normally attack the wild boar, because one would not be sure who would win the battle and who would die. Normally the large tiger attacks the calf of the boar, just as the boar attacks the calf of the tiger. Although the wild boar is normally a vegetarian, it has a tremendous weakness for tiger meat and buffalo meat. The wild boar, having an angry disposition (such a creature is called kaopin in Sanskrit), is frequently carried away by rage and meets with a premature death. Some people think that wild boars for generations have been converted into domesticated pigs. But no, this is not correct. Domesticated pigs and wild boars are two different kinds of creatures, although they both belong to the pig genus.
summary: The population growth rate of wild boars is not similar to that of domesticated pigs.
Normally the large tiger attacks the calf of the boar, just as the boar attacks the calf of the tiger.
Domesticated pigs and wild boars are two different kinds of creatures, although they both belong to the pig genus.

paragraphs.text: Domesticated pigs do not like to move about freely. They like to be under the shelter of human beings, as they have no means of self-preservation, very much like the goat and the cow. When I was in China, I saw people taking very good care of pigs. I saw a housewife feeding her pigs with cooked, salted rice-water.
summary: Domesticated pigs do not like to move about freely.
When I was in China, I saw people taking very good care of pigs.
I saw a housewife feeding her pigs with cooked, salted rice-water.

paragraphs.text: Wild boars are not at all amenable to human control. They want to live independently. Their front teeth are more pointed and sharp than the raised horn of the rhinoceros. By temperament the rhinoceros is calm, but the wild boar is hot-tempered. For human beings, the wild boar is more dangerous than the rhinoceros. Carnivorous people say that the meat of the rhinoceros is as tasty as that of the wild boar.
summary: Wild boars are not at all amenable to human control.
By temperament the rhinoceros is calm, but the wild boar is hot-tempered.
Carnivorous people say that the meat of the rhinoceros is as tasty as that of the wild boar.

paragraphs.text: The one-horned rhinoceros of the Sunderbans has become extinct due to human greed for its meat. Of course, killing the rhinoceros is not as easy as killing the wild boar. The hide of the rhinoceros is impenetrable, but that of the wild boar is extremely tender. The rhinoceros is feeble-eyed, while the wild boar is keeneyed. Although a rhinoceros is not amenable to human control, if well treated it tries to make friends with people, especially with children. The wild boar, however, is always ready to attack any other creature. It has been noticed in the Sundarbans that when the number of wild boars and Sundarbans deer has reduced, the number of tigers has also either reduced or they have invaded human settlements. In any case, due to their rapid growth, pigs have come to be known as kot́ija. However, this word would apply better to domesticated pigs and not to wild boars. ( 8 )
summary: The one-horned rhinoceros of the Sunderbans has become extinct due to human greed for its meat.
Although a rhinoceros is not amenable to human control, if well treated it tries to make friends with people, especially with children.
However, this word would apply better to domesticated pigs and not to wild boars.

paragraphs.text: Yak (Camrii): In Tibet and adjacent areas, the yaks, called cámrii, are available both in the wild and domesticated state. Their milk is very similar to cowʼs milk, except that it has a bad odour. The wool of the yaks is lengthy and handsome. Many a time the attractive appearance of a human being or an animal winds up being the cause of that creatureʼs death. The impressive hide of the deer or its horns is often responsible for its death; the wings of the bright green insect are often responsible for its death; once the feathers of a peacock were considered to be the cause of its death. Similarly, the handsome hair of the camrii is often considered to be the cause of its death. It is said: Kesheśu camriiḿ hanti, meaning, “for its hair a yak is killed”.
summary: Yak (Camrii): In Tibet and adjacent areas, the yaks, called cámrii, are available both in the wild and domesticated state.
Many a time the attractive appearance of a human being or an animal winds up being the cause of that creatureʼs death.
It is said: Kesheśu camriiḿ hanti, meaning, “for its hair a yak is killed”.

paragraphs.text: In English camrii is called yak. The female yak is called giripriyá. Some people firmly believe that the ox on which Lord Shiva used to roam around the world was no ordinary ox, but a male yak. Apparently the male yak is somewhat ferocious looking. At least, people of the plains would become frightened at its initial appearance, although there is no reason to fear it. It is very calm and quiet by nature. On its own it never attacks anyone; and even when attacked, it does not normally retaliate. It fights only when its life is in danger. Its lengthy, beautiful hair, when tied around a stick, is known as cámar. In ancient times, ritually blessed persons used to be fanned with a cámar.
summary: In English camrii is called yak.
It is very calm and quiet by nature.
In ancient times, ritually blessed persons used to be fanned with a cámar.

paragraphs.text: Usually, on reaching the five different stages of life, one had to pass through certain rituals called abhiśek. The first was at the early stage of childhood on the occasion of játakarma or naming ceremony; the second was during the sacred thread ceremony; the third was the marriage ceremony; the fourth was upon ascension to the throne or when being crowned as the crown prince; and the fifth was when, by the grace of the Guru, one received initiation into higher spiritual practices. This kind of spiritual initiation at the directive of the Guru was called Sámrájya Diikśá [initiation of universal sovereignty]. On this occasion, at the directive of the Guru, one of his junior disciples used to fan his senior disciple with the cámar. These five stages combined were called Paiṋcábhiśek [five-fold initiation]. On these occasions, there was the practice of using conch shells, five lamps and the cámar. Yes, Kesheśu cámriiḿ hanti – for the sake of its hair, the yak was killed by humans. ( 9 )
summary: Usually, on reaching the five different stages of life, one had to pass through certain rituals called abhiśek.
On this occasion, at the directive of the Guru, one of his junior disciples used to fan his senior disciple with the cámar.
Yes, Kesheśu cámriiḿ hanti – for the sake of its hair, the yak was killed by humans.

paragraphs.text: Dwindling usefulness of our domestic animals: You all know that in everyday life people are reducing the use of animals. The job of tilling is now being done by power-tillers and tractors. The bullock cart is going out of use; the use of the horse-carriage is now as good as nil. For the sake of milk, people will probably keep cows for some time to come. After the discovery of synthetic milk, people will give up keeping cows at home, since for tilling and milking cows will no longer be necessary. For use in oil mills, bullocks have already become redundant.
summary: Dwindling usefulness of our domestic animals: You all know that in everyday life people are reducing the use of animals.
For the sake of milk, people will probably keep cows for some time to come.
For use in oil mills, bullocks have already become redundant.

paragraphs.text: Just as the necessity of cows will disappear in future, the necessity of horses also has almost come to an end. I surmise that in some dayʼs time, the horse will turn into an animal in the zoo. However, there was a time when the word ‘carriage’ was inalienably linked up with the horse, and along with the carriage they would invariably use the expression ‘horse-carriage’ (ghoŕá-gáŕii). In the field of speed, the horse was in such high demand! In the past, on the roads and resting places, on highways, in big towns and at road crossings, there was an arrangement for keeping large cisterns for quenching the thirst of horses and for bathing them by the roadside. In our own city of Kolkata, at various places there were such big cisterns filled with water. The black gram that was kept as fodder for the horses was soaked in these cisterns. In the Buddhist and even post-Buddhist eras, such large cisterns filled with water were prevalent on the roads and city thoroughfares. ( 10 )
summary: Just as the necessity of cows will disappear in future, the necessity of horses also has almost come to an end.

In the past, on the roads and resting places, on highways, in big towns and at road crossings, there was an arrangement for keeping large cisterns for quenching the thirst of horses and for bathing them by the roadside.
In the Buddhist and even post-Buddhist eras, such large cisterns filled with water were prevalent on the roads and city thoroughfares.

chapters.title: Lions and Other Dog Family Members

paragraphs.text: Dog family and cat family: You all know that our familiar carnivorous animals are divided into two families: the cat and the dog families. Animals belonging to the cat family have round faces with whiskers (even the tigress and the female cat have whiskers). They are not at all inclined to live as a family. They have sharp intelligence and courage, but they display their courage by applying intelligence; that is, they do not like to endanger themselves by simply making a show of their courage. Animals belonging to the cat family have little tolerance towards other animals. Animals belonging to the dog family (in Sanskrit kukkura or kukura; in Bengali kukur) have long and pointed faces; some of them even live in families (such as the lion). They have average intelligence. They thrust themselves into dangerous situations to display their courage. They are quite generous in nature and even make sacrifices.
summary: Dog family and cat family: You all know that our familiar carnivorous animals are divided into two families: the cat and the dog families.
Animals belonging to the cat family have little tolerance towards other animals.
They are quite generous in nature and even make sacrifices.

paragraphs.text: In the dog family, the largest animal is the African lion, now on the verge of extinction. The lions of Ráŕh became extinct about one hundred years ago. The Gujrat lion, the lion of Girnar or the Gir lion, both male and female, have no mane. In another lion species, only the males have a mane and not the females. (In Sanskrit and Bengali a lion is called siḿha, in Persian babar, in English lion, in Latin leo). Apart from this, there is the wolf in northern India called lákŕá bágh (in Sanskrit called brka, in English known as wolf). Then there are different species of dogs and jackals. Amongst these familiar animals, the smallest is the fox.
summary: In the dog family, the largest animal is the African lion, now on the verge of extinction.
(In Sanskrit and Bengali a lion is called siḿha, in Persian babar, in English lion, in Latin leo).
Amongst these familiar animals, the smallest is the fox.

paragraphs.text: Among the feline species the largest of them all is the kudo bágh or Royal Bengal Tiger of the Sundarbans. In Bengali it is called bágh, in Sanskrit byághra or shárdul, in Persian sher and in English tiger. There are black tigers, then jaguars of South America, gulbághás or panthers, cheetahs, and chitra byághras or leopards. Then there are also hyenas, which are called huŕárs, huńd́árs, begoyás, gobághás, in Sanskrit tarakśu. Smaller than this is the civet cat (bhám), the pole cat (khat́t́ásh, in spoken Bengali kát́t́ash), wild cats and our own domesticated cat.
summary: Among the feline species the largest of them all is the kudo bágh or Royal Bengal Tiger of the Sundarbans.
There are black tigers, then jaguars of South America, gulbághás or panthers, cheetahs, and chitra byághras or leopards.
Smaller than this is the civet cat (bhám), the pole cat (khat́t́ásh, in spoken Bengali kát́t́ash), wild cats and our own domesticated cat.

paragraphs.text: Both animals of the cat and dog families are carnivorous; they do not eat uncooked vegetarian food, although they sometimes eat cooked food. What is interesting is that although there are large and small varieties of dogs, they are not of any distinct subspecies. Its father is a wolf and its mother is a female jackal. Such is the identity of the dog. That is why, while seeking primitive fossils, I have come across the fossils of wolves and the fossils of jackals, but no fossils of the dog. In their early stage, all animals belonging to the dog family look very much alike. As they grow up, differences in their appearance become prominent; their cry also becomes distinct from other animals. Alsatians are very close to wolves. Domesticated wolves (they are not easily amenable to human control) and Alsatians have very little differences. They have a very powerful sense of smell and can easily differentiate between various kinds of scents. Hence in the task of apprehending criminals, they help human beings to a great extent. Both the dog and cat families of animals make distinctive sounds. ( 1 )
summary: Both animals of the cat and dog families are carnivorous; they do not eat uncooked vegetarian food, although they sometimes eat cooked food.
As they grow up, differences in their appearance become prominent; their cry also becomes distinct from other animals.
Both the dog and cat families of animals make distinctive sounds.

paragraphs.text: The dog is a sharp-snouted member of the canine family, and the tiger is a round-snouted member of the feline family. There is an inherent hostility between these two. According to biologists, members of the canine family are sharp-snouted, carnivorous, swift runners, make noise when they run, and have a strong sense of smell (the Alsatian is an exception). They also display a great deal of affection towards their young. The largest animal in this group is the maned lion, native to Africa. In addition, there is the medium-sized, maned Indian lion, the maneless Indian lion or gurjar lion, the wolf (brkabyághra), Alsatian, ( 2 ) the ordinary domesticated Indian dog, the wild Indian dog, the jackal (shrgála), the fox (ulkámukhii), and so on. In addition there are many kinds of short-haired and long-haired dogs differing in variety and from country to country. Some people are of the opinion that while the dog no doubt belongs to the canine family, it is not an original species but rather a cross-breed – the wolf is its father and the jackal its mother; this was the ancient conception.
summary: The dog is a sharp-snouted member of the canine family, and the tiger is a round-snouted member of the feline family.
The largest animal in this group is the maned lion, native to Africa.

Some people are of the opinion that while the dog no doubt belongs to the canine family, it is not an original species but rather a cross-breed – the wolf is its father and the jackal its mother; this was the ancient conception.

paragraphs.text: Although dogs live in groups, different members of the canine family do not mix with each other. For example, wolves and lions are not on good terms with each other. Wolves will chase a dog if they see one and will kill it, regardless of whether they eat it or not. Dogs will also chase jackals if they see them.
summary: Although dogs live in groups, different members of the canine family do not mix with each other.
Wolves will chase a dog if they see one and will kill it, regardless of whether they eat it or not.
Dogs will also chase jackals if they see them.

paragraphs.text: The tiger, however, is a different family of animal, a feline. Members of the feline family do not remain in groups. They are extremely greedy and self-seeking. The father does not show one iota of affection towards his progeny and often kills them. Members of this family suffer great pain at the time of dying. Even though the father does not feel any affection for his progeny, the mother does to a great extent. Female cats and tigers raise their young with a great deal of affection and even cry for a long time when their offspring die. ( 3 )
summary: The tiger, however, is a different family of animal, a feline.
The father does not show one iota of affection towards his progeny and often kills them.
Female cats and tigers raise their young with a great deal of affection and even cry for a long time when their offspring die.

paragraphs.text: The fundamental difference between the cat family and the dog family is that animals of the dog family move around in search of prey, just as the dog moves in search of food. It sniffs here and there, and, if not getting the desired object, runs somewhere else. Creatures of the cat family do not do this; at a convenient place they wait and come upon a scent and then, following the scent, suddenly swoop down upon their prey. Of course tigers also jump or leap upon their prey; that is why the tiger that leaps upon its prey is called ‘leaping tiger’. In the smaller arena, the cat also leaps upon the rat in a similar manner.
summary: The fundamental difference between the cat family and the dog family is that animals of the dog family move around in search of prey, just as the dog moves in search of food.
Creatures of the cat family do not do this; at a convenient place they wait and come upon a scent and then, following the scent, suddenly swoop down upon their prey.
In the smaller arena, the cat also leaps upon the rat in a similar manner.

paragraphs.text: Creatures of the dog family always leave an impression of sincerity in all their activities. By proving their manliness, they satisfy their ego. Even risking their life, they nourish their manliness. Animals of the cat family do not do so. They are opportunists; seeking an opportunity, they act. This is the difference between the cat and the dog.
summary: Creatures of the dog family always leave an impression of sincerity in all their activities.
Animals of the cat family do not do so.
This is the difference between the cat and the dog.

paragraphs.text: That also is the distinction between the lion and the tiger. The lion, due to its imperial appearance and its mane, is called the king of animals, although its physical strength is less than that of the Royal Bengal Tiger. Like other creatures of the dog family, the intelligence of the lion is somewhat less than that of the tiger. The lion and other members of the dog family act rashly and without premeditation. Animals of the cat family never do this. The creatures of the dog family often live in herds and in families. Those of the cat family never do so.They believe in exclusiveness and solitary life. They have no friends, no allies, none with whom to share their pleasures and woes, to whom they can communicate their feelings. They are entirely solitary.
summary: That also is the distinction between the lion and the tiger.
The creatures of the dog family often live in herds and in families.
They are entirely solitary.

paragraphs.text: Since the animals of the dog family have less intelligence, they often retreat in their battle for life; even the members of the cat family are also losing the battle for existence, but to a far less extent than members of the dog family. The African lion – the powerful and gigantic king of maned animals – is very large in size. The females do not have manes. At one time lions were the undisputed monarchs in the African savannah. No one dared to do battle with them for power. It was as if the lion felt: “I am the monarch of all I survey; no one dare to dispute my sovereign rights.” Even then, lions lost the battle of intelligence to frail creatures – human beings. The Sahara Desert and the large stretch of forestland to the south no longer reverberate with the triumphant roar of the lion. Yes, there are lions; but theirs is not real living, it is just survival. Even in our Ráŕh region, the heavily forested sandy beds of the Mayurákśii, Ajay, Damodar, Dvarakeshvar and Subarnarekha rivers once reverberated with the roars of lions.
summary: Since the animals of the dog family have less intelligence, they often retreat in their battle for life; even the members of the cat family are also losing the battle for existence, but to a far less extent than members of the dog family.
It was as if the lion felt: “I am the monarch of all I survey; no one dare to dispute my sovereign rights.
Even in our Ráŕh region, the heavily forested sandy beds of the Mayurákśii, Ajay, Damodar, Dvarakeshvar and Subarnarekha rivers once reverberated with the roars of lions.

paragraphs.text: Although the Ráŕhii lion was smaller in size than the African lion, the appearance of the males was impressive. Compared to its body, the face was quite large, and the teeth sharper. It is about 150 years since Dumka, Birbhum and Samantabhum became devoid of lions. Other areas –Sikharbhum, Senbhum, Manbhum, Bhanjabhum, Singhabhum, Barahabhum, and Sabarbhum – are also now bereft of lions. Even a century ago the females of this species had no manes. Yet in their sweeping forcefulness, in their raging violence, in their vanity of existence, they were simply unrivaled. Due to their uncongenial environment on the red soil of Ráŕh, these lions have become extinct. Only some fossils of this animal are found on the riverbeds of the dying and narrow rivers. The Girnar lion of western India, although unsightly in appearance, somehow survived in the hilly forest areas of Girnar in Gujrat due to its more congenial environment. As a result of recent conservation measures, the Girnar lion has been partially preserved [from extinction]. Still homelier than this unsightly lion, the females of this species are more numerous today because of their superior intelligence. If governmental safeguards are withdrawn at any time, it will not be long before these lions become extinct. ( 4 )
summary: Although the Ráŕhii lion was smaller in size than the African lion, the appearance of the males was impressive.
Due to their uncongenial environment on the red soil of Ráŕh, these lions have become extinct.
If governmental safeguards are withdrawn at any time, it will not be long before these lions become extinct.

paragraphs.text: Nature and habitat of the lion: The lion (siḿha) is a long-faced animal belonging to the dog family (the tiger belongs to the round-faced feline family.) [As mentioned earlier] the largest animal of this family is the African lion. Huge in appearance, with a large face, the male lions have manes. Of course, the lioness has no mane. If there are hills nearby, they live in caves; where there are no hills they live in the bush. They do not like dense forests. Another large animal of this family is the Rárhii lion. About one hundred to one hundred twenty five years ago, on the dry fields and the forests of Ráŕh, these lions used to roam about triumphantly. Their kingdoms were in Dumka, Deoghar, the southwest of Birbhum (i.e., in Dubrajpur and Khairashol areas), West Burdwan, Bankura, West Midnapur, Bhainjabhum and Manbhum (in Purulia, Dhanbad and other areas). Many villages of these areas have the word siḿha and gharghará associated with them. Near Ananda Nagar is the village Siḿghághrá (siḿhagharghárá). Close to it is Ghágrá (gharghará) village. There are many villages associated with the word siḿha, such as Birsiḿha, Banbirsiḿha, etc. Kings used to have names like SiḿhaVáhu, Vijaysingha, and so on. Some time ago, in the adjoining areas of the Shushunia hills (Bankura), the fossils of lion jaws were discovered, just as fossils of large mammoths have also been found in that region. Somewhat smaller in appearance than the Ráŕhii lion is the Girnar lion of Gujarat. The male Girnar lions do not have manes. From a distance they look somewhat like dogs. ( 5 )
summary: Nature and habitat of the lion: The lion (siḿha) is a long-faced animal belonging to the dog family (the tiger belongs to the round-faced feline family.
, in Dubrajpur and Khairashol areas), West Burdwan, Bankura, West Midnapur, Bhainjabhum and Manbhum (in Purulia, Dhanbad and other areas).
From a distance they look somewhat like dogs.

paragraphs.text: The large lions of Africa used to roam about in large number in the savannah and dry bushland of Africa and in the southern areas of the Sahara desert. Recently, their number has gone down appreciably. The males have manes, while the females do not.
summary: The large lions of Africa used to roam about in large number in the savannah and dry bushland of Africa and in the southern areas of the Sahara desert.
Recently, their number has gone down appreciably.
The males have manes, while the females do not.

paragraphs.text: The Girnar lions of Gujarat, or of the Girnar forest, are inhabitants of the dry, semi-desert areas of Gujarat. Their number has dwindled to such an extent that they have nearly come to the point of extinction. Due to special efforts by the Government of India to save this species, their population has increased to some extent. This is a good sign.
summary: The Girnar lions of Gujarat, or of the Girnar forest, are inhabitants of the dry, semi-desert areas of Gujarat.
Their number has dwindled to such an extent that they have nearly come to the point of extinction.
Due to special efforts by the Government of India to save this species, their population has increased to some extent.

paragraphs.text: Once the [Rárhii lion] used to roam throughout Ráŕh, especially in western Ráŕh, in large numbers. Even today in the Shushunia hills of Bankura, in the Biharilal (some say Biharinath) hills, in Panchakot of Manbhum, Tilabani, Joichandi and Ayodhya hills, in the Dalma hills of Singhbhum, in Bhanjabhum, in Dimdiha of Manbhum, in the hills of Sapkuthi, Taherbera and Jabar hills [near Ananda Nagar], many such lion fossils can be found. This Rárhii lion became completely extinct nearly ninety years ago. [As mentioned earlier], once the favourite haunts of the Rárhii lion were the bushes of Baglata, Gurabazar and Guridi, adjacent to Ananda Nagar. Today there is not a single lion in that area. Yet the names of the villages are associated with the lion – Siḿghaghará [the roaring sound of the lion], Ghágrá [the roar of the lion], Sat́ká [the runaway lion], Bághlatá [Baglata; where the tiger cowers down]. The names of the villages bear out the intimate relations of these places with the lion. ( 6 )
summary: Once the [Rárhii lion] used to roam throughout Ráŕh, especially in western Ráŕh, in large numbers.
[As mentioned earlier], once the favourite haunts of the Rárhii lion were the bushes of Baglata, Gurabazar and Guridi, adjacent to Ananda Nagar.
The names of the villages bear out the intimate relations of these places with the lion.

paragraphs.text: Wolf (brka byághra): Our very familiar animal, the wolf (lákŕá or nekŕe bágh, in Sanskrit brka byághra) belongs to the dog family. This dog-faced animal is a peculiar species of the Ráŕh region. In the conservation areas of Ráŕh, this type of wolf can be found even today in sufficient numbers. They live in the caves of hills, in rough terrain, and in hollows in the ground. As little as seventy years ago, near the police stations of Rajnagar in Birbhum, these wolves were a source of worry to the owners of domesticated animals. Today, because of deforestation, there is hardly a single wolf in Birbhum, although there are some in other districts. The proverb ‘wolf at the door’ is derived from the greedy nature of wolves. The Alsatians and various wild dogs also come in this category. It is interesting to note that these latter animals live in herds. They believe in living together as a group, unlike cats such as the civet cat, wild cat, polecat, etc. who prefer to live in isolation. ( 7 )
summary: Wolf (brka byághra): Our very familiar animal, the wolf (lákŕá or nekŕe bágh, in Sanskrit brka byághra) belongs to the dog family.
Today, because of deforestation, there is hardly a single wolf in Birbhum, although there are some in other districts.
who prefer to live in isolation.

paragraphs.text: The wolf – lákŕá or lákaŕ bághá in north India – is always going out for the purpose of eating. In some peopleʼs opinion, the wolf can take into its stomach significantly more than the weight of its own body. Just as the ant can carry a load that is much heavier than its own body, the wolf can eat more. The wolf has very little capacity for carrying loads. Due to his excessive gluttony, the second Pandava brother, Bhima, used to be called Brkodara (one whose stomach is like a wolfʼs). During the time that the Pandavas were incognito, mother Kunti would take the food they would bring home from begging and give half of it to Bhima. The remainder she and her other four sons would eat.
summary: The wolf – lákŕá or lákaŕ bághá in north India – is always going out for the purpose of eating.
The wolf has very little capacity for carrying loads.
The remainder she and her other four sons would eat.

paragraphs.text: Ardha khán Kuntii saha cári sahodare,
summary: Ardha khán Kuntii saha cári sahodare,

paragraphs.text: Ardhek báṋt́iyá den viirbrkodare.
summary: Ardhek báṋt́iyá den viirbrkodare.

paragraphs.text: [Half the four brothers eat along with Kunti, half is apportioned to the brave Bhima.] ( 8 )]
summary: [Half the four brothers eat along with Kunti, half is apportioned to the brave Bhima.

paragraphs.text: Alsatian: You are all familiar with the Alsatian. We look upon the Alsatian as a dog, but in reality it is not a dog. It is an animal very close to the wolf family. Of course, there is a fundamental difference between the two. There are four factors that separate them from each other. The first point of difference is that although the wolf has a very strong sense of smell, the Alsatian has an even stronger sense of smell.
summary: Alsatian: You are all familiar with the Alsatian.
Of course, there is a fundamental difference between the two.
The first point of difference is that although the wolf has a very strong sense of smell, the Alsatian has an even stronger sense of smell.

paragraphs.text: The second point of difference is that the wolf, whether it eats it or not, will slay a dog that crosses its path. But the wild Alsatian (let alone the domesticated Alsatian) is not that hostile towards the dog.
summary: The second point of difference is that the wolf, whether it eats it or not, will slay a dog that crosses its path.
But the wild Alsatian (let alone the domesticated Alsatian) is not that hostile towards the dog.

paragraphs.text: The third point of difference is that the wolf can consume food about two and half times its own size. After that, of course, it lies flat on the ground for a few days like a dead animal. The Alsatian does not eat so much.
summary: The third point of difference is that the wolf can consume food about two and half times its own size.
After that, of course, it lies flat on the ground for a few days like a dead animal.
The Alsatian does not eat so much.

paragraphs.text: Fourthly, the wolf is not easily amenable to domestication, but the Alsatian can be domesticated and is very devoted to its master. In ancient times the crossbreeding of the wolf and the jackal led to the birth of the dog. There is no proof actually as to whether the wolf and the jackal, in the same manner, crossbred to produce the Alsatian. If at all there is a mixture of the wolf and the jackal in the Alsatian, there is more of the wolf.
summary: Fourthly, the wolf is not easily amenable to domestication, but the Alsatian can be domesticated and is very devoted to its master.
There is no proof actually as to whether the wolf and the jackal, in the same manner, crossbred to produce the Alsatian.
If at all there is a mixture of the wolf and the jackal in the Alsatian, there is more of the wolf.

paragraphs.text: In all languages of the world, there is mention of the wolf but not the Alsatian. In Sanskrit the wolf is called brk byághra. In the Vedic age there were vague references to the fact that some human beings, after killing the wolf, used to eat its meat, particularly its heart. In Sanskrit literature, even in ancient Bengali literature, there are references to the wolf as a voracious eater. ( 9 )
summary: In all languages of the world, there is mention of the wolf but not the Alsatian.
In the Vedic age there were vague references to the fact that some human beings, after killing the wolf, used to eat its meat, particularly its heart.
In Sanskrit literature, even in ancient Bengali literature, there are references to the wolf as a voracious eater.

paragraphs.text: Jackal: The jackal (shiyál) is a very familiar animal of the equatorial region. Its history is also very old. This animal reached its present state through several evolutions. People of various countries of the world have ruthlessly slaughtered jackals due to their greed for wool and leather. There are even some tribals in India who eat the meat of jackals.
summary: Jackal: The jackal (shiyál) is a very familiar animal of the equatorial region.
This animal reached its present state through several evolutions.
There are even some tribals in India who eat the meat of jackals.

paragraphs.text: Synonyms of shiyál are shivá, yambuka, jambukukkura, badrikukkura, etc. Berries are a favourite fruit of jackals. That is why jackals are called jambukukkura and badrikukkura. Jackals are eaten by tribal people. Apart from this, there is a small group of people in Ráŕh who are known as shiálkhore [jackal-eaters] or shiálkhego [jackal-eating people]. Although jackals like jujube fruits, they are also very fond of berries. ( 10 )
summary: Synonyms of shiyál are shivá, yambuka, jambukukkura, badrikukkura, etc.
Jackals are eaten by tribal people.
Although jackals like jujube fruits, they are also very fond of berries.

paragraphs.text: Fox: The fox (khekshiyál) makes the khi… khi… khi sound more often than it scowls or snarls. Hence the khi… khi sound indicates a fox and not a jackal. Of course, the chaste Sanskrit word for fox is ulkámukhii. Some people believe that foxes have phosphorus in their mouth and teeth, and as they scowl, due to contact with the air, that phosphorus lights up. The Sanskrit word ulká means meteor in English. Because its mouth glitters, it is called ulkámukhii in Sanskrit.
summary: Fox: The fox (khekshiyál) makes the khi… khi… khi sound more often than it scowls or snarls.
Some people believe that foxes have phosphorus in their mouth and teeth, and as they scowl, due to contact with the air, that phosphorus lights up.
Because its mouth glitters, it is called ulkámukhii in Sanskrit.

paragraphs.text: In North India khikir means fox. One does not have to search for foxes in the forest. Wherever there are jujube trees (plum trees), one will find these animals in their vicinity in holes in the ground. Both the jackal and the fox belong to the same family. In ancient times they had the same ancestors. Nowadays the fox is smaller in size than the jackal. The protruding part of their mouth is somewhat different. Both are nocturnal creatures. Of course, the fox more than the jackal sometimes emerges during the daytime. When the fox yawns, its mouth lights up, but this is not so with the jackal. The skin of the fox is thinner than the skin of the jackal, so nothing can be made from the skin of the fox; but yarns, shoes and caps are prepared from the hide of the jackal. Few people are interested in eating foxes. It is said that the meat of the fox is very hard and dry. In the spring, winter and summer, fox droppings are full of jujube seeds. One can thus easily find out the habits of foxes. The cry of the fox sounds like khi- khi- khi- khi and that of the jackal sounds like hukká-huá, hukká-huá. At night jackals cry out together in herds, but foxes do not do so. ( 11 )
summary: In North India khikir means fox.
Of course, the fox more than the jackal sometimes emerges during the daytime.
At night jackals cry out together in herds, but foxes do not do so.

paragraphs.text: Dog: The word kukkura [dog] is also used in the sense of kukura. The word kukkura is formed by adding the suffix urań to the verbal root kuk. In it there is an additional ka. Some call the suffix kurańa as well. The word kukur is prevalent both in Bengali and in Bhojpuri. The word is used in its original Sanskrit form. In Punjabi it is called kukkur. The word is derived from Sanskrit. Again, according to some, the original Sanskrit word is kukkura, and kukura is the prákrta form [spoken form] or the grhita Sanskrit form [word from another language accepted in Sanskrit].
summary: Dog: The word kukkura [dog] is also used in the sense of kukura.
The word kukur is prevalent both in Bengali and in Bhojpuri.
Again, according to some, the original Sanskrit word is kukkura, and kukura is the prákrta form [spoken form] or the grhita Sanskrit form [word from another language accepted in Sanskrit].

paragraphs.text: According to some zoologists, a dog is not an original species [sui generis]; it is a hybrid creature. According to some scholars, a dog is a hybrid of the wolf and the vixen. In ancient times wild dogs were rather scarce, precisely for the same reason. There is hardly any dog fossil amongst the available fossils of ancient animals. Nowadays, however, wild dogs are also prevalent. These wild dogs live gregariously in jungles, and even a gigantic tiger has been seen to be flabbergasted and killed by a concerted attack of these dogs.
summary: According to some zoologists, a dog is not an original species [sui generis]; it is a hybrid creature.
There is hardly any dog fossil amongst the available fossils of ancient animals.
These wild dogs live gregariously in jungles, and even a gigantic tiger has been seen to be flabbergasted and killed by a concerted attack of these dogs.

paragraphs.text: Although the dog is a hybrid of the wolf and the vixen, it must be said that there are many radical, extreme differences between a wolf and a dog. A wolf is voracious, but a dog feels satisfied with a small meal. It is difficult to tame a wolf, but a dog loves to be domesticated. A dog is extremely faithful and loyal to its master. A wolf is neither faithful nor loyal to its master. A dog is not ferocious by nature. It attacks or frightens someone as part of its duty. A wolf is ferocious by nature. It has no sense of duty. A dog would not normally kill a creature if its stomach were full. But a wolf, even when its belly is full, kills a creature. If it has no capacity to eat, it carries the carcass to its den and eats it according to its convenience. Dogs do not generally fight with other members of the dog family. They fight with members of the feline family. But a wolf does not observe any such principle. A wolf avoids the strong and unnecessarily attacks the weak. Although there is a family resemblance between the wolf and the dog, whenever a dog is sighted the wolf attacks and kills it.
summary: Although the dog is a hybrid of the wolf and the vixen, it must be said that there are many radical, extreme differences between a wolf and a dog.
It has no sense of duty.
Although there is a family resemblance between the wolf and the dog, whenever a dog is sighted the wolf attacks and kills it.

paragraphs.text: There are many differences between a jackal and a dog. A dog generally moves about during the daytime, but jackals are night prowlers by nature. A jackal moves in the daytime only when it is in danger, it has to change location or is excessively hungry. A jackal lives in a hole, but a dog never likes to live in a hole. It prefers to live in the open. A jackal cannot be tamed; but a dog can. By virtue of being night prowlers, jackals periodically howl in chorus to preserve their solidarity and register their presence. However, dogs do not have this habit. They bark collectively only when they have to fight an enemy as a body. Although both jackals and dogs belong to the canine family, a dog chases a jackal whenever it sees one. A jackal runs away at the sight of a dog. By nature a dog is brave and a jackal is cowardly.
summary: There are many differences between a jackal and a dog.
By virtue of being night prowlers, jackals periodically howl in chorus to preserve their solidarity and register their presence.
By nature a dog is brave and a jackal is cowardly.

paragraphs.text: The Alsatian dogs are close relatives of foxes. The dogs of Bhutan, although not cowardly, closely resemble jackals in cold countries.
summary: The Alsatian dogs are close relatives of foxes.
The dogs of Bhutan, although not cowardly, closely resemble jackals in cold countries.

paragraphs.text: Although a fox belongs to the dog family, its relation with the dog is very remote. In spite of some similarity between a dog and a jackal in appearance, there is a wide gulf of difference in their natures.
summary: Although a fox belongs to the dog family, its relation with the dog is very remote.
In spite of some similarity between a dog and a jackal in appearance, there is a wide gulf of difference in their natures.

paragraphs.text: The dog has been a companion of human beings since ancient times. History tells us that dogs have been of use and continue to be of use to people in different ways, in their prosperity as well as in their adversity. In the scriptures, a dog has sometimes been shown respect by presenting it as a symbol of dharma. Of course, there is no dearth of people who are opposed to dogs. In northern India, some people say: “Only one who is a dog himself maintains a dog.” In Hindi and Urdu, kukura [dog] is called kuttá. ( 12 )
summary: The dog has been a companion of human beings since ancient times.
Of course, there is no dearth of people who are opposed to dogs.

chapters.title: Tiger and Other Cat Family Members

paragraphs.text: Tiger: The second meaning of the word khat́akhádaka is byághra or tiger (bi-á-ghra + d́a = byághra); that is, a creature whose olfactory organ is very strong. If a tiger senses the specific scent of its prey, it will easily locate it and then rush out to seize it. Just as the crow is khat́akhádaka by virtue of its lips, similarly a tiger is khat́akhádaka by virtue of its nails and teeth. Another characteristic of the tiger is that by mere conjecture [instinct] it can take a precise leap and fall exactly upon its prey.
summary: Tiger: The second meaning of the word khat́akhádaka is byághra or tiger (bi-á-ghra + d́a = byághra); that is, a creature whose olfactory organ is very strong.
Just as the crow is khat́akhádaka by virtue of its lips, similarly a tiger is khat́akhádaka by virtue of its nails and teeth.
Another characteristic of the tiger is that by mere conjecture [instinct] it can take a precise leap and fall exactly upon its prey.

paragraphs.text: There are various types of tigers in the world. Of course, chief among them are the Royal Bengal tiger, black tiger, panther, cheetah (leopard), hyena, civet cat or pole cat, wild cat and our domesticated cat (not wolves, because they belong to the dog family).
summary: There are various types of tigers in the world.

Of course, chief among them are the Royal Bengal tiger, black tiger, panther, cheetah (leopard), hyena, civet cat or pole cat, wild cat and our domesticated cat (not wolves, because they belong to the dog family).

paragraphs.text: There are many similarities and dissimilarities between tigers and lions – both carnivorous animals. Judging from circumstances, the tiger must have come to India from the direction of China, while the lion must have been the original inhabitant of India. The tiger loves rain-affected regions and dense forest areas. It even likes slightly salty water. The lion is fond of land with scanty rainfall and bushy forests. It does not like salty water. Both tigers and lions are courageous animals. In physical strength, the Royal Bengal tigers of the Sundarbans are far more powerful than the African or Ráŕh lions. The lions of Gujarat are more powerful than certain types of tigers and weaker than others. Whether weak or powerful, all lions are courageous, and all tigers are valiant. Both tigers and lions have qualitative distinctiveness. Both are good looking. The tiger is much more intelligent than the lion. If tigers moving in the forest notice that some tree branches have been chopped off, they will suspect that enemies are lurking nearby. If it finds that a goat has been kept tied up in a secluded spot in the forest, it might feel tempted to attack, but it will not go forward and fall upon its prey immediately. Glancing all around, it will advance surreptitiously and run away with the goat. It runs away so fast that even the hunters are stunned. However, the lion has somewhat of a devil-may-care disposition: “Let the enemy come, I donʼt care; surely no one can beat me in physical strength,” is how the lion feels. Without looking around, and even risking its own life, it will fall upon its prey – the goat. It is not as greedy as the tiger or the wolf, especially when its stomach is full. It does not normally attack anyone without reason but it will counterattack someone who charges first. Compared to the tiger, the lion is more compassionate. Not only for its own progeny – which even the tiger feels – it has been found to have affection even for the offspring of other animals. Evidence of this behaviour has been documented.
summary: There are many similarities and dissimilarities between tigers and lions – both carnivorous animals.
The tiger is much more intelligent than the lion.
Evidence of this behaviour has been documented.

paragraphs.text: The damp areas of the Sundarbans are very congenial for tigers, but not for lions. The lion can hardly endure the salty water of that area. While the dry climate and sweet water of Ráŕh are quite congenial for lions, they are not at all congenial for the tiger. Hence in ancient times, although tigers were primarily concentrated in Bengal, both tigers and lions lived in Ráŕh. That is why the Puranic gods and goddesses have both tigers and lions as their mounts; the mount of the tiger god of the forest (Dakśiń Ráy) is naturally a tiger, and the mount for the goddess Rájrájershvarii is a tiger on the back of an elephant. Meanwhile, the mount of the Puranic goddess Durgá is a lion.
summary: The damp areas of the Sundarbans are very congenial for tigers, but not for lions.
Hence in ancient times, although tigers were primarily concentrated in Bengal, both tigers and lions lived in Ráŕh.
Meanwhile, the mount of the Puranic goddess Durgá is a lion.

paragraphs.text: The tiger, having a round face, is an animal of the cat family. Animals of both the dog family and the cat family have a very powerful sense of smell. However, animals of the dog family have to concentrate in order to track a scent. To understand where the milk or fish or meat is, the dog has to apply its mind, and only then does it pick up the scent; but animals of the cat family spontaneously get the scent through their nose. The cat does not have to apply any special faculty to know where in the house the milk or fish is located. The scent wafts towards it, and the cat is compelled by natural law to run in that direction. If the housekeeper drives it away, even then the cat remains drawn by the scent, voluntarily or involuntarily. We say that even after a beating, the cat forgets after some time and returns. Whether the cat received a beating or not, it is a particular scent that draws it back. Among the animals of the cat family, the tiger also has a very powerful sense of smell. The derivative meaning of the word byághra is “one who has a very strong sense of smell”. The number of tiger species is quite large. ( 1 )
summary: The tiger, having a round face, is an animal of the cat family.
If the housekeeper drives it away, even then the cat remains drawn by the scent, voluntarily or involuntarily.
The number of tiger species is quite large.

paragraphs.text: Pole cat: Khat́t́ash or kat́t́ásh is a feline animal. The derivative meaning of the word khat́t́ásh is “one which rests on a soft bed or prefers a soft bed”. In common usage, khat́t́ásh means “creatures of the cat family”.
summary: Pole cat: Khat́t́ash or kat́t́ásh is a feline animal.
The derivative meaning of the word khat́t́ásh is “one which rests on a soft bed or prefers a soft bed”.
In common usage, khat́t́ásh means “creatures of the cat family”.

paragraphs.text: You all know that animals of the cat family love a comfortable environment. They prefer a soft bed or the cozy side of an oven. The pole cat (khat́t́ásh) is an animal that lives outside the house; but even in the forests or bushes it prefers to lie down on soft grass or on soft creepers and the leaves of a tree. Although by nature they are not timid, they are afraid of humans. So they prefer to live apart from human settlements.
summary: You all know that animals of the cat family love a comfortable environment.
The pole cat (khat́t́ásh) is an animal that lives outside the house; but even in the forests or bushes it prefers to lie down on soft grass or on soft creepers and the leaves of a tree.
So they prefer to live apart from human settlements.

paragraphs.text: After construction of the dam on the Damodar River, in Ráŕh and in South Bengal the Jalangi, Mathabhanga, Ichamati, Kumar, Bhaerava, Nabaganga, Garai, Madhumati, Shivsa, Rupsa and Citra Rivers all dried up. As a result there was a severe onslaught of malaria in the region. Once known for its wealth and clamour of human beings, once resounding with the notes of birds, the then Banagram of Jessore district turned into a forest, having fallen victim to all-engulfing malaria. Due to fear of malaria, many people left their hearth and home and settled in and around Kolkata on the bank of the Bhagirathi. Not only Banagram, but three other sub-divisions r– Magura, Jessore-Sadar and Jhinaidaha – were reduced to the same plight, except for the Narail sub-division of Jessore. People moved away, and in their place came pole cats or Kat́t́ásh, herds of them. So there was a popular saying: “Kat́t́ásh is the king of Banagram and the lion of the forest.” ( 2 )
summary: After construction of the dam on the Damodar River, in Ráŕh and in South Bengal the Jalangi, Mathabhanga, Ichamati, Kumar, Bhaerava, Nabaganga, Garai, Madhumati, Shivsa, Rupsa and Citra Rivers all dried up.
Due to fear of malaria, many people left their hearth and home and settled in and around Kolkata on the bank of the Bhagirathi.
So there was a popular saying: “Kat́t́ásh is the king of Banagram and the lion of the forest.

paragraphs.text: Civet cat (gandhagokul): The gokul [cat] that emits a sweet smell [gandha] is called gandhagokul [civetcat]. You know that certain creatures possess certain kinds of smell, good or bad. This is nothing but the secretion of hormones from certain glands. The glandular secretions of the musk rat emit a bad smell. While moving, the musk rat emits a foul smell particularly from the secretion of its lymphatic glands, which distresses the human nose. Due to differences in their hormones, the pungent smell that emanates from a tigerʼs body does not exude from the body of a cat. This smell can be perceived to a very small degree from the body of a wildcat (ban-beŕál). You will scarcely notice this in a khat́t́ásh (or kat́ash). Yet you would notice an odour in a similar but comparatively smaller creature such as the bhám. Though smaller than tigers, hyenas have this bad smell about them. Certain animals with testicles emit a foul smell from the secretion of their glands, but not when their testicles are removed. So the good or bad smell indicates the smell derived from the glandular secretion of hormones. Male goats with testicles have a severe foul smell; but goats without testicles have no foul odour at all. People who consume too much of onions, garlic and meat, which are difficult to digest, emit a bad smell from the secretion of certain glands. Hence excessive intake of onions, garlic, hard-to-digest meat and certain vegetables invariably causes a bad smell in human beings.
summary: Civet cat (gandhagokul): The gokul [cat] that emits a sweet smell [gandha] is called gandhagokul [civetcat].
You will scarcely notice this in a khat́t́ásh (or kat́ash).
Hence excessive intake of onions, garlic, hard-to-digest meat and certain vegetables invariably causes a bad smell in human beings.

paragraphs.text: Those who are careful about taking food and do not allow profuse sweating will not generate a bad odour from their body. Of course, sweat itself has no smell, but when it remains on the body for more than 45 minutes, a bad odour develops. The moment the bad smell starts to develop, it is advisable to mop the sweat from the body with a towel or piece of cloth, or wash it off with water. On the other hand, persons who do yogic exercises or take part in devotional singing of kiirtana continuously for a long time secrete certain hormones from specific parts of their anáhata cakra [fourth psycho-spiritual plexus], vishuddha cakra [fifth plexus] and ájiṋá cakra [sixth plexus]. Such secretions emit a sweet fragrance similar to jasmine or ripe jackfruit (although not exactly comparable). So, devotees or yogis generally have a sentient aroma. One of the signs of pure love for God is the emanation of a sweet fragrance from the body of a devotee. When a person even in seclusion tries to feel the spiritual proximity of Parama Puruśa, they can feel the presence of a sweet fragrance wafting across the nose. This is in fact nothing but the sweet-smelling hormones secreted from their glands and concentrated at the tip of the nose. Although a biological phenomenon (related to bio-psychology), it can only be looked upon as the grace of the Supreme.
summary: Those who are careful about taking food and do not allow profuse sweating will not generate a bad odour from their body.
So, devotees or yogis generally have a sentient aroma.
Although a biological phenomenon (related to bio-psychology), it can only be looked upon as the grace of the Supreme.

paragraphs.text: According to natural law, there are certain creatures whose bodies emanate a fragrance similar to sweet-smelling sunned rice. The gandhagokul [civet-cat] is one such creature. This creature, which is midway between the fox and the mole of the forest, can hardly see in the daylight. Like owls, they are almost blind during the day, but are not blind at night. Since they see very little during the day and are afraid of dogs, they do not come out in the daytime. At night, when they stay somewhere for any length of time, they leave behind the sweet scent of fragrant, sunned rice.
summary: According to natural law, there are certain creatures whose bodies emanate a fragrance similar to sweet-smelling sunned rice.
Like owls, they are almost blind during the day, but are not blind at night.
At night, when they stay somewhere for any length of time, they leave behind the sweet scent of fragrant, sunned rice.

paragraphs.text: The gandhagokul [civet-cat] is a creature of the Ráŕh region. Once they could be found in large numbers in Burdwan, Medinipur, Bankura and Manbhum districts; but because of human oppression they are about to become extinct. By nature they are timid. That is why people often slay them. If arrangements are not made to safeguard their lives, in the near future they will disappear from the face of the earth.
summary: The gandhagokul [civet-cat] is a creature of the Ráŕh region.
By nature they are timid.
If arrangements are not made to safeguard their lives, in the near future they will disappear from the face of the earth.

paragraphs.text: By comparison, in order to save them from danger, nature has given to some helpless creatures the power to exude a foul smell through glandular secretions. The llama, which is an animal of the camel group, feels endangered when attacked by enemies and emanates a very foul smell from its body, due to the secretion of hormones from its glands. Due to that foul smell, the enemy is compelled to run away. ( 3 )
summary: By comparison, in order to save them from danger, nature has given to some helpless creatures the power to exude a foul smell through glandular secretions.
The llama, which is an animal of the camel group, feels endangered when attacked by enemies and emanates a very foul smell from its body, due to the secretion of hormones from its glands.
Due to that foul smell, the enemy is compelled to run away.

paragraphs.text: The meaning of the word otu is “one who hunts a scent”, and gandhotu means “someone who preys upon a creature by their scent”. Cats or animals of the cat family usually prey upon something or someone. So in the etymological sense, gandhotu means, “one who preys by scent” or “creatures of the cat family”. In common usage, gandhotu means bhám [the civet cat].
summary: The meaning of the word otu is “one who hunts a scent”, and gandhotu means “someone who preys upon a creature by their scent”.
So in the etymological sense, gandhotu means, “one who preys by scent” or “creatures of the cat family”.
In common usage, gandhotu means bhám [the civet cat].

paragraphs.text: The Royal Bengal Tiger of the Sundarbans, the black tigers and jaguars of South America, the panthers and the leopards, all belong to the cat family. Of course, the original cheetahs became extinct about fifty years ago. Smaller than these cheetahs are the gobághá or hárols or bigobá, in English they are called hyenas and in Sanskrit tarakśu. These gobághá or hyenas are smaller in size than normal tigers. Hence they are afraid of adult humans. Next to them [in size] are the bháms. Smaller than bhám cats are the pole cats (khát́t́ás ) and even smaller are the wild cats (bon-beŕál), our known kuṋdo beŕál, domesticated cats (the tomcat and the female cat – meni beŕál). Beginning with the Royal Bengal Tiger up to the civet cat, they are all very similar in appearance and nature. They emit a very foul odour from their body. The kat́ás, bon-beŕál and kuṋdo-beŕáls are smaller in size. In addition, they eat food other than meat. Hence their bodies barely emit any strong odour … in fact, they have almost no smell at all. ( 4 )
summary: The Royal Bengal Tiger of the Sundarbans, the black tigers and jaguars of South America, the panthers and the leopards, all belong to the cat family.
Smaller than bhám cats are the pole cats (khát́t́ás ) and even smaller are the wild cats (bon-beŕál), our known kuṋdo beŕál, domesticated cats (the tomcat and the female cat – meni beŕál).
Hence their bodies barely emit any strong odour … in fact, they have almost no smell at all.

paragraphs.text: Royal Bengal Tiger: The second meaning of the word karvara is “proud animal” or “large tiger”. Another name for what we call “Royal Bengal tiger” in English, kuṋdo bágh in Bengali, is karvara. It is the largest member of the cat family. Among its various traits are its keen intelligence and its powerful sense of smell. It is able to ascertain which animals are found in each direction by checking the wind.
summary: Royal Bengal Tiger: The second meaning of the word karvara is “proud animal” or “large tiger”.
It is the largest member of the cat family.
It is able to ascertain which animals are found in each direction by checking the wind.

paragraphs.text: Although they are much stronger than humans, they are much less intelligent, and they know this. So if they catch a human scent in the wind, they prefer not to tread that path. However, if they happen on a person unexpectedly, they will attack them out of a sense of self-preservation. There are a small number of karvara tigers who, despite belonging to the same family, develop a taste for human flesh by eating dead bodies in burial grounds or in the forest. Some can no longer struggle with other animals in their old age, and therefore kill and eat human beings because humans cannot run from them or match them in physical strength. It is very easy for them to kill humans, so those karvara tigers who become man-eaters in this way, and remain so for a long time, undergo some physical changes. Their snout becomes comparatively long and their stomach becomes thinner. If people are aware of which Bengal tigers are man-eaters and which are not, they can take more precautionary measures. ( 5 )
summary: Although they are much stronger than humans, they are much less intelligent, and they know this.
Some can no longer struggle with other animals in their old age, and therefore kill and eat human beings because humans cannot run from them or match them in physical strength.
If people are aware of which Bengal tigers are man-eaters and which are not, they can take more precautionary measures.
