paragraphs.text: The elephant is very capricious. Many years ago I once fell victim to the whims of an elephant and was in deep trouble (nestnábud: nástánábud used in Bengali is incorrect; either nistnábud or nestnábud can be used). It was towards the end of the month of Áshvin or the beginning of Kárttik [mid-October]. I ( 1 ) had gone to Arrah to take part in a conference. At that time Arrah was the headquarters of Sahabad District. In ancient times, the northern part of Sahabad District was known as Árańyadesh (the name Arrah originated from that], and the southern part was known as Rohitarájya (named after King Harishchandraʼs son, Rohitáshva). To the north of Sahabad lay the Gauṋgá, on its eastern border was the Sone River, on its western border the Karmanáshá River and to the south the Vindhya Mountains. When emperor Akbar divided his empire into fifteen subáh [provinces], he cut a portion from the province of Bengal and created a new province which he named Bihar. Sahabad was a district in that province; Arrah was its headquarters. Shershah Surii was an illustrious son of Sahabad; his tomb is in Sasaram. (Actually Sahasrarám or Sahasrám or Sasaram comes from the name Sahasraram Singh.)
summary: The elephant is very capricious.

In ancient times, the northern part of Sahabad District was known as Árańyadesh (the name Arrah originated from that], and the southern part was known as Rohitarájya (named after King Harishchandraʼs son, Rohitáshva).
(Actually Sahasrarám or Sahasrám or Sasaram comes from the name Sahasraram Singh.

paragraphs.text: The name Sahabad comes from Shershah; the Paraganá [former administrative division in India] within Malda District, which contained Gaoŕa, the capital of Bengal, was named Shershahabad Paragana after Shershah. Although it is the headquarters of a very large district, Arrah is a mid-sized rather than a very large city. However, it has a flourishing market.
summary: The name Sahabad comes from Shershah; the Paraganá [former administrative division in India] within Malda District, which contained Gaoŕa, the capital of Bengal, was named Shershahabad Paragana after Shershah.
Although it is the headquarters of a very large district, Arrah is a mid-sized rather than a very large city.
However, it has a flourishing market.

paragraphs.text: When I got down at Arrah station, I saw that a large procession was there to take me from the station. It had elephants at the front and behind them horses, behind the horses motorcycles and behind the motorcycles rows of bicycles. The elephant that had been chosen for me was an aerávat [a very big elephant like the renowned mammoth] of a local mahárájá [king]. It was tall and imposing with a litter on its back. On the litter was the mahárájáʼs throne, fashioned of silver and studded with jewels.
summary: When I got down at Arrah station, I saw that a large procession was there to take me from the station.
The elephant that had been chosen for me was an aerávat [a very big elephant like the renowned mammoth] of a local mahárájá [king].
On the litter was the mahárájáʼs throne, fashioned of silver and studded with jewels.

paragraphs.text: The elephant was sitting to the north of the station. Even though he was sitting, I needed a ladder to be able to climb up. On the litter, a silver wall encircled the throne. On the wall there were small, coloured bulbs to magnify the resplendence of the procession.
summary: The elephant was sitting to the north of the station.
On the litter, a silver wall encircled the throne.
On the wall there were small, coloured bulbs to magnify the resplendence of the procession.

paragraphs.text: The procession started off in a timely fashion. We were going down Arrahʼs main market road with the band out in front. The grandeur of the procession was especially worth seeing. When the elderly people saw it, they said that the city of Arrah had never before seen such a colourful procession. And such a magnificently decorated elephant had never passed through there before. Several motorcycles were travelling beside me. In front was the car that had been arranged for me. At the right moment the bulbs around me lit up. It increased the radiance indeed, but the heat of the bulbs in that month of October made me damp with sweat. It was my first experience of such a fierce radiance.
summary: The procession started off in a timely fashion.
Several motorcycles were travelling beside me.
It was my first experience of such a fierce radiance.

paragraphs.text: The procession continued on and on. Travelling along the public thoroughfare to the beat of the band, the elephantʼs bulky feet began to dance. Its speed slackened. With its dancing beat, the mahout at the front and myself behind were bouncing up and down incessantly.
summary: The procession continued on and on.
Travelling along the public thoroughfare to the beat of the band, the elephantʼs bulky feet began to dance.
With its dancing beat, the mahout at the front and myself behind were bouncing up and down incessantly.

paragraphs.text: We were going along well. There were a great number of people taking part in the procession. Their loud noise rent the skies.
summary: We were going along well.
There were a great number of people taking part in the procession.
Their loud noise rent the skies.

paragraphs.text: But providence is unfavourable!
summary: But providence is unfavourable!

paragraphs.text: Suddenly I saw an electric wire running from one side [of the road] to the other. Its height was a little lower than that of the elephant. The litter was even higher, and still higher was the throne. And on top of that, there I was, even higher still!
summary: Suddenly I saw an electric wire running from one side [of the road] to the other.
The litter was even higher, and still higher was the throne.
And on top of that, there I was, even higher still!

paragraphs.text: The danger was right in front of us. If four feet or so could have been cut off from the legs of the elephant from the ground upwards, then perhaps it might have been possible to avoid the danger of the wire, but that would also create a problem. If its legs were cut, then the elephant would no longer be able to move, let alone dance. The mahout was beating the elephant on its head with the goad, saying, “Sit Sam, sit Sam, sit Sam.” Who was listening to whom? The elephant was at that moment in another world. He was busy dancing to the beat of the band. The command of the mahout did not even reach his ears.
summary: The danger was right in front of us.
” Who was listening to whom?
The command of the mahout did not even reach his ears.

paragraphs.text: The participants in the procession sensed the impending danger. One of them quickly took off his dhoti and folded it. Four strong men caught each of the four corners of the folded dhoti with their two hands holding on tightly. Incidentally, the men of Arrah district are very tall. Most of them are strong as well. Having presently been divided into two pieces, the northern part of Shahabad district is called Bhojpur; its headquarters remains in Arrah. The southern part is named Rohatas with its headquarters at Sasaram. Many of you have heard about the strength and bravery of the people of Bhojpur; and the water of Rohatas Districtʼs Bhavuya subdivision is the best [water] in all of Bihar for aiding digestion.
summary: The participants in the procession sensed the impending danger.
Most of them are strong as well.
Many of you have heard about the strength and bravery of the people of Bhojpur; and the water of Rohatas Districtʼs Bhavuya subdivision is the best [water] in all of Bihar for aiding digestion.

paragraphs.text: Hence there is no scope for doubting that the people are strong. But for me to jump down from such a height, they had to use all their strength to hold on to the four corners of the dhoti so that those corners would not come out of their hands from the impact of my body. The distortion that comes in the face from employing excessive force was evident in their faces. You must be familiar with this kind of grimace. It is more or less this type of grimace that occurs when one is getting ready to brace for the pain before giving blood or getting an injection. I could see that they were hanging on to the corners of the dhoti with all their might, so I was not worried. At least I knew that if I jumped onto the dhoti, their hands would not slacken and cause me fall to the ground. Just to the side of the men that were holding the dhoti stood several strong young men of twenty-four or twenty-five years of age. They had their hands upraised and were saying: “Donʼt jump onto the dhoti; jump on us instead. We will catch you.”
summary: Hence there is no scope for doubting that the people are strong.
It is more or less this type of grimace that occurs when one is getting ready to brace for the pain before giving blood or getting an injection.
They had their hands upraised and were saying: “Donʼt jump onto the dhoti; jump on us instead.

paragraphs.text: On one side I was looking at those holding the dhoti and on the other the boys with their upraised hands. Then I asked: “Why is the car over there? What is the harm if I jump onto the hood of the car?” All of them together broke out in a clamour, saying “no, no.” Their contention was that the hood of the car was made of hard metal. I might get hurt if I jumped onto it.
summary: On one side I was looking at those holding the dhoti and on the other the boys with their upraised hands.
” All of them together broke out in a clamour, saying “no, no.
I might get hurt if I jumped onto it.

paragraphs.text: By this time the elephant was almost right up to the wire, hardly ten cubits [4.6 metres] away. A delay of about one more minute and the elephant would run into the wire. A terrible accident would ensue.
summary: By this time the elephant was almost right up to the wire, hardly ten cubits [4.
A delay of about one more minute and the elephant would run into the wire.
A terrible accident would ensue.

paragraphs.text: I looked at those holding the dhoti, and then I looked at the boys with their upraised arms. Then I looked at the car. Jumping onto the hood of the car would be honorable. Then again, jumping onto the dhoti would be honorable as well. Jumping onto the boys would not be honorable because one or another of the boys could break their hand; someone could also sprain or break a finger. I could see that everyone was ready, waiting for me to jump. The readiness [reflected] on the faces of those holding the dhoti was something to behold. They gave a loud cry: “Jay Bábá, Jay Bábá, Jay Bábá!” I stood up from the throne and climbed up on the silver walls that encircled me. I was then about two stories above the ground. My childhood friend, Shamsu (Shamsujjaman Mallik), who was standing on one side of the elephant, was repeating the name ‘Bismillah’ over and over for my safety. From one edge of the throne, I jumped from the silver wall adorned with bulbs.
summary: I looked at those holding the dhoti, and then I looked at the boys with their upraised arms.
The readiness [reflected] on the faces of those holding the dhoti was something to behold.
From one edge of the throne, I jumped from the silver wall adorned with bulbs.

paragraphs.text: But then... what happened then? Did I survive that journey? Yes, I did indeed survive, but there was a little ‘mishap’. It was the end of Áshvin or the beginning of Kárttik, the month of October. For the holidays at that time, I was wearing a brand new, gold-threaded Shantipuri dhoti given to me by my paternal uncle. When I jumped I failed to notice that one corner of my dhoti had become stuck on one of the pointed ends of the throne. So I jumped, but a piece of the dhoti about two cubits long caught on the pointed end and became completely torn up and ruined. Alas, that brand new, gold-threaded, Shantipuri dhoti!
summary: Did I survive that journey?
For the holidays at that time, I was wearing a brand new, gold-threaded Shantipuri dhoti given to me by my paternal uncle.
Alas, that brand new, gold-threaded, Shantipuri dhoti!

paragraphs.text: I landed on the hand-held dhoti. The amount of force they exerted was written on their faces. With the shout of “Jay Bábá!” everyone had become anxious. This was their victory as well. I did not fall on the ground. They had caught me. The bhukti pradhán [district secretary] of Arrah was standing just to the side. He rushed over and caught me again, opening the car door and putting me inside, then closing the door behind me. I looked and saw the thrill of victory and sigh of relief on the faces of the boys who had held the dhoti. The boys who had their hands upraised said with regret: “Why didnʼt you jump on us? It would have been fine!”
summary: I landed on the hand-held dhoti.
I did not fall on the ground.
It would have been fine!

paragraphs.text: I looked and saw that the elephant was by then about two cubits away from running into the electric wire. The elephant was still dancing, even though the band had stopped [playing] earlier.
summary: I looked and saw that the elephant was by then about two cubits away from running into the electric wire.
The elephant was still dancing, even though the band had stopped [playing] earlier.

paragraphs.text: Not only the elephant was dancing, the whole procession was dancing to the beat. The beat was not dying out at all. The beginning of the Bhojpuri song that they were singing is still dancing in my mind.
summary: Not only the elephant was dancing, the whole procession was dancing to the beat.
The beat was not dying out at all.
The beginning of the Bhojpuri song that they were singing is still dancing in my mind.

” Harassed and beaten, this time the elephant sat down.

The elephant was sitting down, but his trunk was now dancing to the same beat that his feet had been dancing to before. The members of the procession had formed a circle around him, all of them dancing to that same beat. Their joyful sound, their booming “Jay” and the stanzas of their song, were reverberating throughout the atmosphere:

paragraphs.text: Birds and Animals, Our Neighbours [a compilation]
summary: Birds and Animals, Our Neighbours [a compilation]

footnotes.text: ‘I’ in the story is the author himself. –Trans.
The foregoing twenty-two paragraphs are from Shabda Cayaniká Part 13, Discourse 94.

paragraphs.text: According to ancient Puranic legend, on the western bank of the spot where the Náráyańii and Gańd́aka rivers met the Ganges River, a huge elephant and a huge turtle, symbolizing Hari [Lord Krśńa] and Hara [Lord Shiva] respectively, fought a duel. The people came there to organize a big fair annually on the full moon day in the Bengali month of Kárttika [in October during autumn]. Humans, birds and animals dear to Lord Shiva all crowded there together. In order to attract more people, shops were set up for buying and selling food items. People used to gather there in large numbers. Various animals from different parts of the country and abroad, such as elephants, camels, horses, cows, buffaloes, goats and sheep, were brought together at the fair. No other such fair was known to be held anywhere in the world until that time. That fair at the Hari-Hara ground continues to be held even today on the autumnal full moon day.
summary: According to ancient Puranic legend, on the western bank of the spot where the Náráyańii and Gańd́aka rivers met the Ganges River, a huge elephant and a huge turtle, symbolizing Hari [Lord Krśńa] and Hara [Lord Shiva] respectively, fought a duel.
People used to gather there in large numbers.
That fair at the Hari-Hara ground continues to be held even today on the autumnal full moon day.

paragraphs.text: To the north of the fairground, the rail lines stretch from Hazipur junction to Sonepur junction. Close to the fairground is a huge mango orchard. To the east of the ground is the Náráyańii-Gańd́ak, and beyond it is Vaishali district with Hazipur as the district headquarters. The spot falls under the jurisdiction of Sonepur Police station in Chapra district of Bihar. To the south of this place flows the river Ganges, and the ghat is popularly known as Pahleja Ghat. To the west lies the rest of Chapra district. Although the common language of Chapra district is Bhojpuri, the language of the Sonepur police station area is Bajjiká Maithili.
summary: To the north of the fairground, the rail lines stretch from Hazipur junction to Sonepur junction.
The spot falls under the jurisdiction of Sonepur Police station in Chapra district of Bihar.
Although the common language of Chapra district is Bhojpuri, the language of the Sonepur police station area is Bajjiká Maithili.

paragraphs.text: [As mentioned earlier], for a long time this has been the largest animal fair in the world. Now I am told that in Russia, near Moscow, a similar large animal fair is held. That fair is known to be even larger than the fair on Hazipur fairground nowadays. It is very likely because, with the abolition of the zamindary system, there is hardly any customer for elephants, although there are a few sellers. Few elephants are brought for sale. Is it only because of this? Even if the zamindary system had remained, the import of elephants would still have declined, because elephants are fast being replaced by four-wheeled jeeps. Yet is this the only reason? The elephant consumes every week twenty maunds ( 1 ) of branches, twigs and leaves of trees. During their stay in the forest, an elephant spoils about sixty maunds of such vegetation per week. Every week the elephant has to be provided with eight maunds of rice and half a maund of clarified butter. A mahout has to be employed to tend the elephant. Lest the elephantʼs head turns hot, it has to be regularly bathed in water. The jeep has no such problems. Other than expenses for petrol or diesel and occasional servicing, no other incurring expenditure is involved in its maintenance.
summary: [As mentioned earlier], for a long time this has been the largest animal fair in the world.
Yet is this the only reason?
Other than expenses for petrol or diesel and occasional servicing, no other incurring expenditure is involved in its maintenance.

paragraphs.text: The import of horses has also declined; those who once used them for transport are now using jeeps, motorcycles, scooters, etc. There is now hardly any use for horse-drawn carriages. In its place have come petrol-operated cars and even cars operated by electricity. So the demand for horses and elephants has declined. The use of camels has also decreased, although not by much. As before, the people of northern India use the camel for tilling the soil even today. Whereas for tilling the land one requires at least two bullocks, only one camel will do the same job. And the camel also offers milk. Furthermore, the camel is also the ship of the desert. So the utility of the camel prevails almost as much as before. I say ‘almost’, because for drawing the plough there is increasing use of tractors. Whatever the case might be, the importance of the Hari-Hara fair has noticeably diminished. Yet the glamour of the fair is still there. On account of this animal fair at Hari-Hara grounds, the railway platform of the Sonepur station was once the longest platform in India, probably in the world. Now I learnt that the platform of the Kharagpur station of the South Eastern Railway has wrested that glory. This is quite likely. ( 2 )
summary: The import of horses has also declined; those who once used them for transport are now using jeeps, motorcycles, scooters, etc.
Furthermore, the camel is also the ship of the desert.
This is quite likely.

footnotes.text: One imperial maund weighed 82.28 pounds. At different times in history the weight of a maund has ranged from 25 to 85 pounds.
The foregoing four paragraphs are from Shabda Cayaniká Part 15, Discourse 113.

chapters.title: How Far is Animal Slaughter Justifiable?

paragraphs.text: In ancient times any secretive slaughter of animals was considered an act of cowardice. Any animal that had less strength than a human being was not directly slaughtered; it was given the opportunity to fight a battle. That was the prevalent system in the pre-Buddhist era. In the Buddhist and post-Buddhist periods, although animal slaughter was not entirely banned, any slaughter of animals on religious grounds was condemned. In a society influenced by the Jain religion, not only for the sake of religion but even for consumption, animal slaughter was considered a lowly and mean act. However, as I was saying, in the pre-Buddhist period, slaughtering an animal secretly was considered a mean act, although people of those days in the name of religion and for the sake of food slaughtered animals and birds.
summary: In ancient times any secretive slaughter of animals was considered an act of cowardice.
In the Buddhist and post-Buddhist periods, although animal slaughter was not entirely banned, any slaughter of animals on religious grounds was condemned.

However, as I was saying, in the pre-Buddhist period, slaughtering an animal secretly was considered a mean act, although people of those days in the name of religion and for the sake of food slaughtered animals and birds.

paragraphs.text: Although they uttered the prayer Sarvaḿ khalvidaḿ Brahma [“Let everyone live in happiness”], yet in the name of religion they committed animal slaughter. They did not oppose the slaughter of innocent animals; in fact, they even supported it. This is quite regrettable. Maybe in those days the mindset of the people was such that the time was not yet ripe for reflecting about animals, birds and plants. Yet there were certain restrictions on animal slaughter. Animal slaughter and meat eating were not permitted on every religious occasion; female animals could not be slaughtered. Domesticated animals could not be slaughtered without giving them the opportunity to give battle. Fish could be caught in a net but could not be caught by using fishing bait or by tempting them with food. Those who did not observe these restrictions were called kut́aka. Forests where animal slaughter was forbidden were known as mrgadáva or sanctuaries (nirbhaya kánan, just as one near Varanasi adjacent to Sarnath was Rśi-pattan Mrgadáva; in the Prákrt language it is called Iśi-pattan Mrgadáva). Those who secretly killed any animal in these protected areas (mrgadávas) were also known as kut́akas. Those who took to this secret killing of animals – their nature was known as kaot́akika. For the word kaot́akika in its etymological sense, one could even use the expression kaot́ika.
summary: Although they uttered the prayer Sarvaḿ khalvidaḿ Brahma [“Let everyone live in happiness”], yet in the name of religion they committed animal slaughter.
Domesticated animals could not be slaughtered without giving them the opportunity to give battle.
For the word kaot́akika in its etymological sense, one could even use the expression kaot́ika.

paragraphs.text: In common usage, the word kaot́akika would mean “the secret killer of animals”. Those who killed animals without letting anyone know, who disobeyed state injunctions and killed animals secretly (meaning the poachers), those who killed weak animals without giving them the opportunity to defend themselves (that is, the butchers) – all these were known as kaot́akikas.Those who killed animals publicly or secretly, who killed birds and beasts by giving them the opportunity to defend themselves or without giving them any such opportunity, who defied state injunction and killed animals secretively or in secret places, were also called kaotilika (kutilika + ań). They were looked down upon as mean people in the society. ( 1 )
summary: In common usage, the word kaot́akika would mean “the secret killer of animals”.

Those who killed animals publicly or secretly, who killed birds and beasts by giving them the opportunity to defend themselves or without giving them any such opportunity, who defied state injunction and killed animals secretively or in secret places, were also called kaotilika (kutilika + ań).
They were looked down upon as mean people in the society.

paragraphs.text: In ancient times, to please the gods, offerings made by human beings were called grihabali; not only offerings to the gods but even offerings addressed to the forefathers or to please ghosts and spirits were also known as grihabali. Human nature is such that whatever one likes to eat, one believes that others also like to eat the same.
summary: In ancient times, to please the gods, offerings made by human beings were called grihabali; not only offerings to the gods but even offerings addressed to the forefathers or to please ghosts and spirits were also known as grihabali.
Human nature is such that whatever one likes to eat, one believes that others also like to eat the same.

paragraphs.text: One of my distant aunts would invariably offer to a highly placed guest in her house fried cakes of poppy-seeds along with other food items, the reason for which can be easily surmised. Similarly, in those days whatever items people liked to eat, they used to offer them as sacrificial offerings – such as the goat, the buffalo the horse, the heart and liver, and barley. (They came across fine rice and wheat a little later). Not only among the Aryans of those days, but also among people of other religious beliefs in later times, the practice of animal sacrifice persisted. Still later, the whole affair turned into a case of individual liking or preference – whatever they liked, they sacrificed in the name of the gods, ancestors and spirits only nominally, but in reality it was to satisfy their craving to eat those items.
summary: One of my distant aunts would invariably offer to a highly placed guest in her house fried cakes of poppy-seeds along with other food items, the reason for which can be easily surmised.
(They came across fine rice and wheat a little later).

Still later, the whole affair turned into a case of individual liking or preference – whatever they liked, they sacrificed in the name of the gods, ancestors and spirits only nominally, but in reality it was to satisfy their craving to eat those items.

paragraphs.text: Consider a situation where, on the occasion of a religious ceremony, animal sacrifice had still not taken place yet all the arrangements, such as fixing the number of persons to be invited, how many would be offered meat, and so forth, were made beforehand. Verbally it was declared that the animals were being freed from animal life. This [slaughter] of their own dear animals was treated as a sacrifice. We people of common intelligence hardly understand the meaning of this kind of sacrifice. How, by doing harm to someone or putting an end to someoneʼs life, can the [so-called] glory of sacrifice be attained by human beings? It is beyond our common understanding. Is not that sacrifice wherein one gives up something of oneʼs very own the real sacrifice? Is not feasting [with the meat of a sacrificed animal] the rich people or oneʼs own people and hoping to achieve some kind of holiness similar to living in a foolʼs paradise? Is not someone committing these acts at the cost of othersʼ lives?
summary: Consider a situation where, on the occasion of a religious ceremony, animal sacrifice had still not taken place yet all the arrangements, such as fixing the number of persons to be invited, how many would be offered meat, and so forth, were made beforehand.

paragraphs.text: Growth in the animal population takes place in three ways. First mammals grow in the motherʼs womb in a membrane (placenta), and after attaining their full size they become restless in the womb and are born with the placenta tied to the navel. The nurse severs the link between the navel of the baby and the placenta, which we can describe as analogous to the shell of an egg. Just as the interior of the egg is covered with a shell, the embryo of the mammal similarly remains encased in a placenta. In spoken language this placenta is called phul (in Nepali language the egg is called phul). The life of a child-bearing woman is endangered if the placenta takes a long time to come out of the womb, after the birth of the child. After the placenta comes out of the womb, it is either burnt or buried in the ground [in traditional societies.] For the proper extrication of this placenta, there are certain homeopathic medicines. In ancient Indian therapeutics, certain instruments were recommended or used for extricating the dead baby from the womb, for bringing out the placenta, or for bringing out the live baby from the womb; they were called garbhashauṋku.
summary: Growth in the animal population takes place in three ways.
In spoken language this placenta is called phul (in Nepali language the egg is called phul).

In ancient Indian therapeutics, certain instruments were recommended or used for extricating the dead baby from the womb, for bringing out the placenta, or for bringing out the live baby from the womb; they were called garbhashauṋku.

paragraphs.text: These mammals have to depend on the motherʼs milk after their birth. If the baby continues to be fed wholly on the motherʼs milk, without being given any other food for quite some time, it will still be hale and hearty, just like the children of cows, buffaloes and other animals. That which comes out of the motherʼs body as milk essence, which is a metamorphosed form of motherʼs blood, is termed as stan – root verb + yat suffix = stanna. Stan + ac = Stan [breast] means “the motherʼs milk which provides essential calcium for the nutritional well-being of the baby”. Be it formula milk, milk from the midwife, powdered milk, or the milk of the female donkey – none is comparable to the motherʼs milk. So, those who deprive the baby of motherʼs milk do maximum harm to the baby. How much humans or animals are indebted to their mother becomes evident from the fact that right from the earliest stage in the womb, the blood and vitality of the baby comes from the motherʼs body. Even after birth, for quite some time the baby is nourished from motherʼs milk which was transmuted from the motherʼs blood. So in ancient India, probably for this reason, the father is compared to heaven by saying:

paragraphs.text: The transformation from oviparous creatures to mammals has led to significant complexities in the animal body. In some countries of the world there are animals which are midway between the oviparous and the mammal stage. The (duckbill) platypus is such a creature. Closely related to the cat; the duckbill (platypus) lays eggs, yet it is a mammal. Bats are much closer to mammals than the duckbill (platypus). They give birth to young ones, which remain in an immature state after birth. Akin to the bat order – perhaps its sub-order – is the vampire [bird; Geospiza nebulosa or sharp-beaked finch] and the titmouse (cámciká). These two belong to the same order. Whether they are oviparous or mammalian, the progeny of all creatures remain helpless after birth for some time. The home for these helpless babies is the “lying-in-room” or “birthing room”. The newborn child is entirely helpless – frail and helpless (árta or átura). That is why the birthing room is called the room for the helpless; in colloquial Bengali it is called áturghar (áturálaya) or “sick-room”.

If the baby does not cry, it should be understood that it has little chance of survival. So, the mild sound of the first cry of the human or animal baby is the very sign of life.

Although there is no objection to carrying loads for those who are accustomed to it, they must not stoop over to lift a heavy load onto their heads. It is better if others will help them to lift it up. In this stage of pregnancy a daily bath is a rule, but one must not bathe after sunset. It is better to lie down on a hard bed.

chapters.title: Renaissance in All the Strata / Economic and Constitutional Guarantees for Animalsʼ Rights

paragraphs.text: The subject of todayʼs discourse is, “Renaissance in all the strata of life.”
summary: The subject of todayʼs discourse is, “Renaissance in all the strata of life.

paragraphs.text: The real meaning of the word “renaissance” is reawakening. That is, humanity was sleeping, and now it must wake up from the cimmerian slumber and do something in all the spheres of life, in all the strata of existence.
summary: The real meaning of the word “renaissance” is reawakening.
That is, humanity was sleeping, and now it must wake up from the cimmerian slumber and do something in all the spheres of life, in all the strata of existence.

paragraphs.text: There are three important strata in life: the physical stratum, the psychic stratum and the spiritual stratum. In the physical stratum, there are many strata: say, scientific achievement, social progress, political life, economic life, culture life. People often say that this twentieth century is the century of science. No, it is not the truth. Human life has been associated with science from the prehistoric era, from the very birth of humanity on this earth about one million years ago, and not only in this twentieth century. And as long as there will be a single human being, there will be an age of science.
summary: There are three important strata in life: the physical stratum, the psychic stratum and the spiritual stratum.
No, it is not the truth.
And as long as there will be a single human being, there will be an age of science.

paragraphs.text: Nowadays science means creating new weapons – strengthening the hands of warmongers; but the spirit of science should not be like this, and at the start, in the primordial phase of human life, it was not so. Yes, there is necessity of weapons – weapons not for strengthening the hands of warmongers, but for providing security for good ideas, good thoughts and good persons.
summary: Nowadays science means creating new weapons – strengthening the hands of warmongers; but the spirit of science should not be like this, and at the start, in the primordial phase of human life, it was not so.
Yes, there is necessity of weapons – weapons not for strengthening the hands of warmongers, but for providing security for good ideas, good thoughts and good persons.

paragraphs.text: Science should be just like art: science for service and beatitude. Art for service and beatitude, I said; and now I say, science is also for service and beatitude. Science should always be utilized for the proper progress of human society.
summary: Science should be just like art: science for service and beatitude.
Art for service and beatitude, I said; and now I say, science is also for service and beatitude.
Science should always be utilized for the proper progress of human society.

paragraphs.text: Then the social. In the social sphere there are several sub-strata, and the real spirit of social progress is to dispel all social disparities. Each and every member of the human society should enjoy equal rights as members of the same family, but there is disparity and it is the duty of the Renaissance movement to dispel the disparity and bring about equality, equilibrium and equipoise amongst human beings.
summary: In the social sphere there are several sub-strata, and the real spirit of social progress is to dispel all social disparities.

Each and every member of the human society should enjoy equal rights as members of the same family, but there is disparity and it is the duty of the Renaissance movement to dispel the disparity and bring about equality, equilibrium and equipoise amongst human beings.

paragraphs.text: There are disparities, disparities of different types and different kinds. For instance, there are biological disparities existing in the society, which are being encouraged by certain selfish persons. The biological disparity between human and animal, between human and plant, between animal and plant – that disparity must not be there. Just as a human being wants to survive, a pigeon also wants to survive – similarly a cow also wants to survive, or a tree. Just as my life is dear to me, so the lives of created beings are also equally dear to them. It is the birthright of human beings to live in this world, and it is the birthright of the animal world and plant world also to remain on this earth. To recognize this right, and to get it recognized by the entire human society, the Renaissance movement will have to do something concrete.
summary: There are disparities, disparities of different types and different kinds.
Just as a human being wants to survive, a pigeon also wants to survive – similarly a cow also wants to survive, or a tree.
To recognize this right, and to get it recognized by the entire human society, the Renaissance movement will have to do something concrete.

paragraphs.text: Then there are physico-psychic ailments. Some people argue that animals have been created by Parama Puruśa for our food. I knew a certain person who used to say that if people do not eat goatsʼ meat, the world would become populated only by goats. And others said that if people do not eat chickens, there would not be even a single inch of space on this earth – it would be filled with chickens! Now my point is, even though human beings do not eat vultures, is there a crowd of vultures in the world? How foolish such people are! People do not eat earthworms – has there been an uncontrollable growth of earthworms on earth? Only out of excessive greed, people eat chickens and goats and are simply searching for logic to support their actions and cover up their weakness. This sort of cunning will not do. In the mobility of the psychic world, there are certain defective thoughts prevailing – that we humans are destined to rule this earth, and the creatures are destined to be ruled by us. You will have to fight against this type of psychology with the help of your strong weapon. What is that weapon? Neohumanism. All have the equal right to live here: this universe is for all. It is not the patrimony of human beings only. This is also the duty of renaissance people. ( 1 )
summary: Then there are physico-psychic ailments.
Only out of excessive greed, people eat chickens and goats and are simply searching for logic to support their actions and cover up their weakness.
This is also the duty of renaissance people.

It helps the existential faculty reach the pinnacled state.
Neohumanism will bring equality in the social sphere and remove all sorts of disparities, therefore human progress will be greatly accelerated.

paragraphs.text: When PROUT and Neohumanism are established, the whole existence of human beings will become effulgent in the attainment of the Supreme.
summary: When PROUT and Neohumanism are established, the whole existence of human beings will become effulgent in the attainment of the Supreme.

paragraphs.text: At present human beings are thinking about their own minimum requirements more than about the minimum requirements of animals and plants. A day is coming when some of the animals, if not all, will come within the realm of our social membership. Today we say that each and every human being will get the minimum requirements. Tomorrow we will say that the minimum requirements will also include the needs of dogs, cows, monkeys, etc. To fulfil these requirements, there should be more and more production.
summary: At present human beings are thinking about their own minimum requirements more than about the minimum requirements of animals and plants.
Today we say that each and every human being will get the minimum requirements.
To fulfil these requirements, there should be more and more production.

paragraphs.text: The earth is not only for human beings, it is for other living beings also. So we will have to do something for them. The minimum requirements and maximum amenities should also be given to animals. Today cows, dogs and monkeys are developing; tomorrow more and more animals will be in this category. Animals will also develop longings for different psycho-physical pabula, so they should be guaranteed minimum requirements and maximum amenities too. We will have to do something for them also. This is the demand of Neohumanism, of Neo-Humanistic ideas. This demand should be fulfilled by PROUT. ( 2 )
summary: The earth is not only for human beings, it is for other living beings also.
Animals will also develop longings for different psycho-physical pabula, so they should be guaranteed minimum requirements and maximum amenities too.
This demand should be fulfilled by PROUT.

paragraphs.text: Charter of Rights

The formation of a World Government will require a world constitution. A charter of principles or bill of rights should be included in such a constitution and encompass at least the following four areas. First, complete security should be guaranteed to all the plants and animals on the planet. Secondly, each country must guarantee purchasing power to all its citizens. Thirdly, the constitution should guarantee four fundamental rights – spiritual practice or Dharma; cultural legacy; education; and indigenous linguistic expression. Fourthly, if the practice of any of these rights conflicts with cardinal human values then that practice should be immediately curtailed. That is, cardinal human values must take precedence over all other rights. All the constitutions of the world suffer from numerous defects. The above points may be adopted by the framers of different constitutions to overcome these defects. ( 3 )
summary: The formation of a World Government will require a world constitution.
Thirdly, the constitution should guarantee four fundamental rights – spiritual practice or Dharma; cultural legacy; education; and indigenous linguistic expression.
The above points may be adopted by the framers of different constitutions to overcome these defects.

paragraphs.text: I have already told you how spiritual aspirants should live their lives. I have said that a real sadhaka [spiritual aspirant] will properly discharge their duties in the relative world, and will at the same time attend properly to their duties in the spiritual world; and between the two worlds, there will be a happy blending. In the external world there should be an objective adjustment, and at the same time there should, in the psychic world, be a subjective approach.
summary: I have already told you how spiritual aspirants should live their lives.

I have said that a real sadhaka [spiritual aspirant] will properly discharge their duties in the relative world, and will at the same time attend properly to their duties in the spiritual world; and between the two worlds, there will be a happy blending.
In the external world there should be an objective adjustment, and at the same time there should, in the psychic world, be a subjective approach.

paragraphs.text: Furthermore, never forgetting that human life is an ideological flow, human beings should always move towards the supreme ideology. They have been moving in this direction since time immemorial and, through this process of movement, have reached the present stage of humanity. Passing through many lives as worms, insects, birds, and animals, they have undergone countless pains, miseries, tortures and humiliations. Take for example the life of a goat. A goat spends its life eating grass, until the day comes when the butcher grabs it, kills it, skins it and sells its flesh piece by piece in the market. That goat at one time had to live such a miserable life. But today it has forgotten all this. Through a process of forward movement, today it may have attained a human life.
summary: Furthermore, never forgetting that human life is an ideological flow, human beings should always move towards the supreme ideology.
A goat spends its life eating grass, until the day comes when the butcher grabs it, kills it, skins it and sells its flesh piece by piece in the market.
Through a process of forward movement, today it may have attained a human life.

paragraphs.text: Human life is more secure than animal life. Many animals live in the jungle where there is something to fear every minute; where the weak are the prey of the strong. To escape this atmosphere of fear and insecurity, many wild animals have sought refuge with human beings. They have been fed grass, leaves and other types of fodder until the right moment came to kill them for their flesh. Even today, this is generally what happens. Animals fully trust human beings; they trust them even up to one minute before their death. But when they see a person approaching them with a weapon in hand, they realize that those they had trusted as their friends are actually their enemies. Although human beings feed their animals, the love or attachment which they have for them is purely external. There is no genuine love in [humans]. This is how wretched animal life can be.
summary: Human life is more secure than animal life.
Animals fully trust human beings; they trust them even up to one minute before their death.
This is how wretched animal life can be.

paragraphs.text: Every human being has had to pass through that sort of painful animal life in the past. But that does not mean we should be the cause of misery for those animals who have taken shelter with us today. On the contrary, we should have a merciful attitude towards them. A woman who has been badly treated or humiliated by her mother-in-law should be careful that she does not treat her daughter-in-law in the same way. Human beings should carry out their duties properly in the external world and should always ensure that no being suffers unnecessarily from any undue mistreatment. In the physical sphere, the rights of all should be protected. Each and every human being should be guaranteed the basic necessities of life: food, clothing, medicine, shelter and education. “I wonʼt exploit anyone, and I will not allow others to exploit me.” This is the spirit of proper objective adjustment. And while this proper objective adjustment is maintained, work must continue in a progressive way. You will have to move ahead on the path of life while keeping an adjustment with the external world.
summary: Every human being has had to pass through that sort of painful animal life in the past.
In the physical sphere, the rights of all should be protected.
You will have to move ahead on the path of life while keeping an adjustment with the external world.

paragraphs.text: You must always remember that your existence is not only a physical one. It is animals who are primarily concerned with the physical world, who struggle merely to survive. Those animals which live in jungles are constantly confronted by the fear of tigers, lions, bears, elephants, snakes, crocodiles and a host of other ferocious creatures; while those which have surrendered to human beings, such as goats, sheep and cows, are confronted in the last moment of their lives with the fear of being slaughtered by a human. So it is quite obvious that animal life is less secure than human life.
summary: You must always remember that your existence is not only a physical one.

Those animals which live in jungles are constantly confronted by the fear of tigers, lions, bears, elephants, snakes, crocodiles and a host of other ferocious creatures; while those which have surrendered to human beings, such as goats, sheep and cows, are confronted in the last moment of their lives with the fear of being slaughtered by a human.
So it is quite obvious that animal life is less secure than human life.

paragraphs.text: In todayʼs world, human beings face difficulties in maintaining an objective adjustment with the physical world. As we have not yet been able to build an ideal human society, we will have to first concentrate on providing everyone with the basic requirements of life. Once that task is accomplished, we will be able to build an ideal society. To enable society to progress spiritually, people will be given sufficient scope and time for spiritual practices.
summary: In todayʼs world, human beings face difficulties in maintaining an objective adjustment with the physical world.
Once that task is accomplished, we will be able to build an ideal society.
To enable society to progress spiritually, people will be given sufficient scope and time for spiritual practices.

paragraphs.text: The subjective approach is to first withdraw the crude mind gradually from the external world and merge it in the subtle mind, and then to merge the subtle mind in unit consciousness. When unit consciousness is merged in Cosmic Consciousness, a human being is said to have attained the supreme fulfilment in life. In the present world, human beings face such tremendous difficulties in maintaining their objective adjustment that they cannot afford to give any time for their subjective approach. This is the greatest tragedy of the day! That is why I would like to advise you to build a healthy human society as early as possible, so that each and every human being gets enough scope and time for spiritual progress. ( 1 )

paragraphs.text: CAKRA: Cycle or circle; psycho-spiritual centre, or plexus. The cakras in the human body are all located along the suśumná canal which passes through the length of the spinal column and extends up to the crown of the head. Some cakras, however, are associated with external concentration points. The concentration points: (1) for the múládhára cakra, the base of the spine, above the perineum; (2) for the svádhiśt́hána, the genital organ; (3) for the mańipura, the navel; (4) for the anáhata, the midpoint of the chest; (5) for the vishuddha, the throat; (6) for the ájiṋá, between the eyebrows; and (7) for the sahasrára, the crown of the head. There are two other cakras which are needed in certain spiritual practices, so the cakras are nine in number.

paragraphs.text: SANSKRIT, SAḾSKRTA: The classical language of India. It first emerged during the Post-Shiva period, and as a spoken language it began to be supplanted by Prákrta prior to the Krśńa period. Although not a spoken language today except in very limited circumstances, it is still important for its vast literature, especially spiritual literature. Sanskrit and English are the languages of the world that have the richest vocabularies. Sanskrit pronunciation was perfected by non-Aryan Tantrics in such a way that each of the fifty letters of the Sanskrit alphabet constitutes one acoustic root of Tantra.

points.body: According to Shrii Prabhat Ranjan Sarkar, two “destructive tendencies” are predominant in the human mind: one is “intra-humanistic”, that is, the exploitation or oppression of fellow human beings; and the other is “inter-creature”, that is, the torture of animals, plants and other living beings. The inevitable result is the “catastrophic ruin of human life as well”. In both tendencies, the disease is one and the same, and it must be eradicated from the very root, the mind. Shrii Prabhat Ranjan Sarkar prescribes the only way to achieve this: bring about a radical change in the human mind on the basis of Neohumanism – by awakening genuine love for the entire living and inanimate universe. Only then will the human, plant and animal worlds be saved from extinction; and “humanity will attain the consummation of its existence.”

points.body: Starting with a series of discourses delivered in Kolkata in the early 1980ʼs, Shrii Prabhat Ranjan Sarkar began to reveal his exquisite vision for saving our imperilled world through a Neohumanistic transformation. Then in 1985 in Kolkata he began giving a remarkable series of discourses which were later compiled into more than thirty volumes in two series, Varńa Vicitrá and Shabda Cayaniká. In nearly all the volumes of those two series, he brought to the fore the issue of preserving non-human creatures, discussing the lives, natures, habitats, status and plights of various animals, birds, insects and plants. In addition he taught us how to behave with and protect these innocent creatures, and urged us all to give them the same care and attention that we give to human beings. Because according to him, all non-human creatures have the same “existential value” as do human beings.

points.body: In 1987, he instructed that those of the aforementioned discussions from those two series that were related to animals, be published in the form of a separate Bengali book, to be titled Ámáder Prativeshii Pashu o Pakśii. Thus the first edition of that book comprised of excerpts from whatever parts of the two series had been published by that time; those parts amounted to somewhat more than half of what finally came to be published. Since then there has been a long-standing demand from our esteemed readers for the publication of an English translation. The publication of the present book is a humble response to that request, and moreover includes additional information now gleaned from the volumes unpublished as of 1987 and from the early- 1980ʼs discourses mentioned above. Where the same information has come in two or more different passages from among all the volumes, normally only one passage has been included herein.

points.body: Because of the aforementioned expansion of the book, it has not been possible to follow exactly the organization of it originally given by the author; hence the responsibility for such organization, and for some of the chapter titles, now lies with the editors. In order to provide in a systematic manner a complete panorama of the authorʼs detailed discussions (originally scattered over more than thirty volumes), the present book has been divided into nine parts. Since the subterranean flow of Neohumanism permeates the book, two of the authorʼs groundbreaking discourses on this topic, both of which touch on Neohumanismʼs vast role as the panacea for all world problems, have been included in Part 1. In Parts 2 through 8, we have arranged the authorʼs descriptions of various animals, birds and insects, their species and subspecies, under different headings synchronized with the evolution of the living world from the unicellular or multi-cellular protozoa to the developed ape family. Part 9 contains the authorʼs poignant reflections on the relationship between human beings and animals.

points.body: Every new book translation starts with a draft by the main translator. It is then reviewed by a “first editor” who compares the English translation with the original Hindi or Bengali. Thereafter it is sent for “second editing” to improve the standard of English. On completion of second editing, it is sent for final verification, which includes one more comparison with the original Hindi or Bengali. Other important functions include the coordination of these different steps and the development and management of a global distribution and sales network.

points.body: Some of those who have contributed to these efforts are as follows: retired Professor Dr. Subhas Chandra Sarkar translated all the materials for the book from different parts of Varńa Vicitrá and Shabda Cayaniká, except for the materials taken for different chapters from the already-translated Shabda Cayaniká Part 1 to Part 5, and some or all of the materials for four other chapters: The second of the three “Humans Are So Cruel!” excerpts had already been translated for Neohumanism in a Nutshell Part 2. Some of the material for the “Caring for Child-Bearing Animals” chapter had already been translated for “Advice for Pregnant Women” in The Awakening of Women. “The Whimsical Elephant” was translated by Deváshiiśa for this book, and the Shabda Cayaniká Part 9 portion of the scorpion topic in the “Bugs, Scorpions, Lice and Mosquitoes” chapter was translated by Ácárya Priyashivánanda Avadhuta. The latter also did the first editing of the entire book. Gáyattrii Ghista, Táraka Ghista and Pashupati Landau did the second editing of the entire book. Kirit Dave with the help of others prepared the cover design of the book and also took on coordination of the entire project along with distribution and sales management. Dr. Vishvajita Bhoumick and Shriimati Arpitá Bhoumick prepared the appendix of Latin names for birds and animals. Dr. Vishvajita Bhoumick also helped to proofread the entire book. Mádhava Basak did typing and layout of the book along with many other valuable tasks.

summary: Just as zero cannot have any radius, infinity also has no radius.

points.body: Just as zero cannot have any radius, infinity also has no radius. You can form a circle with a radius greater than zero but less than infinity; only in this circumstance can it exist. Unless the radius of anything is greater than zero and less than infinity, its existence becomes meaningless. Then there may be existence in theory but not in actuality.

points.body: Now, family sentiment is also a kind of socio-sentiment, but its radius is very small. Greater than this is the radius of caste sentiment, and still greater is that of community sentiment, national sentiment, international sentiment, and so on. Now, the narrowest of all the socio-sentiments is technically called “socio-sentiment minimitis,” and the greatest is called “socio-sentiment maximitis” or “socio-sentiment excellencio.” What is the difference between these two terms?

points.title: It is said that once the scholars in Navadvipa researched for a long time whether the s…

summary: It is said that once the scholars in Navadvipa researched for a long time whether the sound is produced before or after the palmyra fruit hits the ground.
After three days and nights, it was found at daybreak that almost all the scholars were dead.
The palmyra fruits fell on their heads, and that is how they died!
points.body: It is said that once the scholars in Navadvipa researched for a long time whether the sound is produced before or after the palmyra fruit hits the ground. The story goes that the scholars carried on this debate for three days and nights, and five maunds [approximately 411 pounds] of snuff were consumed in the process! After three days and nights, it was found at daybreak that almost all the scholars were dead. And what was the cause? The palmyra fruits fell on their heads, and that is how they died!

points.title: Now, this socio-sentiment, in its stage of excellencio or in theory maximitis, is calle…

summary: Now, this socio-sentiment, in its stage of excellencio or in theory maximitis, is called “humanism.

When I use the term “internationalism,” I am admitting the existence of separate nations, and along with this I must naturally also think, within the nations, of the peopleʼs five fundamental requirements of life (food, clothes, education, shelter, and medical care).
So internationalism is not the solution either.
points.body: Now, this socio-sentiment, in its stage of excellencio or in theory maximitis, is called “humanism.” Suppose I was working for a particular nation, but now I am working for all nations. When I admit the existence of nations and say that I am working for all nations, then it is neither humanism nor universalism – it is merely internationalism. When I use the term “internationalism,” I am admitting the existence of separate nations, and along with this I must naturally also think, within the nations, of the peopleʼs five fundamental requirements of life (food, clothes, education, shelter, and medical care). But when I discover that one nation is trying to thrive on the life-blood of another, I oppose it, and this opposition ultimately leads to world war. So internationalism is not the solution either.

points.title: Now, if we enlarge the circumference beyond the scope of nationalism or internationalis…
points.prompt: Recall and explain from memory: Now, if we enlarge the circumference beyond the scope of nationalism or internationalis…
summary: Now, if we enlarge the circumference beyond the scope of nationalism or internationalism and embrace all people within one fold, this is called “humanism,” or, still better, “ordinary” or “general” humanism.
points.body: Now, if we enlarge the circumference beyond the scope of nationalism or internationalism and embrace all people within one fold, this is called “humanism,” or, still better, “ordinary” or “general” humanism.

points.title: What is this humanism?
points.prompt: Recall and explain from memory: What is this humanism?
summary: What is this humanism?
The first is that even within humanism there is still intra-humanistic clash; and secondly, in the living world, humans are not the only living beings – there are many other creatures as well.
But this destruction will upset the balance among the plant, animal, and human worlds and result in the catastrophic ruin of human life as well.
points.body: What is this humanism? It is socio-sentiment maximitis. Is this the panacea for all problems? Does it provide answers to all questions? No, it does not, for two reasons. The first is that even within humanism there is still intra-humanistic clash; and secondly, in the living world, humans are not the only living beings – there are many other creatures as well. If people completely ignore them, indeed this may not create any great conflict in the external world, because non-human creatures are psychologically undeveloped. (Even if they are physically developed, mentally they are undeveloped.) Thus it is easy for human beings to destroy the animal and plant kingdoms. But this destruction will upset the balance among the plant, animal, and human worlds and result in the catastrophic ruin of human life as well.

points.title: Now, what does “intra-humanistic clash” mean?
points.prompt: Recall and explain from memory: Now, what does “intra-humanistic clash” mean?
summary: Now, what does “intra-humanistic clash” mean?

This is humanitarian, no doubt, but at the back of my mind I am thinking, “Let me utilize these people as the suppliers of our raw materials and the purchasers of our finished products, because these people are now obligated to us.
So the humanistic approach is not perfect; it is adulterated.
points.body: Now, what does “intra-humanistic clash” mean? Suppose I find that a particular social group is suffering from starvation, and I provide food for them. This is humanitarian, no doubt, but at the back of my mind I am thinking, “Let me utilize these people as the suppliers of our raw materials and the purchasers of our finished products, because these people are now obligated to us.” This sort of mentality will one day destroy peace in society. So the humanistic approach is not perfect; it is adulterated.

points.title: Suppose we discover that a particular group is educationally backward
points.prompt: Recall and explain from memory: Suppose we discover that a particular group is educationally backward
summary: Suppose we discover that a particular group is educationally backward.
But through this so-called “literacy drive,” we inject ideas in their minds that paralyze them mentally, and then we ultimately govern these mentally-paralyzed people as colonized people.
This is the mentality at work.
points.body: Suppose we discover that a particular group is educationally backward. We feel pity for its people because they are also our fellow human beings. So we think, “Let us introduce them to the printed word at least!” and actually we do something towards that end. But through this so-called “literacy drive,” we inject ideas in their minds that paralyze them mentally, and then we ultimately govern these mentally-paralyzed people as colonized people. In this way the peace of the world will be destroyed. This is all “intra-human conflict.” The intention is to develop them socially in the way we like and thus destroy their originality. This is the mentality at work.

points.title: What is the reason for this type of mentality?
points.prompt: Recall and explain from memory: What is the reason for this type of mentality?
summary: What is the reason for this type of mentality?
This adulterated [humanism] is not genuine [humanism], nor is it true humanistic spirit; it is ordinary human sentiment or pseudo-humanistic strategy in another form.
It has some affinity with pseudo-reformist strategy.
points.body: What is the reason for this type of mentality? “I pity them” – this vanity, this superiority complex – will eventually create satellite social groups. This adulterated [humanism] is not genuine [humanism], nor is it true humanistic spirit; it is ordinary human sentiment or pseudo-humanistic strategy in another form. It has some affinity with pseudo-reformist strategy.

points.title: How does pseudo-reformist strategy work?
points.prompt: Recall and explain from memory: How does pseudo-reformist strategy work?
summary: How does pseudo-reformist strategy work?
We do not want any great changes; we will just go ahead step by step.
” This is pseudo-reformist strategy.
points.body: How does pseudo-reformist strategy work? What is its nature? It arises within socio-sentiment: “Yes, what my opponents [revolutionaries] say is correct; but if this really materializes, it will greatly inconvenience me and disturb my individual sentiment. So what we must do is to try to adjust with the existing situation. We do not want any great changes; we will just go ahead step by step. Externally we may speak of reform, but in our heart of hearts, we have decided not to allow any change to take place.” This is pseudo-reformist strategy. ( 1 )

points.title: And what is “pseudo-humanistic strategy”?
points.prompt: Recall and explain from memory: And what is “pseudo-humanistic strategy”?
summary: And what is “pseudo-humanistic strategy”?
” In the absence of a firm foundation, this sort of ordinary human sentiment remains unstable.
This situation is prevalent all over the world today; you must make sincere efforts to see that it no longer continues.
points.body: And what is “pseudo-humanistic strategy”? “Outwardly we preach the gospels of humanistic idealism, but in actuality we stab others in the back.” In the absence of a firm foundation, this sort of ordinary human sentiment remains unstable. This situation is prevalent all over the world today; you must make sincere efforts to see that it no longer continues.

summary: Intra-humanistic clash is a continuing phenomenon, and as a result there are constant conflicts between individual and individual, between group and group.
It is because this so-called ordinary humanism or general humanism is nothing more than an enlarged form of nationalism: only its radius is large, or maximitis, as I said in the beginning.
That is the only difference.
points.body: Intra-humanistic clash is a continuing phenomenon, and as a result there are constant conflicts between individual and individual, between group and group. What is the reason? It is because this so-called ordinary humanism or general humanism is nothing more than an enlarged form of nationalism: only its radius is large, or maximitis, as I said in the beginning. That is the only difference.

summary: So you see, socio-sentiment minimitis and socio-sentiment maximitis, although they differ in radius, are both mental diseases which demand our equal attention.
The socio-sentiment maximitis or excellencio that is included in socio-sentiment results in clash not only among human beings, but also in mutual clash among humans, animals and plants.
Thus today or tomorrow they will become exploited, either directly or indirectly, and the exploitation will be more intense in the economic sphere than in other spheres.
points.body: So you see, socio-sentiment minimitis and socio-sentiment maximitis, although they differ in radius, are both mental diseases which demand our equal attention. Suppose in someoneʼs body there is a certain disease in one place affecting a limited area, and the same disease in another place affecting a broader area. The disease is the same; the difference lies only in the magnitude of the affected area. The socio-sentiment maximitis or excellencio that is included in socio-sentiment results in clash not only among human beings, but also in mutual clash among humans, animals and plants. If, instead of firmly establishing oneʼs mind in humanism, one is guided by pseudo-humanistic strategy, one is bound by some means or the other to bring the social group to which one has given aid within the scope of oneʼs own socio-sentiment. Thus today or tomorrow they will become exploited, either directly or indirectly, and the exploitation will be more intense in the economic sphere than in other spheres.

points.body: This has one very interesting aspect, which most people overlook. Depending upon the degree of economic affluence, some countries are called “developed,” some “developing,” and some “undeveloped.” Now the interesting thing is that none of these so-called developed countries can stand on their own legs. They are simply compelling the developing and undeveloped countries to buy their industrial goods by creating circumstantial pressure on them. None of these countries becomes developed by developing its own resources.

points.body: So as long as there are bondages of nationhood – maximitis bondages (not to mention minimitis) – the tendency to exploit individuals or the collectivity will continue to exist. This is bound to have its repercussions on political life as well as religious life. I said yesterday that religion is being used to create satellites; the propagators of religion are performing this unjust action consciously or unconsciously. But behind all this lies the wealth of those who seek to create satellite groups as suppliers of their raw materials or customers for their finished products. Thus there is pervasive corruption in religious life. None of these religions is Bhágavata dharma, the all-embracing human dharma.

points.title: There is degeneration in cultural life also

summary: There is degeneration in cultural life also.

The rulers and exploiters, who are motivated by socio-sentiment maximitis (otherwise known as general humanism), want to exploit people in all spheres of life – social, economic, political, cultural, and religious.
Hence humanism cannot be considered the panacea; it is not a perfect remedy.
points.body: There is degeneration in cultural life also. Once oneʼs cultural life is controlled, one becomes a slave. The rulers and exploiters, who are motivated by socio-sentiment maximitis (otherwise known as general humanism), want to exploit people in all spheres of life – social, economic, political, cultural, and religious. Hence humanism cannot be considered the panacea; it is not a perfect remedy.

points.title: Often certain social groups – be they international groups or the largest social groups…
points.prompt: Recall and explain from memory: Often certain social groups – be they international groups or the largest social groups…
summary: Often certain social groups – be they international groups or the largest social groups – seek to preserve their existences by destroying non-human creatures – animals and plants.

The kind of persecution which is being perpetrated against animals today may be perpetrated by one social group against another tomorrow, because the very tendency to torture others is predominant in the blood of exploiters.
That is why I said that this is all pseudo-humanistic strategy, not even humanistic strategy.
points.body: Often certain social groups – be they international groups or the largest social groups – seek to preserve their existences by destroying non-human creatures – animals and plants. But all animals and plants also have the urge for self-preservation; no creature dies willingly. This destructive tendency is operating not only in the inter-creature world (the torture of animals and plants), but also in the intra-creature world (within the human world itself). The kind of persecution which is being perpetrated against animals today may be perpetrated by one social group against another tomorrow, because the very tendency to torture others is predominant in the blood of exploiters. They are not free from this disease – they merely mouth high ideals. That is why I said that this is all pseudo-humanistic strategy, not even humanistic strategy.

points.title: What do people do to meet their growing needs for agricultural lands, for industries, e…
points.prompt: Recall and explain from memory: What do people do to meet their growing needs for agricultural lands, for industries, e…
summary: What do people do to meet their growing needs for agricultural lands, for industries, etc.?
We have destroyed their natural habitat, the forests, but we never bothered to consider any alternative arrangements for their shelter.
Rather it will be a great loss for human society, because each and every living entity, whether plant or animal, has two types of value: one, its utility value, and the other, its existential value.
points.body: What do people do to meet their growing needs for agricultural lands, for industries, etc.? They bring about large-scale deforestation; but no one bothers to think about the creatures that live in those forests. Thus the tigers and elephants haunt the villages, kill the people and demolish their houses. Why? Out of their instinct for self-preservation. We have destroyed their natural habitat, the forests, but we never bothered to consider any alternative arrangements for their shelter. We have recklessly destroyed large areas of forests without caring to think that thereby we are destroying the balance among the human, plant, and animal worlds. And we never realized – and still do not – that this wanton destruction of the animal and plant worlds will be of no benefit to human beings. Rather it will be a great loss for human society, because each and every living entity, whether plant or animal, has two types of value: one, its utility value, and the other, its existential value.

points.title: Human beings usually preserve those creatures which have an immediate utility value for…
points.prompt: Recall and explain from memory: Human beings usually preserve those creatures which have an immediate utility value for…

points.body: Human beings have limped forward in their journey of history for the last million years bearing the burden of this defective social system; all have not been given equal justice. That is why I say that neither has justice been done to humanity (the abstract noun for “human beings”) nor has justice been done to humanism ( 1 ) (the abstract noun for “the work performed by human beings for human beings”). Now it is high time to carry out a reappraisal of the downtrodden humanity, of downtrodden humanism. Oftentimes, some people have lagged behind, exhausted, and have collapsed on the ground, their hands and knees bruised and their clothes stained with mud. Such people have been thrown aside with hatred and have become the outcasts of society; they have been forced to remain isolated from the mainstream of social life. points.body: When some people started advancing, they thought more about themselves and less about others; nor did they think about the animals and plants. But if we analyze with a cool brain, it becomes quite clear that just as my life is important to me, othersʼ lives are equally important to them; and if we do not give proper value to the lives of all creatures, then the development of the entire humanity becomes impossible. If people think more about themselves as individuals or about their small families, castes, clans or tribes, and do not think at all about the collectivity, this is decidedly detrimental. Similarly, if people neglect the entire living world – the plant world, the animal world – is this not harmful? That is why I say that there is a great need to explain humanity and humanism in a new light, and this newly-explained humanism will be a precious treasure for the world.

points.body: But there is something more beyond this, which I have described as “spirituality as a mission.” So first there is “spirituality as a cult”, secondly, “spirituality in essence”, and thirdly, “spirituality as a mission.” All existential phenomena are emanating from the Existential Nucleus. points.body: Led by the urge of self-interest, human beings are neglecting ecology at every step. We have to remember that the sky, the air, birds, hills, wild animals, reptiles, insects and flies, fish, marine creatures and aquatic plants are all bound by an inalienable bond. Human beings are only a part of that vast common society. No one can survive to the exclusion of others. Not even humanity. By foolishly destroying the forest, wild animals, annihilating the fish and the birds, no possible human interest could be served. Whoever is born on this earth dies. One only survives on this earth for the period allotted to one by nature. As a result of human folly, many creatures and geological phenomena will not survive for that period. Long before their natural end, they will be swallowed up by eternity. Humanity through its own madness has annihilated numerous creatures and objects and has thus prepared its own funeral pyre. This act of sheer short-sightedness is intolerable. People will have to be alert henceforth. They must shape their thoughts, works and plans in accordance with the science of ecology. There is no other way left open to them.

points.body: Due to humanityʼs heedlessness, not only hilsa and mango fish but also many other creatures are about to disappear from this earth. Human beings will have to undergo penance for this. I have said a little earlier that there is an inalienable bond among all beings created by nature, and each of those beings maintains natureʼs laws in one manner or another. In my childhood days I used to hear that hilsa fish appear in greater numbers every third year, in still greater numbers in the tenth year, and in even greater numbers at an interval of every thirty years. Since presently human beings are violating the laws of ecology, the entire natural order is not functioning properly. The law governing the hilsa fish is also applicable to the mango [fruit]. To enhance the production of mangoes, people have adopted many unnatural methods. Hence that particular law of nature has also ceased to function. In our childhood we were told, “With mango comes the paddy, with tamarind the flood.” ( 1 ) Nowadays such patterns no longer occur. ( 2 )
